# Fast PR checks: each changed component, and each that reads a changed file, runs its own Linux unit tests. Native,
# macOS, coverage-gate, browser and end-to-end checks are outside PR CI; see
# docs/validation-and-release.md#what-pr-ci-does-not-run. Merge candidates rerun
# only the plan and process checks; the PR run covered the code. After Update branch,
# a suite whose inputs main's new commits left untouched reuses the earlier head's result.
# Contributor code runs with a read-only token and no release credentials.
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, 'ci-rollout/**']
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, converted_to_draft]
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      scope:
        description: 'Affected component; full for core suites, all for every component'
        type: choice
        options: [full, cli, tui, backend, desktop, process, all, companions, website, os, provider, firmware, pro, mobile, daemons, pty]
        default: full
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      scope:
        description: 'full, cli, tui, backend, desktop (VM tests), or process (repository tooling only)'
        type: string
        default: full

permissions:
  contents: read

# The managed runtime shipped by the CLI; keep release.yml's pin in sync.
env:
  CLI_NODE_VERSION: 24.22.2
  CI_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

# Supersede individual PR jobs, not the whole workflow: an always-running final
# gate on an obsolete revision must not hold the next revision's scheduling lock.
# Keep PR event actions separate: synchronize and ready_for_review can arrive
# together for the same head, and must each complete their own required checks.
# New synchronize events still supersede older synchronize jobs.
# Every matrix row has its own group. Explicit runs and merge candidates use run
# IDs, so their requested validation is preserved. Summaries and the final gate
# have no lock: an older aggregate can finish after newer work without cancelling it.

jobs:
  plan:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-plan
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    # Read-only lookups of an earlier head's ci/required run, whose results an update merge may
    # reuse (docs/validation-and-release.md#reuse-after-update-branch). No write scope.
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read
      checks: read
    outputs:
      plan: ${{ steps.select.outputs.plan }}
      ready: ${{ steps.select.outputs.ready }}
      cli: ${{ steps.select.outputs.cli }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.select.outputs.desktop }}
      tui: ${{ steps.select.outputs.tui }}
      backend: ${{ steps.select.outputs.backend }}
      companions: ${{ steps.select.outputs.companions }}
      website: ${{ steps.select.outputs.website }}
      experience: ${{ steps.select.outputs.experience }}
      authoring: ${{ steps.select.outputs.authoring }}
      home-assistant: ${{ steps.select.outputs.home-assistant }}
      desktop-logging: ${{ steps.select.outputs.desktop-logging }}
      os: ${{ steps.select.outputs.os }}
      provider: ${{ steps.select.outputs.provider }}
      firmware: ${{ steps.select.outputs.firmware }}
      pro: ${{ steps.select.outputs.pro }}
      mobile: ${{ steps.select.outputs.mobile }}
      daemons: ${{ steps.select.outputs.daemons }}
      pty: ${{ steps.select.outputs.pty }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Run 37659523265 spent the entire 5-minute planning budget fetching blobs for every
          # historical asset. Keep all commits/trees for merge-base and the complete diff, but
          # materialize only the workflow and planner sources this job reads.
          sparse-checkout: |
            .github
            scripts
      - name: Validate the integration workflows
        # actionlint needs Go 1.25 or newer, and `go run` otherwise switches to the newest toolchain it is told of.
        # On 2026-10-08 that was go1.26.9, listed before it was published (proxy and checksum database: 404), and
        # every PR's planning failed. A toolchain that exists keeps planning off Go's release timing.
        env:
          GOTOOLCHAIN: go1.26.8
        run: >-
          go run github.com/rhysd/actionlint/cmd/actionlint@v1.7.12
          .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/cli-e2e.yml .github/workflows/ci-health.yml
          .github/workflows/website-checks.yml .github/workflows/experience-checks.yml
          .github/workflows/authoring-browser-checks.yml .github/workflows/home-assistant-checks.yml
          .github/workflows/desktop-logging-checks.yml .github/workflows/windows.yml .github/workflows/backend-cache.yml
      - id: select
        env:
          CI_SCOPE: ${{ inputs.scope || 'full' }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: python3 scripts/ci-plan.py --scope "$CI_SCOPE" --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-plan.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ci-plan
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ci-plan.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 14

  process-checks:
    outputs:
      local_receipts: ${{ steps.local.outputs.local_receipts }}
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-process-checks
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
          sparse-checkout: |
            /.github/
            /scripts/
            /desktop/scripts/
            /cli/scripts/release-cli.sh
            /backend/scripts/release-be.sh
            /.gitattributes
            /.gitignore
            /.gitmodules
            /Makefile
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
      - name: Verify declared source checkout
        run: python3 scripts/ci-source-inputs.py process
      - name: Require local validation receipts for mapped paths
        id: local
        env:
          CI_PLAN: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.plan }}
        run: python3 scripts/local-checks.py
      - name: Validation deadlines, cleanup, receipts and release version guards
        # The fixtures commit in temporary repositories. Each commit starts a detached
        # `git maintenance run --auto`, which can still be writing objects/pack when the
        # test removes the folder (test_queue_validated_pr: "Directory not empty: 'pack'").
        env:
          GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: "1"
          GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: maintenance.auto
          GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: "false"
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
      - name: Style allowlists only shrink (desktop/design/desktop-design-system.md)
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          git fetch --quiet --depth=1 --no-tags origin "$BASE_SHA"
          python3 scripts/check-ui-style.py --against "$BASE_SHA"
      - name: Record source inputs for CI evidence reuse
        run: python3 scripts/ci-source-inputs.py process --record "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-source-inputs.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ci-source-inputs
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ci-source-inputs.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 7

  desktop-tests:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-desktop-tests-${{ strategy.job-index }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.desktop == 'true'
    name: desktop-tests (${{ matrix.os }}, ${{ matrix.shard }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-22.04]
        # Six shards split by measured file times (scripts/desktop-test-durations.json): each needs about 6 of its 10
        # minutes on a slow runner, so the suite can grow a fifth before one runs short (task #3458;
        # scripts/tests/test_desktop_tests.py checks the split keeps a quarter of the limit free).
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
          sparse-checkout: |
            /.github/
            /scripts/
            /desktop/
            /cli/
            /tests/
            /daemons/
            /store/
            /docs/images/
            /mobile/pubspec.lock
            /backend/src/lib/communityContract.ts
            /backend/src/lib/hubMetricsContract.ts
            /mobile/lib/p2p/terminal_p2p_plugin.dart
            /mobile/lib/p2p/terminal_p2p_link.dart
            /mobile/lib/p2p/terminal_p2p_policy.dart
            /mobile/lib/ws/terminal_transport_plugin.dart
            /mobile/lib/ws/relay_codec.dart
            /mobile/lib/e2ee/relay_session_crypto.dart
            /.gitattributes
            /.gitignore
            /.gitmodules
            /Makefile
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
      - name: Verify declared source checkout
        run: python3 scripts/ci-source-inputs.py desktop
      - name: No new hard-coded styles in Swarm UI (desktop/design/desktop-design-system.md)
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        run: python3 scripts/check-ui-style.py --only desktop/lib/super_tabs
      - id: toolchain
        run: |
          version="$(sed -n "s/^  FLUTTER_VERSION: '\([^']*\)'.*/\1/p" .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml)"
          test -n "$version"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: ./.github/actions/desktop-flutter
        with:
          version: ${{ steps.toolchain.outputs.version }}
      - name: Every Desktop shard keeps a quarter of its time limit (task #3458)
        if: matrix.shard == 1
        # Named in full: a renamed test then fails here instead of matching nothing and passing (review of #3241).
        working-directory: scripts/tests
        run: python3 -m unittest -v test_desktop_tests.DurationSplitTests.test_ci_split_leaves_every_shard_a_quarter_of_its_time_limit
      - name: Run bounded Desktop VM shard
        env:
          DESKTOP_SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: python3 scripts/test-desktop.py --shard "$DESKTOP_SHARD/6" --workers 4 --timeout 600
      - name: Preserve complete test logs and receipts
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: desktop-shard-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: .harness/validation/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 7

  # The optional product has its own dependencies, bundle and suites. CLI-only CI
  # deliberately checks core without installing or building this package.
  companion-subsystems:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-companion-subsystems
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.companions == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: companions
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.CLI_NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: |
            cli/package-lock.json
            companions/package-lock.json
      # Shared source helpers retain their own dependency resolution during typecheck.
      - run: npm ci --prefix ../cli --ignore-scripts
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm run build
      - run: npm run test:bundle
      # CPU-budget fuzz runs alone, separate from subprocess-heavy fixture tests.
      - run: npx vitest run src/shared/guard.fuzz.spec.ts --maxWorkers=1
      - run: npm test -- --exclude src/shared/guard.fuzz.spec.ts --maxWorkers=3

  cli-typecheck:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-cli-typecheck
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.cli == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: cli
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.CLI_NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: cli/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
      - run: npx tsc --noEmit

  cli-tests:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-cli-tests-${{ strategy.job-index }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.cli == 'true'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: cli
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.CLI_NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: cli/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
      # Vitest partitions files using the same config in every shard. Keep the
      # existing worker cap/isolation: subprocess fixtures still need spare CPUs.
      # Opt-in real-engine suites retain their existing explicit skips.
      - name: Discover the complete default-suite inventory
        run: npx vitest list --config vitest.ci.config.ts --filesOnly --json="$RUNNER_TEMP/inventory-${{ matrix.shard }}.json"
      - name: Run default-suite shard
        run: npx vitest run --config vitest.ci.config.ts --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/4 --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile.json="$RUNNER_TEMP/result-${{ matrix.shard }}.json"
      - name: Preserve inventory and test results
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: cli-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/inventory-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
            ${{ runner.temp }}/result-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 7

  # Unit tests only. Native fixtures and connected-shell checks run in the release workflow.
  tui-test:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-tui-test
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.tui == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: tui
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          workspaces: tui
          shared-key: tui-pr
          cache-bin: false
      - run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux zsh
      - name: Unit tests
        env:
          TERM: xterm-256color
          COLORTERM: truecolor
        run: env -u NO_COLOR cargo test --locked

  backend-desk:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-backend-desk
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.backend == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # A real Redis for the Redis-backed unit tests, which skip without one: a cache stamp that could repeat passed CI unseen
    # for that reason (review of #2456).
    services:
      redis:
        image: redis:7.2.5
        ports: ['6379:6379']
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "redis-cli ping" --health-interval 2s --health-timeout 2s --health-retries 15
    env:
      REDIS_TEST_URL: redis://127.0.0.1:6379/15
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22.23.2
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: backend/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
      # The whole backend unit suite (src/**/*.test.ts, including the shared desk layout test): it once ran only the desk
      # test, and main broke 48 team-session tests unseen (#1926).
      - name: Backend unit suite
        run: npm test -- --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile.json=vitest-results.json
      - name: The Redis-backed tests ran
        run: node scripts/redis-tests-ran.mjs vitest-results.json

  # The backend integration suite (npm run test:integration, backend/integration), which every backend PR once ran locally
  # for 60-90 minutes behind a per-Mac lock (task #2459). Four shards balanced by integration/ci-durations.json; each
  # integration file starts its own MongoDB replica set (mongodb-memory-server-core), so shards share no database, and the
  # suite opens no Redis (src/lib/noRedis.test-support.ts).
  backend-integration:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-backend-integration-${{ strategy.job-index }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.backend == 'true'
    name: backend-integration (${{ matrix.shard }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: backend
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: 22.23.2
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: backend/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
      # The tests download mongod 7.0.24 into $TMPDIR/harness-super-tab-mongodb-binaries (integration/plans.test-support.ts).
      # Restore only: backend-cache.yml saves it from main, where every PR can read it; a PR's own save would be its alone.
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: /tmp/harness-super-tab-mongodb-binaries
          key: super-tab-mongod-7.0.24-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}
      - name: Backend integration shard
        env:
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
        run: >-
          npx vitest run --config vitest.integration.ci.config.ts --shard="$SHARD/4"
          --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile.json="$RUNNER_TEMP/integration-$SHARD.json"
      - name: Preserve per-file results (durations refresh integration/ci-durations.json)
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: backend-integration-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/integration-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 7

  website-checks:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-website-checks
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.website == 'true'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/website-checks.yml

  os-checks:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-os-checks
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.os == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - name: OS source, installer and update contracts
        run: make -C os check

  provider-checks:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-provider-checks-${{ strategy.job-index }}
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.provider == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package: [reference-provider, example-provider]
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: provider/${{ matrix.package }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.CLI_NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: provider/${{ matrix.package }}/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
      - run: npm run typecheck
      - run: npm test

  firmware-checks:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-firmware-checks
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.firmware == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      IDF_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/.ci-esp-idf
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          repository: espressif/esp-idf
          ref: 8c750b088c7cd857d079c0eeb495da199b359461 # v5.5
          path: .ci-esp-idf
          sparse-checkout: |
            components/json
            components/esp_rom
      - name: Prepare the SDK's pinned cJSON source
        run: git -C "$IDF_PATH" submodule update --init --depth 1 components/json/cJSON
      - name: Use Clang for the host fixture warning and sanitizer contracts
        run: |
          clang-18 --version
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/firmware-bin"
          ln -s "$(command -v clang-18)" "$RUNNER_TEMP/firmware-bin/cc"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/firmware-bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Run every host firmware contract (physical acceptance remains separate)
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          from pathlib import Path
          import subprocess
          files = sorted(Path('devices/harness-device/firmware/test').glob('test_*.py'))
          assert files, 'firmware test inventory is empty'
          failures = []
          for path in files:
              print(path, flush=True)
              try:
                  subprocess.run(['python3', str(path)], check=True, timeout=120)
              except (subprocess.CalledProcessError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
                  failures.append(str(path))
          if failures:
              raise SystemExit('Failed firmware contracts: ' + ', '.join(failures))
          print(f'Passed all {len(files)} firmware host contracts')
          PY
      - name: Run the Harness Pro host contracts
        env:
          PRO_FONT: ${{ github.workspace }}/devices/harness-pro/firmware/fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --user --break-system-packages pillow==12.1.1
          bash devices/harness-pro/firmware/test/run.sh
          python3 devices/harness-pro/firmware/test/test_tree_isolation.py
          python3 devices/harness-pro/firmware/test/test_fonts.py

  pro-firmware-build:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-pro-firmware-build
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.pro == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # The ESP-IDF release the Harness Pro is built and flashed with (README: ~/esp/esp-idf-5.5.4).
    container: espressif/idf:v5.5.4
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: devices/harness-pro/firmware
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - name: Build the ESP32-P4 firmware
        run: |
          . "$IDF_PATH/export.sh" > /dev/null
          # The font generator needs Pillow; the image's system python3 has no pip, so it goes in the IDF environment.
          python -m pip install pillow==12.1.1
          idf.py -B build -DPROJECT_VER=0.0.99-ci build
      - name: Fit the app in its OTA partition
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import csv
          from pathlib import Path
          rows = csv.reader(line for line in Path('partitions.csv').read_text().splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.startswith('#'))
          limit = int(next(row[4] for row in rows if row[0].strip() == 'ota_0').strip(), 0)
          size = Path('build/harness_pro.bin').stat().st_size
          print(f'harness_pro.bin: {size} bytes of {limit} in ota_0 ({100 * size / limit:.1f}%)')
          if size > limit:
              raise SystemExit('harness_pro.bin does not fit the ota_0 partition')
          PY

  pro-golden:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-pro-golden
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.pro == 'true'
    # macOS arm64, where the baseline is recorded: the code-drawn shapes (arcs, juggling balls) use float maths whose
    # last bits differ between Apple arm64 and Linux x86-64, so the hashes only match on the same platform.
    runs-on: macos-15
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - name: Compare every Pets screen with the golden hashes
        working-directory: devices/harness-pro/firmware
        env:
          PRO_FONT: fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf
        run: |
          python3 -m pip install --user --break-system-packages pillow==12.1.1
          bash test/golden.sh --check

  mobile-checks:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-mobile-checks
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.mobile == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - name: No new hard-coded styles in Swarm UI (desktop/design/desktop-design-system.md)
        run: python3 scripts/check-ui-style.py --only mobile/lib/swarm
      - id: toolchain
        run: |
          version="$(sed -n "s/^  FLUTTER_VERSION: '\([^']*\)'.*/\1/p" .github/workflows/release-desktop.yml)"
          test -n "$version"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: subosito/flutter-action@v2
        with:
          flutter-version: ${{ steps.toolchain.outputs.version }}
          channel: stable
          cache: true
      - run: flutter pub get
        working-directory: mobile
      - run: flutter test --no-pub --concurrency 4 --reporter expanded
        working-directory: mobile

  daemons-checks:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-daemons-checks
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.daemons == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.CLI_NODE_VERSION }}
      - run: node --test daemons/tools/card.test.mjs daemons/tools/generate.test.mjs

  # The Harness PTY host (pty/, on term/): its Rust tests, then the CLI's terminal contract for the
  # ptyhost backend against the host just built (tmux's half needs tmux and runs locally). Selected by
  # pty/, term/, the vendored terminal and the CLI's code (scripts/ci-plan.py ALSO, PR_READS), and by installer/, whose
  # model and steps (harness-install.exe) are plain Rust that tests here.
  pty-checks:
    concurrency:
      group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.action || 'run' }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}-pty-checks
      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.ready == 'true' && needs.plan.outputs.pty == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6 # v2.9.2
        with:
          workspaces: |
            pty
            term
            installer
          shared-key: pty-pr
          cache-bin: false
      - name: Terminal and host unit tests
        run: |
          cargo test --locked --manifest-path term/Cargo.toml
          cargo build --locked --manifest-path pty/Cargo.toml
          cargo test --locked --manifest-path pty/Cargo.toml
          cargo test --locked --manifest-path installer/Cargo.toml
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.CLI_NODE_VERSION }}
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: cli/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
        working-directory: cli
      - name: ptyhost terminal contract
        working-directory: cli
        env:
          RUN_TERMINAL_CONTRACT: '1'
          HARNESS_PTY_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/pty/target/debug/harness-pty
        run: npx vitest run src/lib/ptyHostBackend.contract.spec.ts --maxWorkers=1

  required:
    name: ci/required
    needs: [plan, process-checks, desktop-tests, companion-subsystems, cli-typecheck, cli-tests, tui-test,
            backend-desk, backend-integration, website-checks, os-checks, provider-checks, firmware-checks, pro-firmware-build, pro-golden,
            mobile-checks, daemons-checks, pty-checks]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.CI_SOURCE_SHA }}
          sparse-checkout: scripts/
      - name: Require every selected job and complete coverage summaries
        env:
          CI_PLAN: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.plan }}
          CI_NEEDS: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
        run: python3 scripts/ci-plan.py --verify --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/ci-required.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ci-required
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/ci-required.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          overwrite: true
          retention-days: 14

sampled_files.README.md:
Harness like a boss.

The ultimate harness for coding agents and beyond.
Claude Code at work. Codex at home. Hermes in the cloud. One command center.
Start with code. Then follow your curiosity and build across disciplines: CAD, circuits, robots, games and music.

Download · How it works · Beyond code · Harnesses · Device

### Every agent, side by side Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Devin, Amp, Copilot and seven more.

### Every machine, side by side Your laptop, home server and GPU box in one window. Link each one with a password. No SSH keys. No Tailscale. No port forwarding.

### Keyboard first ⌘P finds any harness on any machine. ⇧⌘I jumps to the harness waiting on you. ⌘D splits. Every key remaps.

### End-to-end encrypted Code, keys and keystrokes are sealed on your machine. The relay forwards bytes it can't read.

### Fast and light A native app, not Electron. Close it and your agents keep working. Idle measurements on an M2 Max: - **⌘N, ⌘O, ⌘T UI:** 11–13 ms median, 15–18 ms p95. - **Local terminal echo:** 1.1 ms median, 7.2 ms p95, excluding UI rendering. - **Desktop resources:** ~0.1% of one CPU core and 304 MiB, including terminal rendering and scrollback; agent CLIs and the daemon are excluded. Desktop results use a Release fixture with 16 terminals and 1,000 scrollback lines each. See the [workflow and resource benchmarks](docs/performance/2026-09-23-core-experiences.md) and [remote P2P, TURN and relay results](docs/performance/2026-09-23-transport-routes.md) for workloads, slow tails, connection failures and raw data. ### Built the way developers work - **Real terminals.** Every agent runs in its own tmux pane. Scrollback, colors and keys just work. - **Your CLIs, as they are.** Harness never wraps an agent. It reads transcripts and uses the vendor's own hooks. - **A worktree per harness.** Start an agent on its own branch. Your working copy stays clean. - **Remap every key.** One JSONC file, reloaded on save. Chords up to four strokes. - **Local models.** Run open-weight models on your own machines with Grid, Ollama, MLX-LM and vLLM. - **Bytes, not pixels.** Remote terminals stream text peer to peer. No remote desktop. - **Open source, all of it.** App, CLI, daemon, relay and device, in this repo. ## How it works In the workspace, a **harness** is one running session of an agent such as Codex or Claude Code, with its own conversation and working context. A **tab** groups harnesses. Use **New Harness** to start one and **New Tab** to group work. Harnesses in the same tab can message each other with `harness send`: **Agent Messages**, an experiment of your account, off by default and turned on in Settings ▸ Experimental. The Store offers **harnesses** with instructions, tools, and optional viewers for specific crafts. Install a harness, then start it in your workspace. See the [Naming System](docs/naming-system.md) for the complete naming rules. One daemon per machine runs your agents in tmux. It dials out, so no machine opens a port. ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph laptop["Your laptop"] app["Harness app"] -- loopback --> d1["daemon"] d1 --> a1["tmux · Claude Code · Codex"] end subgraph box["Your GPU box"] d2["daemon"] --> a2["tmux · OpenCode · Hermes"] end device["Harness device"] -- USB --> d1 d1 <-. "direct WebRTC" .-> d2 d1 <-- "ciphertext" --> relay["Harness relay · no keys"] relay <-- "ciphertext" --> d2 ``` Every path is sealed end to end: ChaCha20-Poly1305, X25519 session keys, pinned Ed25519 identities. Harness picks the best path on its own. **Direct.** A WebRTC channel between your machines. No server in the path.

**Through Cloudflare.** When a firewall blocks the direct path, the same encrypted channel runs over Cloudflare's TURN network. Harness keeps trying for a direct path.

**Through our relay.** A fallback while WebRTC negotiates. The relay holds no keys and forwards ciphertext.

The [architecture guide](docs/architecture.md) has the details. ## Get started **[Download the app](https://harness.autonomous.ai/desktop?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme)** for macOS or Linux. Add a machine. Run this on it, then **Machines → Link Machine** in the app: ```bash curl -fsSL https://harness.autonomous.ai/cli/install.sh | bash harness login harness remote-password set harness start ``` **In a terminal:** the same line installs `hn` — tmux's keys and your `~/.tmux.conf`, with every harness on every machine ([hn](tui/README.md)). The first time, `hn` signs in and connects the computer: ```bash curl -fsSL https://harness.autonomous.ai/cli/install.sh | bash hn ``` **For agents:** Claude Code and Codex can start, wait for and read other harnesses with the `harness` skill ([harness.autonomous.ai/agents](https://harness.autonomous.ai/agents), which has the Codex lines too): ```bash claude plugin marketplace add autonomous-ai/openharness --sparse .claude-plugin plugins claude plugin install harness@openharness ```
Build from source Needs Node.js 20+, tmux, Xcode and Flutter 3.47+ / Dart 3.13+: ```bash git clone https://github.com/autonomous-ai/openharness.git cd openharness (cd cli && npm ci) make install-cli cd desktop flutter config --enable-swift-package-manager flutter pub get flutter run -d macos ``` `make install-cli` installs this checkout's CLI and restarts the local daemon. See the [development guide](docs/development.md).
## Beyond code: Build across disciplines > “World-class entrepreneurs are polymaths.” — [Peter Thiel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h10kXgTdhNU&t=811s) Coding agents can build far more than software. Give one a harness and it works with the real tools of a craft. You steer in a live viewer. Every clip below is a real session. ### Beyond code: Design **[Blender](store/agents/blender/).** Ask for a lamp and the sliders that matter. Turn them and Blender rebuilds the geometry. Keep the versions you love.

### Beyond code: Circuits **[CircuitJS](store/agents/circuitjs/).** Build a filter. Change one resistor. Overlay the new trace, measure the difference and keep both.

### Beyond code: Robotics **[MuJoCo](store/agents/mujoco/).** Pin a moment in a robot's run. Shove it with 100 N. Watch two futures split.

### Beyond code: Games **[Godogen](store/agents/godogen/).** Your agent makes a playable game. Miss a jump, rewind, try again. Pin the moment so the agent sees what you mean.

### Beyond code: Music **[Strudel](store/agents/strudel/).** The track is code you can perform. Bring voices in and out, mark the good parts, keep the WAV. [Hear it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3d4381b-5f55-406c-9d68-330cd8792fc5).

### Beyond code: Chemistry **[RDKit](store/agents/rdkit/).** Turn a bond and watch the molecule move. Follow the real energy curve. Keep the pose worth a closer look.

### Beyond code: Documents **[Typst](store/agents/typst/).** Your agent writes a real PDF. Circle a detail, quote a line, leave a note. The next draft answers it.

## Domain-specific harnesses (DSH) Code is the common medium. Geometry scripts make parts. Netlists make boards. Animation code makes film. A **domain-specific harness** turns a coding agent into a specialist. It brings the craft's instructions and skills, a pinned toolchain, a project template, checks and a **live viewer**. You chat on one side. The board, the part or the game takes shape on the other. The agent does the reasoning. The harness supplies the tools and the view. It's a folder with a `harness.json`, so adding a craft never touches the app. ### 49 harnesses in the Store | Category | Agents and harnesses | |---|---| | **Coding** | [Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Hermes, Command Code, Devin, Muse Code, Amp, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, Kilo Code](docs/engines.md), [Machine Monitor](store/agents/machine-monitor/), [Trail of Bits Skills](store/agents/trailofbits-skills/) | | Essentials | [Harness Monitor](store/agents/harness-monitor/), [Memories](store/agents/memories/) | | Design | [Autonomous Workshop](store/agents/autonomous-workshop/), [Blender](store/agents/blender/), [Bonsai MCP](store/agents/bonsai-mcp/), [Creative Direction](store/agents/creative-direction/), [Excalidraw](store/agents/excalidraw/), [FreeCAD](store/agents/freecad/), [Generative Art](store/agents/generative-art/), [OpenSCAD](store/agents/openscad/), [text-to-cad](store/agents/text-to-cad/) | | Engineering | [Autonomous Circuit](store/agents/autonomous-circuit/), [CircuitJS](store/agents/circuitjs/), [Home Assistant](store/agents/home-assistant/), [KiCad](store/agents/kicad/), [Orca Slicer](store/agents/orca-slicer/), [Yosys](store/agents/yosys/) | | Media | [Comfy MCP](store/agents/comfy-mcp/), [Manim](store/agents/manim/), [OpenMontage](store/agents/openmontage/), [Remotion](store/agents/remotion/) | | Music | [Ableton AI](store/agents/ableton-ai/), [JUCE Agent Toolkit](store/agents/juce-agent-toolkit/), [Music Studio](store/agents/music-studio/), [Score](store/agents/score/), [Strudel](store/agents/strudel/) | | Productivity | [Marp](store/agents/marp/), [Typst](store/agents/typst/) | | Science & Data | [autoresearch-mlx](store/agents/autoresearch-mlx/), [Data Studio](store/agents/data-studio/), [Lab Bench](store/agents/lab-bench/), [marimo](store/agents/marimo/), [RDKit](store/agents/rdkit/) | | Simulation | [DimOS](store/agents/dimos/), [Drone Pilot](store/agents/drone-pilot/), [Foam-Agent](store/agents/foam-agent/), [MuJoCo](store/agents/mujoco/), [SimSkill](store/agents/simskill/) | | Games | [Game Master](store/agents/game-master/), [Godogen](store/agents/godogen/), [Phaser](store/agents/phaser/), [Voxel Worlds](store/agents/voxel-worlds/) | | Research | [Roundtable](store/agents/roundtable/) | | Local AI | [MLX-LM](store/agents/mlx-lm/), [Model Manager](store/agents/autonomous-grid/), [Ollama](store/agents/ollama/), [vLLM](store/agents/vllm/) | Upstream open-source tools and original workflows. 10 [shared viewers](store/viewers/) install alongside the harnesses that need them. Unlisted experiments are not shown. ### Build your own The next harness is the one for your craft. Wrap a tool you love or your team's toolchain. It can live here or in your own repo. From this repo: ```json { "spec": 1, "id": "examples/hello-world", "name": "Hello World", "engine": "codex", "workspace": { "template": "template", "marker": "index.html" }, "agent": { "instructions": "AGENTS.md" }, "viewer": { "use": "autonomous/web-viewer" } } ``` ```bash harness dsh install "$PWD/store/viewers/web-viewer" --link cp -R store/examples/hello-world ../my-harness harness dsh check ../my-harness harness dsh install ../my-harness --link ``` Press **⌘N → Hello World** and say hello. The [authoring guide](store/README.md) covers the rest. ## Harness device [**Get a Harness device**](https://www.autonomous.ai/harness-device), or build your own from the files below. The [firmware guide](devices/harness-device/firmware/README.md) lists the supported boards and build commands, and the [hardware guide](devices/harness-device/hardware/README.md) covers the design files.

The optional **Harness device** is a round, always-on display that sits beside your keyboard and shows your agents at a glance: what each one is doing, which one has finished, and which one is waiting on you. Read a question and answer it on the screen, or tap and speak a new task, without switching windows. It is open hardware, all the way down. This repository has everything it takes to build one: | Layer | What's here | |---|---| | [Firmware](devices/harness-device/firmware/) | ESP32-S3, ESP-IDF, a 466 × 466 round AMOLED with touch, microphones and audio. Connects to the host's daemon over USB — no Wi-Fi setup, no account on the device. | | [PCB](devices/harness-device/hardware/pcb/) | The EasyEDA Pro project, the schematic, Gerbers, the bill of materials, and pick-and-place data for assembly. | | [Enclosure](devices/harness-device/hardware/3d/) | STEP for editing and STL for printing: the housing, an iron counterweight base, the USB clamp, and the button. | ## Contribute Make a harness for a tool you love. Improve terminals, engines, the daemon or the relay. Port the firmware. Start with the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md). [Architecture](docs/architecture.md) · [Product direction (proposal)](docs/product-direction.md) · [Development](docs/development.md) · [Extending](docs/extending.md) · [CLI](docs/cli.md) · [Security](SECURITY.md) · [MIT license](LICENSE); upstream tools keep their own.

repository.readme:
# Gaia: A Skill Tree 🌲 **Share your skill. We prove that it works. Then we name it to you.** Gaia is not a marketplace of skills, or an installer of some sorts. What we do is we verify your skill, check its capability, and reward them to those who AUTHORED them. Not the model, not the AI, but the HUMAN who authored them. [![Validate](https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree/actions/workflows/validate.yml) [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ### Gaia Ecosystem [![Skill Tree](https://img.shields.io/badge/Skill_Tree-gaiaskilltree.com-f59e0b)](https://gaiaskilltree.com/) [![Research](https://img.shields.io/badge/Research-research.gaiaskilltree.com-ec4899)](https://research.gaiaskilltree.com/) [![Skill Heaven Preview](https://img.shields.io/badge/Skill_Heaven_Preview-gaia--research.github.io%2Fgaia--skill--heaven-a58ae0)](https://gaia-research.github.io/gaia-skill-heaven/) 👉 **Have an original skill? Send it to us.** Run ``` curl -fsSL https://gaiaskilltree.com/install.sh | sh ``` and push your first skill in under 2 minutes. # A few have been named already. Your skill got appraised? Badge is yours forever. [![Gaia rank](https://gaiaskilltree.com/badges/_assets/mbtiongson1/rank.svg?repo=gaia-research%2Fgaia-skill-tree)](https://gaiaskilltree.com/u/mbtiongson1/)
[![Gaia](https://gaiaskilltree.com/badges/_assets/gaia-research/ci-churn.svg?repo=gaia-research%2Fgaia-skill-tree)](https://gaiaskilltree.com/named/#explorer/gaia-research/ci-churn) Generate yours at **[gaiaskilltree.com/badges/](https://gaiaskilltree.com/badges/)**. **Brand & product:** [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md) · [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) · [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) **Keywords:** AI Agent Skill registry • Evidence-Backed Skill Graph • Capability Graph • Model Context Protocol • AI Agents • Attribution --- # Who maintains this? Right now just me. Truth is, Gaia will exist even without anyone sending their skills. I built this because skills should be attributed to the people who proved them. Permanently, not just until the repo goes private. So that means, its the developers who make skills maintaining this. I have a thorough curation process, and the dev community is evidence on why this works. As long as developers making skills exists, this registry will exist. This is open-source, so feel free to contribute! # The structure--literally a "tree" as you know it: ```text ◆ mattpocock/skills [5★] ├─ ○ mattpocock/domain-modeling [2★] ├─ · mattpocock/engineering [4★] │ ├─ · mattpocock/setup-matt-pocock-skills [3★] │ │ ├─ ○ mattpocock/edit-article [3★] │ │ └─ ○ /tool-use │ ├─ · mattpocock/diagnose [3★] │ │ ├─ ○ emilkowalski/write-swift [4★] │ │ ├─ ○ /code-execution │ │ └─ ○ garrytan/correction-pipeline [2★] │ ├─ ○ ████████/zoom-out │ ├─ ○ mattpocock/domain-modeling [2★] (↑ see above) │ ├─ · mattpocock/grill-with-docs [3★] │ │ ├─ · mattpocock/grill-me [3★] │ │ │ └─ ○ /self-critique ◆ garrytan/gstack [5★] ├─ ○ garrytan/office-hours [3★] ├─ ○ garrytan/benchmark [2★] ├─ · garrytan/plan-eng-review [3★] │ ├─ ○ emilkowalski/write-swift [4★] │ ├─ ○ /diff-content │ └─ ○ garrytan/benchmark [2★] (↑ see above) ├─ ○ nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max [4★] ├─ · addy-osmani/planning-and-task-breakdown [3★] │ ├─ ○ /plan-decompose │ └─ ○ garrytan/functional-area-resolver [2★] ├─ · garrytan/design-consultation [2★] │ ├─ · firecrawl/firecrawl-build [2★] │ │ ├─ ○ firecrawl/firecrawl-build-search [3★] │ │ └─ ○ /computer-use Uniques — Basic Skills that reached elite mastery (4★+) through depth alone, with no fusion path forward. ◉ emilkowalski/animation-performance [4★] ├─ ○ addy-osmani/performance-optimization [2★] └─ ○ emilkowalski/animate [4★] ◉ cathrynlavery/diagram-design [4★] ├─ ○ /data-visualize (311 skills total — see docs/tree.md) ``` ### Skills can fuse. Here's how: Do a `gaia scan` and `gaia fuse` render in your terminal: ```text mattpocock/grill-me ────────────┐ ├──▶ mattpocock/grill-with-docs ◇ mattpocock/ubiquitous-language ─┘ ``` Then the whole tree emerges from the fusions. Here's what it looks like. Direct link: https://gaiaskilltree.com/named/#explorer/mattpocock/skills > [!TIP] > **New here?** The interactive tutorial at **[gaiaskilltree.com](https://gaiaskilltree.com/)** covers everything visually: skill tiers, the stars axis, and copy-paste commands. --- ## Stars | Stars | Rank | Notes | |------:|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------| | 0★ | Starless | | | 1★ | Awakened | Default star rank once you push | | 2★ | Named | You get to be on the tree if you reach here | | 3★ | Evolved | You ranked up!! | | 4★ | Extra / Unique | Extra (skill packs/suites), Unique (standalone) | | 5★ | Ultimate | Ultimate / Unique Ultimate | | 6★ | Apex | Apex / Unique Impossible | ## Evidence 1. **Evidence Type** | # | Evidence Type | Notes | |---|---------------|-------| | 1 | `arxiv` | scientific papers | | 2 | `repo` / `repo-own` | contains a repo link | | 3 | `github-stars` | how many github stars you have | | 4 | `peer-review` | someone reviewed your skill | | 5 | `social-signal` | youtube, X, or any post | | 6 | `proxy` | someone used your skill, maybe in another repo and it has a lot of stars | | 7 | `benchmark-result` | benchmark that showcases your skill | | 8 | `verifier-attestation` | our own verifiers attest to your skill | | 9 | `fusion-recipe` | gaia's own fusion structure | 2. **Evidence Grade** | Evidence Name | Grade | |---|----------------| | Platinum | S | | Gold | A | | Silver | B | | Bronze | C | | Grey | ungraded | 4. **Trust Magnitude** This is the evidence grade at the Skill level. > **Detailed Policy:** See [META.md](META.md) for the full evidence methodology, ranking floors, and prestige requirements. > **Public Trust Ledger:** The Trust Ledger ranks every named skill by computed Trust Magnitude — see [`docs/trust/ledger/`](docs/trust/ledger/) (deployed at once the site rebuilds). --- ## Quickstart **1. CLI** Current Gaia CLI version: `9.4.0`. ```bash curl -fsSL https://gaiaskilltree.com/install.sh | sh ``` Python installation alternative: ```bash pip install gaia-cli ```
pipx / Windows alternatives **pipx:** ```bash brew install pipx pipx install gaia-cli ``` **Windows** (PowerShell one-liner installer): ```powershell iex (irm https://gaiaskilltree.com/install.ps1) ``` Manual Python/pip fallback (Windows): ```powershell py -m pip install gaia-cli $env:PATH += ";" + (python -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_path('scripts', 'nt_user'))") ``` **Full Install (for devs)** (editable install with all extras): ```bash git clone https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree.git cd gaia-skill-tree pip install -e ".[embeddings,dev,docs]" ``` The `dev` extra installs packaging/test tools such as `build` and `pytest`; without it, packaging-specific tests are skipped locally with guidance to install developer extras.
**Update** ```bash gaia update ``` **2. Init / Scan** ```bash gaia init ``` ```bash gaia scan ``` Your repo will be scanned for existing skills. Everything will be in `.gaia` folder. **3. Push to this repo!** ```bash gaia push ``` A GitHub issue opens automatically. Don't worry, we thoroughly review every intake. **4. Agent Plugin & MCP** ```bash claude plugin install skill-heaven@gaia-skill-heaven ``` Installs Skill Heaven for Claude Code, bundling its own summon MCP server. Summon skills on demand with `/summon` without permanent context debt. (Note: Standalone `@gaia-research/mcp` is decommissioned and deprecated on npm as of 2026-08-19). --- ## Interactive TUI ```bash gaia ``` Will open all sorts of commands in a nice way. ```bash gaia skills ``` Navigate skills: - **Fuzzy search** by name, description, or intent - **View tree** (`^T`) and **run scan** (`^G`) without leaving the TUI - **Install skills** with one keystroke - Keyboard-native: `↑↓` navigate · `Enter` install · `q` quit --- ## CLI Reference ```text usage: gaia [-h] [--registry REGISTRY] [--global] [--version] {help,init,scan,steward,fetch,pull,update,install,uninstall,share,tree,push,propose,version,whoami,login,logout,reset,graph,stats,appraise,fuse,lookup,path,dev,skills,curate,trust,shadow} ... Gaia CLI options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --registry REGISTRY Path to a local registry checkout. Defaults to auto-resolved local or global registry. --global, -g Use global GAIA_HOME registry, ignoring any local .gaia/ config. --version, -v Print the Gaia CLI version and exit. --tui Launch the TUI (Terminal User Interface). --canon Show canonical registry data instead of local-first view. Getting started: gaia init [--user ] [--scan ] [--yes] [-y] gaia scan [--quiet] gaia push [--dry-run] [--no-issue] gaia Open command selector gaia skills Launch skills explorer (TUI) Daily commands: gaia tree [--named] [--title] gaia appraise [] gaia stats gaia steward scan [--json] gaia steward run [--json] gaia pull gaia fuse [--name ] gaia path [--owned-only] [--json] gaia lookup gaia graph [--format html|json] [-o ] [--no-open] gaia propose [] [--target ] [--no-pr] Skills: gaia skills gaia skills list [--exclude-pending] gaia skills search [--exclude-pending] gaia skills info [--exclude-pending] gaia skills install [--global | --local] gaia skills uninstall Share: gaia share [--user ] [-o ] [--stdout] gaia install Preview & install a shared tree (guided) Utilities: gaia whoami gaia login Sign in with GitHub (device flow) gaia logout Sign out of GitHub (clears the local token) gaia version gaia update gaia dev mcp gaia dev release gaia dev docs [--check] Maintainer commands: gaia dev --help ``` --- ## Agent Plugin & Summon The recommended path for Claude Code is the unified **Skill Heaven** plugin, which bundles its own MCP server: ```bash claude plugin install skill-heaven@gaia-skill-heaven ``` The core mechanic is **`/summon`** — materializing capabilities into session context on demand with zero ambient skill debt. *(Note: The standalone `@gaia-research/mcp` and `skill-hell` npm packages have been decommissioned and deprecated on npm as of 2026-08-19 in favor of the bundled Agent Plugin in `gaia-research/gaia-skill-heaven`.)* Source and releases: . See the [Skill Heaven site](https://gaia-research.github.io/gaia-skill-heaven/) for full installation and door options. --- ## API The registry is available as a static read-only JSON API — no authentication, no rate limits. - **Base URL:** `https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/` - **Docs:** [gaiaskilltree.com/api/](https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/) - **OpenAPI 3.1 spec:** [/api/v1/openapi.json](https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/openapi.json) Quick examples: ```bash # Health check curl https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/health.json # All skills (page 1, sorted by Trust Magnitude) curl https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/skills/index.json # Single skill detail curl https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/skills/garrytan/gstack.json # Trust leaderboard curl https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/leaderboard.json ``` --- ## Agent Discovery To help AI agents and automated clients discover and crawl the registry programmatically: - **registry graph:** [`/graph/gaia.json`](https://gaiaskilltree.com/graph/gaia.json) - **Named skills:** [`/named/`](https://gaiaskilltree.com/named/) - **Trust ledger:** [`/trust/ledger/`](https://gaiaskilltree.com/trust/ledger/) --- ## Ecosystem Companion tools that build on Gaia but run independently: - **[skill-fuse](https://github.com/gaia-research/skill-fuse)** — a standalone skill that combines two AI agent skills into one fused skill. Powered by Gaia, works without it. Registered in the registry as [`gaia-research/fuse`](https://gaiaskilltree.com/named/). --- ## Repository Structure ```text registry/ curated registry data and public generated catalogs registry-for-review/ pending skill batch intake records skill-trees/ per-user skill-tree.json files generated-output/ ignored local scan and render output docs/ docs site src/gaia_cli/ Python CLI package packages/cli-npm/ npm CLI wrapper scripts/ validation, rendering, docs, and release helpers tests/ Python test suite ``` --- ## Contributing Gaia is a shared map of agent capabilities. Common ways to help: - Review draft skills for clarity, overlap, and evidence quality. - Turn accepted reviews into concrete PRs (new skill, fusion, or reclassification). Contribution steps: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). # Gaia: A Skill Tree 🌲 **Share your skill. We prove that it works. Then we name it to you.** Gaia is not a marketplace of skills, or an installer of some sorts. What we do is we verify your skill, check its capability, and reward them to those who AUTHORED them. Not the model, not the AI, but the HUMAN who authored them. [![Validate](https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree/actions/workflows/validate.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree/actions/workflows/validate.yml) [![License: Apache 2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ### Gaia Ecosystem [![Skill Tree](https://img.shields.io/badge/Skill_Tree-gaiaskilltree.com-f59e0b)](https://gaiaskilltree.com/) [![Research](https://img.shields.io/badge/Research-research.gaiaskilltree.com-ec4899)](https://research.gaiaskilltree.com/) [![Skill Heaven Preview](https://img.shields.io/badge/Skill_Heaven_Preview-gaia--research.github.io%2Fgaia--skill--heaven-a58ae0)](https://gaia-research.github.io/gaia-skill-heaven/) 👉 **Have an original skill? Send it to us.** Run ``` curl -fsSL https://gaiaskilltree.com/install.sh | sh ``` and push your first skill in under 2 minutes. # A few have been named already. Your skill got appraised? Badge is yours forever. [![Gaia rank](https://gaiaskilltree.com/badges/_assets/mbtiongson1/rank.svg?repo=gaia-research%2Fgaia-skill-tree)](https://gaiaskilltree.com/u/mbtiongson1/)
[![Gaia](https://gaiaskilltree.com/badges/_assets/gaia-research/ci-churn.svg?repo=gaia-research%2Fgaia-skill-tree)](https://gaiaskilltree.com/named/#explorer/gaia-research/ci-churn) Generate yours at **[gaiaskilltree.com/badges/](https://gaiaskilltree.com/badges/)**. **Brand & product:** [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md) · [CONTEXT.md](CONTEXT.md) · [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) **Keywords:** AI Agent Skill registry • Evidence-Backed Skill Graph • Capability Graph • Model Context Protocol • AI Agents • Attribution --- # Who maintains this? Right now just me. Truth is, Gaia will exist even without anyone sending their skills. I built this because skills should be attributed to the people who proved them. Permanently, not just until the repo goes private. So that means, its the developers who make skills maintaining this. I have a thorough curation process, and the dev community is evidence on why this works. As long as developers making skills exists, this registry will exist. This is open-source, so feel free to contribute! # The structure--literally a "tree" as you know it: ```text ◆ mattpocock/skills [5★] ├─ ○ mattpocock/domain-modeling [2★] ├─ · mattpocock/engineering [4★] │ ├─ · mattpocock/setup-matt-pocock-skills [3★] │ │ ├─ ○ mattpocock/edit-article [3★] │ │ └─ ○ /tool-use │ ├─ · mattpocock/diagnose [3★] │ │ ├─ ○ emilkowalski/write-swift [4★] │ │ ├─ ○ /code-execution │ │ └─ ○ garrytan/correction-pipeline [2★] │ ├─ ○ ████████/zoom-out │ ├─ ○ mattpocock/domain-modeling [2★] (↑ see above) │ ├─ · mattpocock/grill-with-docs [3★] │ │ ├─ · mattpocock/grill-me [3★] │ │ │ └─ ○ /self-critique ◆ garrytan/gstack [5★] ├─ ○ garrytan/office-hours [3★] ├─ ○ garrytan/benchmark [2★] ├─ · garrytan/plan-eng-review [3★] │ ├─ ○ emilkowalski/write-swift [4★] │ ├─ ○ /diff-content │ └─ ○ garrytan/benchmark [2★] (↑ see above) ├─ ○ nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max [4★] ├─ · addy-osmani/planning-and-task-breakdown [3★] │ ├─ ○ /plan-decompose │ └─ ○ garrytan/functional-area-resolver [2★] ├─ · garrytan/design-consultation [2★] │ ├─ · firecrawl/firecrawl-build [2★] │ │ ├─ ○ firecrawl/firecrawl-build-search [3★] │ │ └─ ○ /computer-use Uniques — Basic Skills that reached elite mastery (4★+) through depth alone, with no fusion path forward. ◉ emilkowalski/animation-performance [4★] ├─ ○ addy-osmani/performance-optimization [2★] └─ ○ emilkowalski/animate [4★] ◉ cathrynlavery/diagram-design [4★] ├─ ○ /data-visualize (311 skills total — see docs/tree.md) ``` ### Skills can fuse. Here's how: Do a `gaia scan` and `gaia fuse` render in your terminal: ```text mattpocock/grill-me ────────────┐ ├──▶ mattpocock/grill-with-docs ◇ mattpocock/ubiquitous-language ─┘ ``` Then the whole tree emerges from the fusions. Here's what it looks like. Direct link: https://gaiaskilltree.com/named/#explorer/mattpocock/skills > [!TIP] > **New here?** The interactive tutorial at **[gaiaskilltree.com](https://gaiaskilltree.com/)** covers everything visually: skill tiers, the stars axis, and copy-paste commands. --- ## Stars | Stars | Rank | Notes | |------:|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------| | 0★ | Starless | | | 1★ | Awakened | Default star rank once you push | | 2★ | Named | You get to be on the tree if you reach here | | 3★ | Evolved | You ranked up!! | | 4★ | Extra / Unique | Extra (skill packs/suites), Unique (standalone) | | 5★ | Ultimate | Ultimate / Unique Ultimate | | 6★ | Apex | Apex / Unique Impossible | ## Evidence 1. **Evidence Type** | # | Evidence Type | Notes | |---|---------------|-------| | 1 | `arxiv` | scientific papers | | 2 | `repo` / `repo-own` | contains a repo link | | 3 | `github-stars` | how many github stars you have | | 4 | `peer-review` | someone reviewed your skill | | 5 | `social-signal` | youtube, X, or any post | | 6 | `proxy` | someone used your skill, maybe in another repo and it has a lot of stars | | 7 | `benchmark-result` | benchmark that showcases your skill | | 8 | `verifier-attestation` | our own verifiers attest to your skill | | 9 | `fusion-recipe` | gaia's own fusion structure | 2. **Evidence Grade** | Evidence Name | Grade | |---|----------------| | Platinum | S | | Gold | A | | Silver | B | | Bronze | C | | Grey | ungraded | 4. **Trust Magnitude** This is the evidence grade at the Skill level. > **Detailed Policy:** See [META.md](META.md) for the full evidence methodology, ranking floors, and prestige requirements. > **Public Trust Ledger:** The Trust Ledger ranks every named skill by computed Trust Magnitude — see [`docs/trust/ledger/`](docs/trust/ledger/) (deployed at once the site rebuilds). --- ## Quickstart **1. CLI** Current Gaia CLI version: `9.4.0`. ```bash curl -fsSL https://gaiaskilltree.com/install.sh | sh ``` Python installation alternative: ```bash pip install gaia-cli ```
pipx / Windows alternatives **pipx:** ```bash brew install pipx pipx install gaia-cli ``` **Windows** (PowerShell one-liner installer): ```powershell iex (irm https://gaiaskilltree.com/install.ps1) ``` Manual Python/pip fallback (Windows): ```powershell py -m pip install gaia-cli $env:PATH += ";" + (python -c "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_path('scripts', 'nt_user'))") ``` **Full Install (for devs)** (editable install with all extras): ```bash git clone https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree.git cd gaia-skill-tree pip install -e ".[embeddings,dev,docs]" ``` The `dev` extra installs packaging/test tools such as `build` and `pytest`; without it, packaging-specific tests are skipped locally with guidance to install developer extras.
**Update** ```bash gaia update ``` **2. Init / Scan** ```bash gaia init ``` ```bash gaia scan ``` Your repo will be scanned for existing skills. Everything will be in `.gaia` folder. **3. Push to this repo!** ```bash gaia push ``` A GitHub issue opens automatically. Don't worry, we thoroughly review every intake. **4. Agent Plugin & MCP** ```bash claude plugin install skill-heaven@gaia-skill-heaven ``` Installs Skill Heaven for Claude Code, bundling its own summon MCP server. Summon skills on demand with `/summon` without permanent context debt. (Note: Standalone `@gaia-research/mcp` is decommissioned and deprecated on npm as of 2026-08-19). --- ## Interactive TUI ```bash gaia ``` Will open all sorts of commands in a nice way. ```bash gaia skills ``` Navigate skills: - **Fuzzy search** by name, description, or intent - **View tree** (`^T`) and **run scan** (`^G`) without leaving the TUI - **Install skills** with one keystroke - Keyboard-native: `↑↓` navigate · `Enter` install · `q` quit --- ## CLI Reference ```text usage: gaia [-h] [--registry REGISTRY] [--global] [--version] {help,init,scan,steward,fetch,pull,update,install,uninstall,share,tree,push,propose,version,whoami,login,logout,reset,graph,stats,appraise,fuse,lookup,path,dev,skills,curate,trust,shadow} ... Gaia CLI options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --registry REGISTRY Path to a local registry checkout. Defaults to auto-resolved local or global registry. --global, -g Use global GAIA_HOME registry, ignoring any local .gaia/ config. --version, -v Print the Gaia CLI version and exit. --tui Launch the TUI (Terminal User Interface). --canon Show canonical registry data instead of local-first view. Getting started: gaia init [--user ] [--scan ] [--yes] [-y] gaia scan [--quiet] gaia push [--dry-run] [--no-issue] gaia Open command selector gaia skills Launch skills explorer (TUI) Daily commands: gaia tree [--named] [--title] gaia appraise [] gaia stats gaia steward scan [--json] gaia steward run [--json] gaia pull gaia fuse [--name ] gaia path [--owned-only] [--json] gaia lookup gaia graph [--format html|json] [-o ] [--no-open] gaia propose [] [--target ] [--no-pr] Skills: gaia skills gaia skills list [--exclude-pending] gaia skills search [--exclude-pending] gaia skills info [--exclude-pending] gaia skills install [--global | --local] gaia skills uninstall Share: gaia share [--user ] [-o ] [--stdout] gaia install Preview & install a shared tree (guided) Utilities: gaia whoami gaia login Sign in with GitHub (device flow) gaia logout Sign out of GitHub (clears the local token) gaia version gaia update gaia dev mcp gaia dev release gaia dev docs [--check] Maintainer commands: gaia dev --help ``` --- ## Agent Plugin & Summon The recommended path for Claude Code is the unified **Skill Heaven** plugin, which bundles its own MCP server: ```bash claude plugin install skill-heaven@gaia-skill-heaven ``` The core mechanic is **`/summon`** — materializing capabilities into session context on demand with zero ambient skill debt. *(Note: The standalone `@gaia-research/mcp` and `skill-hell` npm packages have been decommissioned and deprecated on npm as of 2026-08-19 in favor of the bundled Agent Plugin in `gaia-research/gaia-skill-heaven`.)* Source and releases: . See the [Skill Heaven site](https://gaia-research.github.io/gaia-skill-heaven/) for full installation and door options. --- ## API The registry is available as a static read-only JSON API — no authentication, no rate limits. - **Base URL:** `https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/` - **Docs:** [gaiaskilltree.com/api/](https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/) - **OpenAPI 3.1 spec:** [/api/v1/openapi.json](https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/openapi.json) Quick examples: ```bash # Health check curl https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/health.json # All skills (page 1, sorted by Trust Magnitude) curl https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/skills/index.json # Single skill detail curl https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/skills/garrytan/gstack.json # Trust leaderboard curl https://gaiaskilltree.com/api/v1/leaderboard.json ``` --- ## Agent Discovery To help AI agents and automated clients discover and crawl the registry programmatically: - **registry graph:** [`/graph/gaia.json`](https://gaiaskilltree.com/graph/gaia.json) - **Named skills:** [`/named/`](https://gaiaskilltree.com/named/) - **Trust ledger:** [`/trust/ledger/`](https://gaiaskilltree.com/trust/ledger/) --- ## Ecosystem Companion tools that build on Gaia but run independently: - **[skill-fuse](https://github.com/gaia-research/skill-fuse)** — a standalone skill that combines two AI agent skills into one fused skill. Powered by Gaia, works without it. Registered in the registry as [`gaia-research/fuse`](https://gaiaskilltree.com/named/). --- ## Repository Structure ```text registry/ curated registry data and public generated catalogs registry-for-review/ pending skill batch intake records skill-trees/ per-user skill-tree.json files generated-output/ ignored local scan and render output docs/ docs site src/gaia_cli/ Python CLI package packages/cli-npm/ npm CLI wrapper scripts/ validation, rendering, docs, and release helpers tests/ Python test suite ``` --- ## Contributing Gaia is a shared map of agent capabilities. Common ways to help: - Review draft skills for clarity, overlap, and evidence quality. - Turn accepted reviews into concrete PRs (new skill, fusion, or reclassification). Contribution steps: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Programmatic Management The registry is programmatically managed. All meta shifts (adding, merging, splitting, adding evidence) must be performed via the [Gaia CLI](src/gaia_cli/). Hand-editing JSON nodes is deprecated to ensure schema integrity and automated timeline logging. --- ## Privacy Gaia does not store personal information. - **Skills are summarised, not stored.** `gaia scan` records capability type, level, and evidence grade — never file contents, prompt text, or conversation history. - **Only public repo links.** The registry stores your public GitHub username and a public repo URL when you explicitly submit a named skill. Nothing else. - **Generalised by default.** Skill descriptions capture capability categories, not personal details about you or your agent's behaviour. - **No telemetry.** The CLI and the static website collect zero analytics or usage data. Full details: [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) · [gaiaskilltree.com/privacy.html](https://gaiaskilltree.com/privacy.html) **Topics:** gaia-skill-tree, ai-agent, skill-registry, capability-graph, evidence-backed, agent-skills, attribution, model-context-protocol, open-source-ai, llm-ops, agent-framework --- ## Inspiration **Be like Rimuru.** The main inspiration for this repository. sampled_files.pyproject.toml:
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "gaia-cli"
version = "9.4.0"
description = "Gaia Skill Tree CLI for AI agents"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = {text = "MIT"}
authors = [
    { name = "Gaia contributors" },
]
keywords = ["ai", "agents", "cli", "skills", "registry"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Environment :: Console",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Natural Language :: English",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Python Modules",
    "Topic :: Utilities",
]
dependencies = [
    "jinja2>=3.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.17.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "questionary>=2.0.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
embeddings = [
    "sentence-transformers>=3.0.0",
    "numpy>=1.21.0",
]
interactive = []
tui = [
    "textual>=0.50.0",
]
# Optional OS-keychain backend for `gaia login` token storage (PRD #155).
# Without it, the token falls back to a chmod-600 file under GAIA_HOME — login
# still works, it just doesn't use the system keyring.
auth = [
    "keyring>=24.0",
]
# Minimum set required to run `gaia docs build` end-to-end.
# scripts/build_layouts_3d.py (invoked by scripts/generateProjections.py
# during tree.md regen) needs numpy + scipy.linalg for the 3D layout solve.
# Install with `pip install -e ".[docs]"` if you don't want the full [dev] extra.
docs = [
    "numpy>=1.21.0",
    "scipy>=1.7.0",
]
dev = [
    "build>=1.2.0",
    # Strict publication tests require genuine PNG rendering, never a skipped oracle.
    "cairosvg>=2.9.1",
    "numpy>=1.21.0",
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-timeout>=2.1.0",
    "pytest-xdist>=3.5.0",
    "ruff>=0.5.0",
    "scipy>=1.7.0",
    "setuptools>=77",
    "textual>=0.50.0",
    "twine>=5.0",
    "wheel>=0.42.0",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree"
Repository = "https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree"
Issues = "https://github.com/gaia-research/gaia-skill-tree/issues"
Documentation = "https://gaiaskilltree.com/"

[project.scripts]
gaia = "gaia_cli.main:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
include = ["gaia_cli*"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
gaia_cli = [
    "tui/theme.tcss",
    "data/curation/*.json",
    "data/frontier/*.json",
    "data/trust/*.json",
    "data/trust/*.jsonl",
    "data/registry/gaia.json",
    "data/registry/named-skills.json",
    "data/registry/support/*.json",
    "data/registry/benchmark-sources.json",
    "data/registry/named/**/*.md",
    "data/registry/named/**/*.json",
    "data/registry/schema/*.json",
    "data/registry/schema/evidence/*.json",
]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["src", "."]
testpaths = ["tests"]
timeout = 60
timeout_method = "thread"
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers"
markers = [
    "packaging: package build and wheel installation checks",
    "tui: requires the optional 'textual' package (pyproject [tui]/[dev] extra)",
    "smoke: fast pre-push subset; covers high-value contracts (schema sync, wheel build, init, registry resolution, docs cohesion)",
    "integration: spawns subprocesses, hits network/filesystem heavily, or exercises full CLI lifecycle — skipped in fast tier",
    "slow: any single test consistently >2s wall-clock — skipped in fast tier",
]

[tool.ruff]
