repository.readme: **Give the agent you already use a memory you control.** GBrain stores explicit facts with their sources, supports corrections and withdrawal, and makes the same memory available across your agents. Start with keyless memory and keyword retrieval; add semantic search, synthesis, and background enrichment when you need them. GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host; gbrain.io is optional paid hosting. > [!TIP] > **Need hosted? First time running an agent?** Try **[gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=readme)**, hosted GBrain, for the easiest experience: one brain for you and your team, connected to ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor, with nothing to install or keep online. Stuck? Email support@gbrain.io and a person will set it up with you, free. **Keep skills beside knowledge.** New local brains include memory skills in their content root. Agents can join an authorized catalog; only approved editors can publish. Managed coding-agent installs add an owned native router; restart and real-use verification are separate steps. Staged migration preserves sharing choices and personal edits. See [shared brain skills](docs/guides/shared-brain-skills.md). ## Choose your setup 1. **Add GBrain to my existing agent — recommended.** Keep your agent's identity and save memory inside its environment. No new personal-agent identity or private repository is required. Start with the guide for **[Grok Bot](docs/guides/grok-bot.md)**, **[Muse](docs/guides/muse.md)**, or **[Codex / Claude Code](docs/tutorials/connect-coding-agent.md)**. [Other harnesses](#connect-gbrain-to-your-ai-client-mcp). 2. **Use the brain on my own computer from everywhere.** One command publishes it over MCP on your Tailscale tailnet and keeps it running: `gbrain mcp expose` (add `--funnel` for cloud agents such as Grok Bot, Muse and ChatGPT). Follow **[use your brain from anywhere over MCP](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md)**. **Say to your agent:** *"use my brain over mcp"* — *"put my brain on tailscale"*. 3. **Connect my existing hosted brain.** Follow **[hosted harness access](docs/guides/hosted-harness-access.md)** to choose native OAuth or a private machine connection. For dashboard login, clients, and permissions, use **[MCP administration](docs/mcp/ADMIN.md)** with the server's separate owner credential. Delegation is an explicit choice. Grok **Bot** and Grok **Build** are different products. Muse's personal agent and **Muse Code** are different products too. Muse already has native editable memory; GBrain adds an explicit, portable record with provenance and shared access. See each guide's dated evidence and remaining verification steps. I'm Garry Tan, President and CEO of Y Combinator. I built GBrain to run my own AI agents. It's the production brain behind my OpenClaw and Hermes deployments: **155,795 pages, 24,589 people, 5,340 companies**, 66 cron jobs running autonomously. My agent ingests meetings, emails, tweets, voice calls, and original ideas while I sleep. It enriches every person and company it encounters. It fixes its own citations and consolidates memory overnight. I wake up smarter than when I went to bed — and so will you. **It works as a company brain too.** Authenticated remote clients are constrained by source and operation grants plus visibility filters. Local files and shared database credentials are a different trust boundary: sources alone do not isolate those callers. The authorization tests exercise specific access paths, not a universal no-leak guarantee. Read the [sharing boundaries](docs/architecture/brains-and-sources.md#what-confines-remote-callers-and-what-does-not) and [company-brain tutorial](docs/tutorials/company-brain.md) before setting up shared access. Alongside keyword and semantic retrieval, GBrain offers two optional ways to use your stored knowledge: - **A synthesis layer that gives you the actual answer.** Synthesized, well-cited prose across people, companies, deals, and ideas. Not "here are 10 chunks that mention your query"; an actual answer with citations and an explicit note on what the brain doesn't know yet. The gap analysis is the part that changes how you use the brain. - **A typed knowledge graph.** Trusted local page writes extract supported references without LLM calls when auto-linking is enabled. Remote `put_page` edges arrive later, via sweeps, maintenance or `add_link`. Ask "who works at acme-example?": walks are breadth-first, milliseconds on dense clusters ([how](docs/architecture/RETRIEVAL.md#breadth-first-graph-walks)). On BrainBench relationship questions, relationship retrieval lifts production **R@5 from 0.6626 to 0.7241** ([benchmark](docs/architecture/RETRIEVAL.md#the-benchmark)); 0.9791 is the `graph-oracle-parse` upper bound, not a product score. The point of building a 150K-page brain is to use it as a strategic moat. To never lose context. To query what's in your own head without re-reading it. The brain layer is what makes the moat usable. The 24/7 dream cycle is what keeps it sharp. Both run on your hardware, your DB, your keys. It's easier to ship a daemon that runs 24/7 to ingest, enrich, and consolidate than it is to keep an agent in chat working hard. GBrain is that daemon, generalized. Install in 30 minutes. Your agent does the work. As my personal agent gets smarter, so does yours. > **Start keyless.** Your harness subscription and any separately configured model API usage are different costs. The optional personal-agent bootstrap takes about 15 minutes; always-on enrichment needs its own compute and API configuration. Durable preferences and facts can be shared across agents; transient task and harness configuration state stay local. Configured cloud embedding, reranking, extraction, and synthesis providers can receive text, and the harness model sees recalled memory even in keyless mode. Markdown export is not a full database backup. Read [memory boundaries](docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md). > **LLMs:** fetch [`llms.txt`](llms.txt) for the documentation map, or [`llms-full.txt`](llms-full.txt) for the same map with core docs inlined in one fetch. **Agents:** start with [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) (or [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) if you're Claude Code). ## What this looks like Say you have a meeting with Alice tomorrow. You want to walk in remembering what she works on, when you last talked, and what's still open between you. Here's what you'd type, and what you'd get back. **You ask:** > "What do I need to know before my meeting with Alice tomorrow?" **Most personal-knowledge tools give you back a list of pages.** Something like: ``` 1. people/alice — Alice runs engineering at Acme... 2. meetings/2026-03-15-alice-q1 — Q1 product review with Alice... 3. meetings/2026-01-08-acme-kickoff — Kickoff meeting with Acme team... 4. customers/acme — Acme is a series-B fintech we work with... 5. notes/2026-04-22 — Quick chat with Alice about pricing... ``` Five pages you now have to open and read yourself to actually prepare. The tool found the right material, but it didn't do the work. **GBrain gives you back the answer, with sources:** ``` Alice runs engineering at Acme (a series-B fintech). You last spoke on April 22 in a quick pricing chat. Three things are still open from that conversation: 1. She owes you the security review for the new tier (deadline was May 1; no update since). 2. You committed to pricing for a 500-seat tier (you sent it April 25; no response yet). 3. She mentioned they're hiring a CISO; you said you'd intro someone from your network. Heads up: nothing's been added to the brain about Alice or Acme since April 22, six weeks ago. She may have replied through email or Slack DM, channels the brain doesn't see. Worth asking her to catch up before assuming any of this is still current. ``` Every claim has a source page behind it. The "heads up" at the end tells you what the brain doesn't know yet, so you can ask Alice about it directly instead of being surprised. The brain just did your meeting prep. This is the difference between a search engine and a brain. Search finds the pages. The brain reads them for you and writes the answer. ## Install > [!TIP] > **Fastest: hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/cli?ref=readme), for any harness.** One command launches a GBrain hosted on gbrain.io; Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT, Cursor and every other AI you use connect to it, with nothing to keep online. > > ```bash > curl -sSL https://gbrainio.terminalwire.sh | bash > gbrainio terminal connect # in a new terminal > gbrainio workspace new # pick a plan in the browser > curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash # skip if Bun 1.4.4+ is installed > export PATH="$HOME/.bun/bin:$PATH" > bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable # the gbrain CLI only; no local brain > # Claude Code (an existing gbrain entry is kept): > (claude mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || claude mcp add --transport http --scope user gbrain https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup claude-code --instructions-only > # Codex (an existing gbrain entry is kept): > (codex mcp get gbrain >/dev/null 2>&1 || codex mcp add gbrain --url https://gbrain.io/mcp) && gbrain setup codex --instructions-only > ``` > > `gbrain setup --instructions-only` tells the agent the brain is there; agents seldom call an MCP server nobody told them about. It writes the [brain-first block](docs/guides/setup.md#brain-first-instructions) into `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or Codex's `AGENTS.md` (a non-empty `AGENTS.override.md` instead when Codex has one) with a per-turn rule hook, and leaves the MCP entry alone; the same command with `--no-instructions` added takes them out. > > The installer is a shell script for macOS and Linux; read it before you run it. ### Here's how to self-host it GBrain is MIT-licensed and free to self-host. It needs **Bun 1.4.4 or newer**; existing worker installs read the [authorization and queue upgrade guide](docs/guides/authorization-upgrade.md) before restarting on this version. > [!WARNING] > **GBrain is NOT distributed on npm.** The npm `gbrain` package is unrelated and > can shadow the real binary, so never run `npm install -g gbrain` or > `bun add -g gbrain`. Install only via `bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable` > (the soaked stable channel; `#latest-stable` is the alpha line with every release) > or `git clone --branch stable` + `bun install && bun link`. Installed by mistake? `gbrain doctor` gives the fix. > Schema not migrated ([#218](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues/218))? Run > `gbrain apply-migrations --yes --no-autopilot-install`; if it exits 1, run `gbrain doctor --json`, not another `--yes` (`wedged`: relay its fix). ```bash bun install -g github:garrytan/gbrain#stable gbrain setup claude-code # or: gbrain setup codex gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding # any other harness, or no agent ``` `gbrain setup` shows what it will write first (`--dry-run` previews, `--remove` undoes), creates a keyless brain only if none exists, wires MCP, hooks and a brain-first block in the agent's instruction file (`--no-instructions` skips it), and smoke-tests them ([setup guide](docs/guides/setup.md)). For any other coding agent, paste: ```text Add GBrain memory to this existing agent. Read and follow: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/master/INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md Keep my current identity and instructions, start keyless, and show me the search-mode choice. Verify a remember/recall round trip with real GBrain calls. ``` Postgres, thin clients, API keys and upgrades: [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md). Agents: [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md). Memory-only walkthrough: [give your coding agent a memory](docs/tutorials/connect-coding-agent.md). ### CLI standalone (no agent) ```bash gbrain init --pglite --no-embedding # keyless; no server, no Docker gbrain import ~/notes/ --no-embed # index your markdown gbrain search "a phrase from a note" --json gbrain doctor # verify health ``` ### Optional: a new personal agent To have GBrain create a **new persistent personal agent** with identity files and its own private GitHub repo, open Codex (CLI or ChatGPT desktop) or Claude Code in a new, empty folder and paste: ``` Read and follow every step of: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/garrytan/gbrain/stable/BOOTSTRAP_FOR_AGENTS.md Goal: set yourself up as my persistent personal agent in this folder, with gbrain as your memory. Interview me before writing any identity file — never invent answers. Ask before anything destructive. You are not done until `gbrain bootstrap verify` exits 0. ``` The repo is not a complete backup; see the [bootstrap guide](docs/guides/bootstrap.md). For the always-on version (24/7 ingestion and the overnight dream cycle on a server with 8GB+ RAM and its own API usage), run GBrain under [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) or [Hermes](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent) and point it at `INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`; the [personal-brain tutorial](docs/tutorials/personal-brain.md) walks it end to end. ### Connect GBrain to your AI client (MCP) - **Local stdio client:** `gbrain setup claude-code` or `gbrain setup codex` registers `gbrain serve` (lists the memory verbs; `--surface full` lists every tool) behind gbrain's launcher, so a session opened in a cloned repository never loads that repository's `bunfig.toml` or `.env`, and adds the brain-first instructions: agents seldom call a brain nobody told them about. Cursor, Windsurf and other stdio clients take `"$(command -v gbrain)" serve --surface starter --advertise verbs`. - **Plugins with curated skills:** Codex `codex plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain@codex-plugin` + `codex plugin add gbrain@gbrain`; Claude Code `/plugin marketplace add garrytan/gbrain` + `/plugin install gbrain@gbrain`. - **This brain from anywhere:** `gbrain mcp expose` publishes it on your Tailscale tailnet as a user service (`--funnel` for cloud agents such as Grok Bot, Muse and ChatGPT). [Guide](docs/guides/remote-mcp.md). - **A brain on another host:** `gbrain connect https://your-host/mcp --token gbrain_xxx --install` (add `--agent codex` for Codex). Hosted brains use [native OAuth or a private handoff](docs/guides/hosted-harness-access.md); dashboard, clients and permissions live in [MCP administration](docs/mcp/ADMIN.md). Per-client guides: [Claude Code](docs/mcp/CLAUDE_CODE.md) · [Codex](docs/mcp/CODEX.md) · [ChatGPT](docs/mcp/CHATGPT.md) · [Claude Desktop](docs/mcp/CLAUDE_DESKTOP.md) · [Claude Cowork](docs/mcp/CLAUDE_COWORK.md) · [Perplexity](docs/mcp/PERPLEXITY.md) · [Hermes](docs/mcp/HERMES.md) · [OpenClaw](docs/mcp/OPENCLAW.md) · [opencode](docs/mcp/OPENCODE.md) · [Grok Build](docs/mcp/GROK.md) · [Grok Bot](docs/guides/grok-bot.md) · [Muse](docs/guides/muse.md) · [everything MCP](docs/mcp/README.md). ## Two ways to query your brain Raw retrieval (what most personal-knowledge tools ship) and a synthesis layer that gives you an actual answer. They serve different jobs. ```bash # raw retrieval: top pages by hybrid score, no answer-generation call gbrain search "who's working on AI agents at portfolio companies?" # brain layer: synthesized answer with citations and gap analysis gbrain think "who's working on AI agents at portfolio companies?" ``` **`gbrain search`** returns the top retrieved pages, ranked by hybrid scoring (vector + keyword + RRF + source-tier boost + reranker). Use it when you want raw material to skim: agent context windows, citation lookups, finding a specific quote. Configured embedding and reranking providers can still receive text and charge for retrieval. Keyless keyword search needs no model API; synthesis requires a configured chat capability. See [memory boundaries](docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md#where-text-goes). Search also tells you when its results are incomplete because projections are still rebuilding or a bounded vector scan ran short. Ask your agent *"Check whether my search index is ready"*; see [search readiness and recovery](docs/architecture/RETRIEVAL.md#chunk-rebuilds-after-upgrading) before treating an empty result as proof that a page is missing. **`gbrain think`** runs the same retrieval, then composes a synthesized answer across the results with explicit citations to the source pages AND an honest note on what the brain doesn't know yet. The gap analysis is the differentiator: the answer tells you when a page is stale, when a claim is uncited, when two pages contradict each other, when there's a hole you should fill. **Say to your agent:** *"What do we know about acme-example?"* — *"Tell me about alice-example before my meeting tomorrow"* — *"Search for who's working on AI agents."* Your agent routes these to the brain automatically; you never type the commands yourself. **Why it compounds.** Pair the brain layer with `find_trajectory` and you get answers like *"how have the company's metrics changed AND what does the team look like right now AND what did they promise / share AND when did we last meet AND what's the value-add I can offer here"*: well-scored, well-cited, in one shot. That's the strategic moat. That's why building a 150K-page brain is worth the effort. `gbrain agent run "..."` exposes the same surface to a sub-agent through the Minions queue, with crash-safe two-phase persistence. Same answers, durable. ## How to get data in Start with an explicit fact or a notes folder; opt into connectors, capture, and enrichment separately. **Already have a company knowledge repository?** Say to your agent: *“Connect our existing company brain, preserve its files, and show me the import plan first.”* Try `gbrain sources demo company-brain` without keys or private data, then inspect your committed Markdown with `gbrain sources inspect --profile company-brain`. The [company-brain ingestion guide](docs/guides/company-brain-ingestion.md) covers explicit destination approval, typed relationships, and resumable verification. It does not enable embeddings, sharing, schedules, or curation automatically. **Say to your agent:** *"Remember this with its source"* — *"What should I import first?"* [Data ingestion guide](docs/guides/data-ingestion.md) covers files, conversations, connectors, Google data, and capture commands. ## Your brain's shape (schema packs) Most personal-knowledge tools force one fixed layout: their idea of "notes" + "people" + "tags." Drop a Notion export or your own years-old Obsidian vault on top, and the agent doesn't know what a `Projects/` folder means or whether `Reading/` is people or sources. **gbrain doesn't have a fixed layout.** It ships with bundled schema packs and lets you author your own when none fit: - **`gbrain-base-v2`** (default) — 15-type DRY/MECE canonical taxonomy (14 canonical + `note` catch-all): `person`, `company`, `media`, `tweet`, `social-digest`, `analysis`, `atom`, `concept`, `source`, `deal`, `email`, `slack`, `writing`, `project`, `note`. Subtypes/format/origin pushed to frontmatter. - **`gbrain-base`** (legacy) — the wider 24-type layout. Stays bundled for back-compat; brains on it can upgrade via `gbrain onboard --check --explain` → `gbrain jobs submit unify-types --params '{"target_pack":"gbrain-base-v2","apply":true}'` (omit `"apply":true` for a dry-run preview — that is the default). - **`gbrain-recommended`** — extends `gbrain-base` with the 13 additional directories from `docs/GBRAIN_RECOMMENDED_SCHEMA.md` (source, place, trip, conversation, personal, civic, project, etc.). Activate with `gbrain schema use gbrain-recommended`. - **Your own pack** — `gbrain schema detect` clusters your actual filesystem into proposed types, `gbrain schema suggest` runs an LLM pass over them, and `gbrain schema review-candidates --apply` promotes the ones you like. Three commands and the brain knows your shape. Authoring a successor pack (declares `migration_from:` so existing brains can opt in): see [`docs/architecture/pack-upgrade-mechanism.md`](docs/architecture/pack-upgrade-mechanism.md). ```bash gbrain schema active # which pack is running, which tier set it gbrain schema list # bundled + installed packs gbrain schema detect # propose types matching your filesystem gbrain schema suggest # LLM-refined proposals on top of detect gbrain schema review-candidates # human gate: promote / rename / ignore gbrain schema use my-pack # activate ``` **Say to your agent:** *"My schema isn't matching my notes — propose new types from my corpus"* — *"Add a page type for lab results to my brain's schema."* The schema-author skill runs the detect → suggest → review flow for you. The active pack threads through every read + write path: `parseMarkdown` infers page type from the pack's path prefixes; `whoknows` scopes expert routing to types declared `expert_routing: true`; `extract_facts` runs only on `extractable: true` types. The retained search-cache key includes the pack name + version, but semantic result reuse is temporarily disabled. Switch packs and the brain re-interprets itself; switch back and nothing's lost. Seven-tier resolution chain (per-call flag → env var → per-source DB key → brain-wide DB key → `gbrain.yml` → `~/.gbrain/config.json` → `gbrain-base` default). Full reference + authoring guide: [`docs/architecture/schema-packs.md`](docs/architecture/schema-packs.md). ## Tutorials Step-by-step walkthroughs for getting the most out of GBrain. Each one takes you from zero to a working outcome, with concrete commands and real numbers. - [**Set up your personal AI agent + brain from zero**](docs/tutorials/personal-brain.md) — the canonical full-stack install. Two GitHub repos, a Telegram bot, AlphaClaw on Render, OpenClaw + GBrain + Supabase. End-to-end in about 2 hours. - [**Set up GBrain as your company brain**](docs/tutorials/company-brain.md) — federated, multi-user, OAuth-scoped institutional memory for a 10-50 person team. About 90 minutes end-to-end. - [**Auto-improve a skill with `gbrain skillopt`**](docs/tutorials/improving-skills-with-skillopt.md) — treat a `SKILL.md` as a trainable parameter. Generate a starter benchmark straight from the skill with `--bootstrap-from-skill` (or write your own), strengthen the judges, then watch the optimizer propose edits and keep only the ones that measurably score higher. ~20 minutes, ~$1 in API calls. Flag + cost + safety reference: [`docs/guides/skillopt.md`](docs/guides/skillopt.md). More walkthroughs in progress: connecting an existing agent (Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes) to a GBrain memory layer; setting up GBrain for VC dealflow with founder scorecards and meeting prep; migrating an existing Notion or Obsidian vault; indexing a codebase as a queryable code brain. Full tutorial index: [`docs/tutorials/`](docs/tutorials/). Want to see a tutorial that isn't here yet? [Open an issue](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/issues) describing the workflow you want documented. ## What it does (the loop) ``` signal → search → respond → write → auto-link → sync (every (brain-first (informed (page + (typed edges (cron message) retrieval) by context) timeline) + backlinks) keeps fresh) ``` - **Signal detector**, after you opt in, captures durable ideas and entity mentions from substantive messages. Explicit remembering works without automatic capture; paid enrichment is a separate choice. - **Brain-first lookup** before any external API call. The cheapest, fastest, most personal information source you have. - **Auto-link** extracts graph links for trusted local page writes. No LLM calls; pure pattern matching on page references such as `[[people/alice-example]]`. Unresolved extracted facts keep their provenance without inventing a backing page. - **Cron-driven enrichment** runs while you sleep: dedup people pages, fix citations, score salience, find contradictions, prep tomorrow's tasks. The whole loop is described in [`docs/architecture/topologies.md`](docs/architecture/topologies.md) with diagrams. **Say to your agent:** *"Did upkeep run?"* (your agent's open `gbrain serve` runs the free upkeep while it is idle; `gbrain maintain --schedule` adds a timer for a brain no agent opens) — *"Run dream"* — *"Did the dream cycle run?"* ## Capabilities GBrain combines keyword and semantic retrieval, typed graph traversal, optional cited synthesis, background jobs, and curated agent skills. **Say to your agent:** *"What search mode am I running?"* — *"Who works at acme-example?"* — *"What does my brain know about this project?"* [Capability reference](docs/guides/capabilities.md) keeps the commands, benchmark scope, cost controls, and feature-specific guides. ## Integrations Data flowing into the brain. Each integration is a recipe — markdown + setup hints — that ships in `recipes/` and is discoverable via `gbrain integrations list`. **Say to your agent:** *"Set up voice calls into my brain"* — *"Wire my email and calendar into the brain"* — your agent reads the recipe and walks the setup with you. - **Voice**: Phone calls create brain pages via Twilio + OpenAI Realtime (or DIY STT+LLM+TTS). Setup recipe: [`recipes/twilio-voice-brain.md`](recipes/twilio-voice-brain.md). - **Gmail + Calendar + Contacts (native)**: the google source kind syncs threads, events, and contacts through your own OAuth client and runs the open-loop engine on top (`gbrain waiting`). Setup: [`docs/guides/google-connect.md`](docs/guides/google-connect.md); recipes: [`recipes/email-to-brain.md`](recipes/email-to-brain.md), [`recipes/calendar-to-brain.md`](recipes/calendar-to-brain.md). - **Meeting notes + Slack channels (native)**: the `meetings` source kind (Fireflies first) writes one page per meeting and the `slack` source kind one page per channel per day, synced on a schedule, on brains with or without a Git repository. Setup: [`docs/guides/meeting-and-slack-sources.md`](docs/guides/meeting-and-slack-sources.md). - **Email + calendar (webhooks)**: webhook handlers that route to brain signals. [`docs/integrations/meeting-webhooks.md`](docs/integrations/meeting-webhooks.md). - **Embedding providers**: Voyage (new-install default: `voyage-4` @ 1024d), OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google Gemini, Azure OpenAI, MiniMax, Alibaba DashScope, Zhipu, Ollama (local), llama.cpp llama-server (local), LM Studio, Together, and LiteLLM proxy. Pricing matrix + decision tree in [`docs/integrations/embedding-providers.md`](docs/integrations/embedding-providers.md). Existing vectors are never converted by changing the default; use the explicitly approved [embedding migration](docs/guides/embedding-migration.md). - **Rerankers**: Voyage `rerank-3-lite` hosted (the default unless `search.reranker.model` is set; on in `balanced` and `tokenmax`, same `VOYAGE_API_KEY` as embeddings; `gbrain config set search.reranker.model voyage:rerank-2.5` restores the previous default), plus the `llama-server-reranker` recipe for fully-local cross-encoder rerank via llama.cpp running Qwen3-Reranker against the same `gateway.rerank()` seam. Setup walkthrough in [`docs/ai-providers/llama-server-reranker.md`](docs/ai-providers/llama-server-reranker.md). - **Credential vault + gateway**: `gbrain creds` manages OAuth and API credentials in a local vault ([`recipes/credential-gateway.md`](recipes/credential-gateway.md)); agent-side vault-aware secret distribution: [`docs/integrations/credential-gateway.md`](docs/integrations/credential-gateway.md). - **MCP clients**: every major MCP client is supported. [`docs/mcp/`](docs/mcp/) per-client setup. - **Memorable (procedural memory)**: optional, off by default. Your brain remembers *what* happened; Memorable makes your agent remember *how* — finished sessions become replayable procedures stored on your machine (in a standalone local store, or inside your brain database if you opt in), recalled when a similar task comes back. See the section below, and [`docs/memorable-agents.md`](docs/memorable-agents.md) for the agent-facing detail. ### Memorable — remember how, not just what (optional) Memorable stores replayable procedures from coding sessions. Its relay is off by default and requires an explicit disclosure/consent step; it can send redacted traces and query text off-machine. Read the [Memorable integration guide](docs/memorable-agents.md) for installation, data flow, per-harness limitations, and removal. **Say to your agent:** *"Explain Memorable's data sharing before enabling it."* ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR Repo[Markdown brain repos] --> Sync[Sync and parse] Sync --> Engine{Brain engine} Engine -->|default| PGLite[(PGLite)] Engine -->|shared or large| Postgres[(Postgres and pgvector)] Agent[AI agent or operator] --> Surface[CLI or MCP] Surface --> Ops[Contract-first operations] Ops --> Search[Hybrid retrieval] Ops --> Graph[Typed graph traversal] PGLite --> Search Postgres --> Search PGLite --> Graph Postgres --> Graph Search --> Synthesis[Synthesis and gap analysis] Graph --> Synthesis Synthesis --> Answer[Cited answer] ``` **Two engines, one contract.** PGLite (Postgres 17 via WASM, zero-config, default) for personal brains up to ~50K pages. Postgres + pgvector (Supabase or self-hosted) for shared, large or multi-machine brains. Both implement one `BrainEngine` contract ([`src/core/engine.ts`](src/core/engine.ts)); CLI and MCP share one op registry. **Canonical files preserve file-backed knowledge.** Your brain repo holds the Markdown; the database is an index rebuildable from it, and git deletes become soft-deletes. DB-only pages, unresolved facts, history and operational state need a database backup: [where your memory lives](docs/guides/where-your-memory-lives.md), [system of record](docs/architecture/system-of-record.md). Publish public subsets, share team mounts, or point a thin client at a colleague's brain. Topologies in [`docs/architecture/topologies.md`](docs/architecture/topologies.md). **Two organizational axes (brain ⊥ source).** A *brain* is a database (your personal brain, a team mount you joined). A *source* is a repo inside that brain. Routing uses `.gbrain-source` dotfiles and a 6-tier precedence chain. Diagrams in [`docs/architecture/brains-and-sources.md`](docs/architecture/brains-and-sources.md). **Why the graph matters.** Vector search finds similar text; graph retrieval follows stored relationships. Extracted edges are evidence to inspect, not proof that a relationship is true. Graph freshness depends on the write path and maintenance described in [memory boundaries](docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md#page-writes-and-the-graph-are-separate-outcomes). Deep dive: [retrieval architecture](docs/architecture/RETRIEVAL.md); [entity recall](docs/guides/entity-recall.md). ## Troubleshooting Start with `gbrain doctor`. For database access failures, use `gbrain engine status --probe` and `gbrain db-repair` before changing configuration. **Say to your agent:** *"Check my brain health and show me the repair plan before changing anything."* [Troubleshooting reference](docs/guides/troubleshooting.md) covers installation recovery, PGLite startup, embedding dimensions, locks, import failures, and sync. ## Docs - [`docs/INSTALL.md`](docs/INSTALL.md) — every install path, end to end - [`docs/guides/bootstrap.md`](docs/guides/bootstrap.md) — the persistent-personal-agent bootstrap contract (interview, identity files, hooks, private repo, security posture, uninstall), plus local harness mode (`gbrain bootstrap harness`) for wiring framework-spawned Claude Code/Codex sessions to a running serve - [Anatomy of a page](docs/guides/page-anatomy.md) — frontmatter, timeline, facts; [per-client facts](docs/guides/entity-scoped-facts.md) - [`docs/what-schemas-unlock.md`](docs/what-schemas-unlock.md) — why schemas matter: 7 killer use cases, the structural argument for typed page kinds, the agent-co-curates pattern - [`docs/schema-author-tutorial.md`](docs/schema-author-tutorial.md) — 5-minute walkthrough: fork the bundled pack, add a custom type, backfill existing pages, prove the wiring via `gbrain whoknows` - [`docs/architecture/`](docs/architecture/) — system design, topologies, retrieval theory - [`docs/guides/`](docs/guides/) — how-to runbooks (google connect, open loops, sub-agent routing, minion deployment, skill development, brain-first lookup, idea capture, diligence ingestion) - [`docs/integrations/`](docs/integrations/) — connecting external data sources (voice, email, calendar, embedding providers) - [MCP task guide](docs/mcp/README.md) — deployment and per-client setup (Claude Desktop, Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Cowork) - [MCP administration](docs/mcp/ADMIN.md) — owner dashboard access, client registration, OAuth, permissions, and token recovery - [Evals](docs/eval/) and [research](docs/research/) — methods and results - [`docs/ethos/`](docs/ethos/) — philosophy (thin harness, fat skills, markdown as recipes, origin story) - [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) — entry point for non-Claude agents - [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) — entry point for Claude Code (deep operating context) - [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md) — contributor guide, test discipline, eval-capture mode - [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) — install-path trust model, self-update integrity, automated scanning, OAuth threat model, hardening defaults ## Contributing Run `bun run test` for the fast loop, `bun run verify` for the pre-push gate, `bun run ci:local` to run the full Docker-backed CI stack locally. Detailed test discipline in [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](CONTRIBUTING.md). Community PRs are batched into release waves rather than merged one-by-one — see the community-PR-wave process in [`docs/RELEASING.md`](docs/RELEASING.md). Contributor attribution stays attached via `Co-Authored-By:` trailers. We credit every accepted contribution in [`CHANGELOG.md`](CHANGELOG.md). If you find a bug or want a feature: open an issue first. Quick fixes (typo, doc bug, obvious regression) can go straight to a PR. Anything touching schema, retrieval ranking, MCP protocol, or the security boundary needs a design discussion in the issue first. ## License + credit MIT. I built GBrain to run my OpenClaw and Hermes deployments — the production brain behind my AI agents. Origin story: [`docs/ethos/ORIGIN.md`](docs/ethos/ORIGIN.md). Community PR contributors are credited in `CHANGELOG.md` per release. Attribution for the retired provider's historical embedding and reranker integration remains in Git at `6040075c6cb95be5881cc2e1b76ef7d71f4e5d29`. Voyage AI for the asymmetric-encoding recipe template. Ramp Labs for the search quality improvements lineage.

name: Test

on:
  push:
    branches: [master]
  pull_request:
    branches: [master]
  # Merge queue (inert until the queue is enabled on master): the PR profile,
  # run against the queued merge commit. docs/RELEASING.md#merge-queue.
  merge_group:
  # Nightly full matrix: every Bun version and native target, like a push to master.
  schedule:
    - cron: '23 7 * * *'
  # Manual dispatch lets a local dev/agent offload the suite to GitHub's
  # on-demand runners from ANY branch (see scripts/ship-remote-tests.sh).
  # Frees a load-saturated local machine (e.g. many Conductor agents running
  # their own bun-test suites at once — load avg 120 on 16 cores).
  # Dispatch inputs select manual modes only; they never apply to pull_request,
  # merge_group, push or schedule events (docs/TESTING.md#event-parity).
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      native_only:
        description: Run native platform checks only; this does not satisfy full CI
        type: boolean
        default: false
        required: false
      # Diagnostic modes (docs/TESTING.md#stress-gate, docs/TESTING.md#race-hunt):
      # either one runs only its lane, never the full suite, and its result never
      # opens, updates or closes an issue.
      race_hunt:
        description: Run only the race hunt (every test/postgres-unit-arms.txt file 10 times); diagnostic
        type: boolean
        default: false
        required: false
      stress_files:
        description: Run only the stress gate on these test files (space- or comma-separated test/…/*.test.ts); diagnostic
        type: string
        default: ''
        required: false
      stress_base:
        description: Run only the stress gate on the test files changed versus this ref or SHA; diagnostic
        type: string
        default: ''
        required: false
      stress_head:
        description: Head ref or SHA for stress_base (default HEAD of the dispatched ref)
        type: string
        default: ''
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

# Cancel a superseded run when a newer commit lands on the same PR/branch.
# Keyed on the PR number for pull_request events (unique per PR, so two PRs
# from forks sharing a branch name don't cancel each other) and falls back to
# github.ref for push/scheduled runs. Mirrors heavy-tests.yml; frees runners
# and stops a stale-SHA run from reporting a flaky failure on an obsolete commit.
# Explicit native-only retries use a separate group so full persistence soaks finish.
# Each diagnostic dispatch (race_hunt, stress_*) gets its own group, so one
# replay never cancels another or a full run.
# Event parity (docs/TESTING.md#event-parity): the event suffixes only separate
# runs that must not cancel each other; they change no job, matrix or parameter.
# A push to master is keyed by its commit, so a newer push never cancels it: the Release gate
# (scripts/release-gate.ts) publishes only the release commit's own green runs.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || (github.event_name == 'push' && github.sha) || github.ref }}${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.native_only == true && '-native-only' || '' }}${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && (inputs.race_hunt == true || inputs.stress_files != '' || inputs.stress_base != '') && format('-diagnostic-{0}', github.run_id) || '' }}${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && '-nightly' || '' }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # Trunk Dynamic CI filter (docs/ci-event-parity.md#trunk-dynamic-ci). It asks Trunk
  # which of the gated cheap-tier jobs below this pull-request push needs and writes
  # one output per gated job key; each gated job runs unless its output is exactly
  # 'false'. It fails open: a missing token, a Trunk outage or a job with no verdict
  # runs the job.
  # Event parity (docs/ci-event-parity.md#trunk-dynamic-ci): pull_request only. On a
  # push, merge-queue entry, schedule or dispatch (the full-ci run) this job is
  # skipped, every output is empty, and every gated job runs as before.
  # In Trunk's Learning mode it records verdicts and skips nothing; enforcement is the
  # Mode setting on Trunk's Dynamic CI settings page, not this file.
  # scripts/check-dynamic-ci.ts guards the wiring.
  dynamic-ci:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-2-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      security-regressions: ${{ steps.dynamic-ci.outputs.security-regressions }}
      native-locks: ${{ steps.dynamic-ci.outputs.native-locks }}
      persistence-validation: ${{ steps.dynamic-ci.outputs.persistence-validation }}
      stress-changed-tests: ${{ steps.dynamic-ci.outputs.stress-changed-tests }}
      enumeration-census-tests: ${{ steps.dynamic-ci.outputs.enumeration-census-tests }}
    steps:
      - id: dynamic-ci
        uses: trunk-io/dynamic-ci@5bcddbf3615c2b032c21eed1b514c91164bda4a8  # v1 (v0.1.7)
        continue-on-error: true
        timeout-minutes: 3
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN }}
          job-keys: security-regressions,native-locks,persistence-validation,stress-changed-tests,enumeration-census-tests
          enable-annotation: 'true'

  # Planning gate for the native platform matrix. Pull requests that touch
  # native, lock, IPC, publication, backup, export or sync paths run every
  # native target on the primary Bun version; other pull requests run the Linux
  # x64 smoke cell. Pushes, schedules and manual runs always run the full matrix.
  # Named exception (docs/TESTING.md#event-parity): the native-locks scope
  # reduction on pull requests and merge-queue runs (cross-target cells) is
  # covered by every push to master and the nightly Test schedule,
  # which both run scope=full.
  changes:
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-2-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      actions: read
    outputs:
      native-scope: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.native }}
      convergence: ${{ steps.convergence.outputs.convergence }}
      census: ${{ steps.census.outputs.census }}
      reuse: ${{ steps.reuse.outputs.reuse }}
      reuse-source-run-id: ${{ steps.reuse.outputs.source_run_id }}
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            scripts/ci-native-scope.sh
            scripts/ci-manifest-diff.sh
            scripts/ci-convergence-scope.sh
            scripts/select-e2e.ts
            scripts/ci-reuse.ts
            scripts/lib/gh-issue.ts
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            scripts/ci-native-scope.sh
            scripts/ci-manifest-diff.sh
            scripts/ci-convergence-scope.sh
            scripts/select-e2e.ts
            scripts/ci-reuse.ts
            scripts/lib/gh-issue.ts
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false
      - if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4
      # Master-push reuse (P2, scripts/ci-reuse.ts): a push whose tree equals the
      # tree of a passed full-suite run skips every full lane and records the
      # reused run. Any doubt, a crash included, leaves reuse unset: a full run.
      - id: reuse
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: bun scripts/ci-reuse.ts --workflow test --sha "$GITHUB_SHA" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --output "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" --summary "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" --record "$RUNNER_TEMP/reuse.json"
      - if: steps.reuse.outputs.reuse == 'true'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: reused-full-suite
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/reuse.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 90
      - id: scope
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CHANGED_FILES: ${{ github.event.pull_request.changed_files }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$EVENT" = merge_group ]; then
            # PR profile for the queue: every native target on the primary Bun.
            scope=primary
          elif [ "$EVENT" != pull_request ]; then
            scope=full
          elif ! [[ "$CHANGED_FILES" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] || [ "$CHANGED_FILES" -ge 3000 ]; then
            # The PR files API returns at most 3000 files. An unknown or
            # capped diff cannot establish that native paths are untouched.
            scope=primary
          elif files=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files?per_page=100" --jq '.[].filename'); then
            listed=$(printf '%s\n' "$files" | awk 'NF { count++ } END { print count+0 }')
            if [ "$listed" -ne "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
              scope=primary
            else
              # A version-only package.json / openclaw.plugin.json diff (every
              # release PR) cannot change native behavior (C11).
              kept=$(printf '%s\n' "$files" | bash scripts/ci-manifest-diff.sh drop-version-only) || kept=$files
              if [ -z "$kept" ]; then
                scope=smoke
              else
                scope=$(printf '%s' "$kept" | bash scripts/ci-native-scope.sh) || scope=primary
              fi
            fi
          else
            scope=primary
          fi
          echo "native scope: $scope"
          echo "native=$scope" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # Named exception (docs/TESTING.md#event-parity): a pull request runs the
      # managed-sync convergence gate only when scripts/ci-convergence-scope.sh
      # selects its diff (persistence, sync, projections, storage, the harness
      # and its workflow; never package.json alone). Merge-queue runs, every push
      # to master and the nightly Test schedule always run it; an unknown or
      # unreadable diff runs it too.
      - id: convergence
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CHANGED_FILES: ${{ github.event.pull_request.changed_files }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          convergence=run
          if [ "$EVENT" = pull_request ] && [[ "$CHANGED_FILES" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] && [ "$CHANGED_FILES" -lt 3000 ] \
            && files=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files?per_page=100" --jq '.[].filename') \
            && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$files" | awk 'NF { count++ } END { print count+0 }')" -eq "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
            convergence=$(printf '%s' "$files" | bash scripts/ci-convergence-scope.sh) || convergence=run
          fi
          echo "convergence gate: $convergence"
          echo "convergence=$convergence" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # A pull request runs enumeration-census-tests unless every changed file is
      # a doc (scripts/select-e2e.ts --classify-only says DOC_ONLY); an unknown or
      # unreadable diff runs it.
      - id: census
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CHANGED_FILES: ${{ github.event.pull_request.changed_files }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          census=run
          if [[ "$CHANGED_FILES" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] && [ "$CHANGED_FILES" -lt 3000 ] \
            && files=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files?per_page=100" --jq '.[].filename') \
            && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$files" | awk 'NF { count++ } END { print count+0 }')" -eq "$CHANGED_FILES" ] \
            && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$files" | bun scripts/select-e2e.ts --classify-only --changed-files -)" = DOC_ONLY ]; then
            census=skip
          fi
          echo "enumeration and census tests: $census"
          echo "census=$census" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # Re-run checks for every event, except a master push reusing a passed full-suite run of its exact tree (scripts/ci-reuse.ts). Only dependencies and PGLite snapshots are cached.
  gitleaks:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || (inputs.native_only != true && inputs.race_hunt != true && !inputs.stress_files && !inputs.stress_base) }}
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-2-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 6
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 6
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      # Use the open-source gitleaks CLI, not gitleaks-action@v2: the v2 action
      # now enforces a paid GITLEAKS_LICENSE (fails the job with "missing
      # gitleaks license" for accounts it can't validate). The CLI is free, uses
      # the committed .gitleaks.toml allowlist, and scans the same commit range.
      - name: Cache gitleaks tarball
        uses: actions/cache@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: /tmp/gitleaks-dl
          key: gitleaks-8.30.1-linux-x64
      - name: Install gitleaks (pinned + checksum-verified)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          VER=8.30.1
          BASE="gitleaks_${VER}_linux_x64.tar.gz"
          URL="https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v${VER}"
          mkdir -p /tmp/gitleaks-dl
          [ -f "/tmp/gitleaks-dl/${BASE}" ] || curl -fsSL -o "/tmp/gitleaks-dl/${BASE}" "${URL}/${BASE}"
          # Checksums fetched fresh EVERY run: a cache-restored tarball is
          # re-verified against the published digest, never trusted.
          curl -fsSL -o /tmp/gitleaks_checksums.txt "${URL}/gitleaks_${VER}_checksums.txt"
          ( cd /tmp/gitleaks-dl && grep " ${BASE}\$" /tmp/gitleaks_checksums.txt | sha256sum -c - )
          tar -xzf "/tmp/gitleaks-dl/${BASE}" -C /tmp gitleaks
          install /tmp/gitleaks /usr/local/bin/gitleaks
          gitleaks version
      - name: Verify scanner detects secrets outside exact fixture exceptions
        run: bash scripts/test-gitleaks-config.sh
      # Event parity (docs/TESTING.md#event-parity): every event scans the commit
      # range it introduces.
      - name: Scan for secrets (gitleaks CLI, .gitleaks.toml)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            RANGE="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}..${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}"
          elif [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "merge_group" ]; then
            RANGE="${{ github.event.merge_group.base_sha }}..${{ github.event.merge_group.head_sha }}"
          else
            BEFORE="${{ github.event.before }}"
            case "$BEFORE" in
              ""|0000000000000000000000000000000000000000) RANGE="${{ github.sha }}~1..${{ github.sha }}" ;;
              *) RANGE="${BEFORE}..${{ github.sha }}" ;;
            esac
          fi
          echo "Scanning commit range: $RANGE"
          gitleaks detect --redact --no-banner --log-opts "$RANGE"

  # Gated by dynamic-ci (docs/ci-event-parity.md#trunk-dynamic-ci): runs unless Trunk's verdict is 'false'.
  security-regressions:
    needs: [dynamic-ci]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.dynamic-ci.outputs.security-regressions != 'false' && (github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || (inputs.native_only != true && inputs.race_hunt != true && !inputs.stress_files && !inputs.stress_base)) }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest' && 'ubicloud-standard-2-ubuntu-2404' || matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-26, windows-latest]
        bun: ['1.4.4']
        # Event parity: every event, pull requests and merge-queue runs
        # included, runs every supported Bun version on every OS
        # (docs/TESTING.md#event-parity).
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6  # v2
        with:
          bun-version: ${{ matrix.bun }}
      - name: Install dependencies (bounded, retried once)
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: bun scripts/ci-bun-install.ts --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
      - name: Boundary and transport regressions
        run: bun test --timeout 60000 test/frontmatter-security.test.ts test/data-frontmatter.test.ts test/authorization-boundaries.test.ts test/url-safety.test.ts test/guarded-http.test.ts test/bundle-files-segments.test.ts
      - name: Isolated TLS and proxy regressions
        run: bun test --timeout 60000 test/guarded-http-tls.serial.test.ts
      - name: Colon-slug Windows refusals and bound explicit reads (#5032, #5081)
        run: bun test --timeout 60000 test/colon-slug-windows-5032.test.ts test/cross-lane-5081-5032.test.ts
      - name: Windows durability, skill bundles and local-writer flags (#5595, #5475)
        run: bun test --timeout 60000 test/fs-durable.test.ts test/persistence-windows-flush-5595.test.ts test/bundle-files-windows-5475.test.ts test/init-packaged-skills-native.test.ts test/auth-local-writer-dry-run.test.ts test/scripts/durable-flush-guard.test.ts test/binary-self-update-durable-download.test.ts
      # test/persistence-administration.test.ts is not on this row yet: on
      # windows-latest Bun 1.4.2 segfaults ("Segmentation fault at address
      # 0x42") in its private-IPC test right after the native lock probe; the
      # crash is Bun's, tracked in #6462, and the #5332 bound it exercised is
      # covered by the forced probe inside postgres-disconnect-bounded.
      # Upstream: oven-sh/bun#40023 ("Windows: dispatch libuv events from the
      # event loop, not from inside libuv callbacks") is the fix for the
      # class: on Windows a socket or pipe closed during a nested tick is
      # freed while the outer libuv dispatch still holds it. Re-try the file
      # on this row once a Bun release carries that change.
      - name: Teardown bounds that used to park the Windows unit run (#5332)
        run: bun test --timeout 120000 test/postgres-disconnect-bounded.test.ts
      # Every earlier step runs under PowerShell 7, so Windows PowerShell 5.1, which the backup's owner-only protection
      # launches, is still cold here: on #7409 its first starts outlasted the warm-up's 30 s and the protection's 15 s
      # bounds. The cold path itself is covered by test/backup-powershell-warmup.serial.test.ts.
      - name: Start Windows PowerShell once before the backup steps
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        timeout-minutes: 3
        run: powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command "exit 0"
      - name: Backup archive round trip on this host (#5312)
        run: bun test --timeout 60000 test/backup-archive-roundtrip-5312.test.ts
      # The stale-socket sweep's native AF_UNIX reparse-point path exists only on Windows; macOS runs the POSIX cases
      # here (#6573: the fixture root is under /private/tmp, so the data-dir socket stays under gbrain's 103-byte limit
      # instead of moving to the shortened fallback path); Linux runs them in the unit shards.
      - name: Stale AF_UNIX socket sweep (native tag check on Windows, POSIX cases on macOS) (#5312, #6573)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows' || runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: bun test --timeout 60000 test/backup-stale-socket-5312.test.ts
      - name: Hidden console windows from detached processes (#4992)
        run: bun test --timeout 300000 test/windows-hidden-console.test.ts test/spawn-windows-hide.test.ts test/scripts/windows-hide-guard.test.ts
      # A PGLite data dir too deep for afunix's 108-byte sun_path binds its sockets in the per-user run dir instead,
      # under a non-ASCII profile path, with a 20-cycle bind/close stability probe (Bun Windows IPC crash class, #6462).
      - name: Long Windows PGLite IPC paths use the per-user run dir (#6573)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: bun test --timeout 120000 test/windows-ipc-long-path-6573.serial.test.ts

  # bun audit blocks on pushes, schedules, manual runs, and pull requests or
  # merge-queue entries that change bun.lock, admin/bun.lock, patches/ or a
  # package.json dependency field (or carry the `dependency-audit` label).
  # Elsewhere a new upstream advisory is a warning, so it cannot turn every
  # open PR red at once; the push and nightly runs still fail on it (B11).
  # Named exception with its rule (docs/ci-event-parity.md#dependency-audit-rule): a
  # push-to-master red from a newly published advisory opens the Test master-red
  # issue and a scheduled red the nightly-red issue; the repair PR bumps,
  # overrides, patches or removes the dependency; when no fix exists, an
  # expiring ignore entry needs Garry's approval.
  dependency-audit:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || (inputs.native_only != true && inputs.race_hunt != true && !inputs.stress_files && !inputs.stress_base) }}
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-2-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
      - id: scope
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CHANGED_FILES: ${{ github.event.pull_request.changed_files }}
          LABELS: ${{ toJSON(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name) }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.merge_group.base_sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.event.merge_group.head_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$EVENT" != pull_request ] && [ "$EVENT" != merge_group ]; then
            printf 'blocking=true\nreason=%s runs always block\n' "$EVENT" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif printf '%s' "$LABELS" | grep -q '"dependency-audit"'; then
            printf 'blocking=true\nreason=the dependency-audit label is set\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            files=''
            if [ "$EVENT" = pull_request ]; then
              if [[ "$CHANGED_FILES" =~ ^[0-9]{1,4}$ ]] && [ "$CHANGED_FILES" -lt 3000 ] \
                && listed=$(gh api --paginate "repos/$REPO/pulls/$PR/files?per_page=100" --jq '.[].filename') \
                && [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$listed" | awk 'NF { n++ } END { print n+0 }')" -eq "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
                files=$listed
              fi
            elif listed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/compare/$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" --jq 'if (.files | length) >= 300 then error("capped") else .files[].filename end'); then
              files=$listed
            fi
            # An unknown or capped diff stays empty, which classifies as blocking.
            printf '%s' "$files" | bash scripts/ci-manifest-diff.sh dependency-scope >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          cat "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6  # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4
      - name: Install dependencies (bounded, retried once)
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: bun scripts/ci-bun-install.ts --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
      - name: Install dependencies (bounded, retried once)
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: bun ../scripts/ci-bun-install.ts --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
        working-directory: admin
      - name: bun audit (root + admin)
        env:
          BLOCKING: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.blocking }}
          REASON: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.reason }}
        run: bash scripts/ci-dependency-audit.sh

  verify:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || (inputs.native_only != true && inputs.race_hunt != true && !inputs.stress_files && !inputs.stress_base) }}
    # Pre-test gates: privacy/jsonb/source-id/etc + admin-build (tsc runs in the typecheck job).
    # Lives in its own runner so the matrix shards aren't carrying ~2-3min
    # of verify work in addition to their test files (the old shape stuffed
    # this into `test (1)` via `if: matrix.shard == 1`, which made shard 1
    # the slowest matrix worker). scripts/run-verify-parallel.sh fans out
    # the 20 checks via & + wait (~5s vs ~15-25s sequential).
    # 8 vCPUs: measured 51s vs 48s on 16 and 58s on 4.
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-8-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 12
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6  # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4
      # This job is the ONE designated saver of the bun cache (the others
      # restore-only, so 5 redundant post-job save attempts disappear).
      # admin/bun.lock is in the key because verify's check:admin-build
      # installs from it.
      - uses: actions/cache@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'admin/bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-
      # verify's runner sources test-env.sh and builds the snapshot for its
      # PGLite-booting eval checks — restore the cache so it's the ~40ms
      # freshness check, not a cold build ahead of all ~47 checks.
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: |
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.tar
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.version
          key: pglite-snapshot-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('src/core/**/*.ts', 'test/helpers/legacy-embedding-config.ts', 'scripts/build-pglite-snapshot.ts') }}
      - name: Install dependencies (bounded, retried once)
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: bun scripts/ci-bun-install.ts --frozen-lockfile
      # check:schema-migration-order compares new schema migrations with
      # origin/master's latest version; a depth-1 fetch of the ref is enough.
      - run: git fetch --no-tags --depth=1 origin +refs/heads/master:refs/remotes/origin/master
      # check:vendor-postgres rebuilds vendor/postgres from two pinned downloads (npm, GitHub). They are kept by content
      # hash, so a transient outage cannot turn verify red; every file is hash-checked on use, so a mismatch still fails.
      - uses: actions/cache@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/gbrain-vendor
          key: gbrain-vendor-${{ hashFiles('vendor/update-postgres.sh') }}
      # Receipts (X2): verify records every check's real outcome (pass, fail,
      # timeout, self-skip) as one JUnit testcase; logs stay on failure.
      # The typecheck job below runs tsc, so verify skips its own copy here.
      - run: bun run verify
        env:
          GBRAIN_VERIFY_SKIP_TYPECHECK: '1'
          GBRAIN_TEST_RECEIPT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/receipts
          GBRAIN_VERIFY_LOG_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/verify-logs
      - name: Upload verify logs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: verify-logs
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/verify-logs
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          overwrite: true
      # Guard: no bare `bun test` in workflows/scripts — bun ignores
      # bunfig.toml's timeout, and hooks (beforeAll/afterAll) get the 5s
      # default regardless of per-test third-arg timeouts. Runs directly
      # (not via verify's CHECKS array) to avoid a package.json edit.
      - run: bash scripts/check-bun-test-timeout.sh
      # #5810: every tracked *.sh must parse under bash 3.2 (macOS /bin/bash).
      # The real parser runs in the digest-pinned bash:3.2 image; REQUIRE
      # turns a missing Docker into a failure instead of a skip, and makes the
      # test's real-parser fixture cases mandatory.
      - name: Shell scripts parse under bash 3.2
        env:
          GBRAIN_TEST_BASH32_REQUIRE: '1'
          GBRAIN_TEST_RECEIPT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/receipts
        run: |
          bun run check:bash32
          bash scripts/run-with-receipt.sh verify-tests bash32 -- bun test --timeout 60000 test/scripts/check-bash32.test.ts
      # recipes/agent-voice's vitest unit suite (109 tests) ran in no workflow;
      # pinned vitest + ws into a temp prefix, ~10s.
      - name: agent-voice recipe unit tests (vitest)
        run: bun run test:agent-voice
      - name: Upload receipts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: receipts-verify
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/receipts
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: warn
          overwrite: true

  typecheck:
    if: ${{ github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || (inputs.native_only != true && inputs.race_hunt != true && !inputs.stress_files && !inputs.stress_base) }}
    # tsc runs here, in parallel with verify, instead of inside verify's pool
    # with its 120 s per-check cap. A change to a widely imported type (any new
    # error code in src/core/error-registry.ts) makes the incremental check
    # almost cold. On master c8354664 (run 39140170894), the cold check took
    # 121 s in verify's pool and timed out at the cap. A timed-out tsc also
    # writes no tsbuildinfo, so every rerun restored the same stale state.
    # Step timeout from measurement: 3 x the worst cold CI time (121 s) is
    # about 6 minutes per attempt. tsc is single-threaded, so 4 vCPUs (16 GB)
    # do the work of verify's 8. A cold tsc of the tree peaks at about 6.5 GB
    # RSS (6.51 GB on gbrain#9184's head, 2026-11-11), close to the heap cap
    # in package.json's typecheck script; an incremental run seeded from a
    # distant head's tsbuildinfo goes past it and aborts (exit 134).
    # scripts/ci-typecheck.sh then runs it once more from cold, so the step
    # and job allow two attempts.
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-4-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 21
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6  # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'admin/bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Install dependencies (bounded, retried once)
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: bun scripts/ci-bun-install.ts --frozen-lockfile
      # #6056: `bun run typecheck` is incremental against this tsbuildinfo, so
      # a restored one from an earlier run lets tsc recheck only what changed.
      # Rolling key: every run saves under its own SHA and the next run
      # restores the newest one for the same bun.lock + tsconfig.json
      # (a dependency or compiler-option change starts cold). After
      # `bun install`, which (re)creates node_modules.
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: node_modules/.cache/gbrain-typecheck.tsbuildinfo
          key: tsbuildinfo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'tsconfig.json') }}-${{ github.sha }}
          restore-keys: |
            tsbuildinfo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'tsconfig.json') }}-
      - name: Typecheck (tsc, incremental; cold once more on an abort)
        id: tsc
        timeout-minutes: 12
        run: bash scripts/ci-typecheck.sh bun run typecheck
      # Saved even when this check finds type errors, and whatever the other
      # jobs do: tsc writes its state on an error too, so the next master run
      # starts from this commit instead of an older, colder state. Not saved
      # when tsc's last attempt aborted or timed out, or the step never
      # reported (cancelled): tsc wrote no state, and saving the restored file
      # under this head's key would make every rerun restore it again.
      - name: Save the typecheck state
        if: always() && steps.tsc.outputs.state_written == 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: node_modules/.cache/gbrain-typecheck.tsbuildinfo
          key: tsbuildinfo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'tsconfig.json') }}-${{ github.sha }}

  # Enumeration and census tests: the unit files that fail when a change adds an
  # operation, command, flag, error code, doctor check, caller or route without its
  # reviewed entry, or changes a golden (scripts/ci-census-tests.sh prints them; the
  # crew runs the same command by hand). No aggregate, merge rule or reuse check
  # reads it. Two shards of about 175 s of mined weight each on 2 vCPUs, like one
  # of the two unit shards a 4-vCPU test runner packs.
  # Event parity (docs/ci-event-parity.md#enumeration-and-census-tests): pull
  # requests only, and not on a doc-only diff. Every full run (the full-ci
  # dispatch, every push to master, the nightly schedule) runs these files in the
  # unit shards.
  enumeration-census-tests:
    name: enumeration and census tests (${{ matrix.shard }}/2)
    needs: [changes, dynamic-ci]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.dynamic-ci.outputs.enumeration-census-tests != 'false' && needs.changes.result == 'success' && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.changes.outputs.census != 'skip') }}
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-2-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2]
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6  # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: |
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.tar
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.version
          key: pglite-snapshot-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('src/core/**/*.ts', 'test/helpers/legacy-embedding-config.ts', 'scripts/build-pglite-snapshot.ts') }}
      - name: Install dependencies (bounded, retried once)
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: bun scripts/ci-bun-install.ts --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Run shard ${{ matrix.shard }} of 2
        timeout-minutes: 10
        run: bash scripts/ci-census-tests.sh --run ${{ matrix.shard }} 2

  # Event parity (docs/ci-event-parity.md#full-ci-on-pull-requests): full profile only. A
  # pull request runs the cheap tier; this job runs in the full-ci dispatch on its
  # head before merge (merge-train requires full-suite), on every push to master
  # and on the nightly schedule.
  serial-tests:
    needs: [changes]
    if: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.reuse != 'true' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || (inputs.native_only != true && inputs.race_hunt != true && !inputs.stress_files && !inputs.stress_base))) }}
    # *.serial.test.ts — one bun process per file (module-registry isolation),
    # POOLED across files by scripts/run-serial-tests.sh (was strictly
    # sequential: an 8.5-minute job whose serialization the quarantine
    # contract never required). Lives in its own runner so the matrix shards
    # aren't carrying the serial tail.
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4]
    # The pool is min(cpus, 4) processes: 8 vCPUs measured 222s for shard 2,
    # the same as 16 (224s); 4 vCPUs took 277s. 4 vCPUs (C8): the shards
    # finish in 2-3 minutes, far off the critical path, so the extra ~55s
    # costs nothing while halving the lane's vCPU-minutes.
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-4-ubuntu-2404
    # Keep the existing timeout headroom for memory-constrained runners,
    # bounded rescue attempts, and the machine-exclusive tail on shard 1.
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6  # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-
      # PGLite schema snapshot (~42MB): the runner builds it when absent or
      # stale (its runtime hash is authoritative — a stale restore is rebuilt,
      # never trusted). Cached so the build is paid once per schema change,
      # not once per job per run. This job SAVES; verify + matrix + slow jobs
      # restore-only. The key is an approximation on purpose: it only has to
      # be a superset-trigger of real schema changes.
      # HASH INPUTS HAVE 14 HOMES: 12 legacy keys (five here, six in
      # e2e.yml, one in stress.yml) plus two default-profile keys here
      # (slow-brainbench and brainbench). Edit all together when schema dependencies change;
      # profile names stay distinct, and the serial save reuses its restore key.
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        id: snapshot-cache
        with:
          path: |
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.tar
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.version
          key: pglite-snapshot-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('src/core/**/*.ts', 'test/helpers/legacy-embedding-config.ts', 'scripts/build-pglite-snapshot.ts') }}
      - name: Install dependencies (bounded, retried once)
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: bun scripts/ci-bun-install.ts --frozen-lockfile
      - run: bun run test:serial
        env:
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}/4
          COVERAGE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/coverage
          GBRAIN_TEST_RECEIPT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/receipts
      - name: Upload receipts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: receipts-serial-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/receipts
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: warn
          overwrite: true
      - name: Upload coverage (serial lane)
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02  # v4
        with:
          name: coverage-serial-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/coverage
          retention-days: 14
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          overwrite: true
      - name: Save legacy snapshot (single writer)
        if: success() && matrix.shard == 1
        uses: actions/cache/save@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684 # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: |
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.tar
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.version
          key: ${{ steps.snapshot-cache.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - name: Upload serial timings
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: timings-serial-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: |
            .context/serial-timings.json
            .context/serial-durations.txt
          include-hidden-files: true
          retention-days: 14
          overwrite: true

  # Event parity (docs/ci-event-parity.md#full-ci-on-pull-requests): full profile only. A
  # pull request runs the cheap tier; this job runs in the full-ci dispatch on its
  # head before merge (merge-train requires full-suite), on every push to master
  # and on the nightly schedule.
  slow-brainbench-e2e:
    needs: [changes]
    if: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.reuse != 'true' && (github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || (inputs.native_only != true && inputs.race_hunt != true && !inputs.stress_files && !inputs.stress_base))) }}
    # Dedicated runner for the BrainBench CLI e2e file. At 98s mined it was
    # the matrix's single heaviest atom (10% of the whole corpus weight) and
    # the hard floor on shard-count scaling; a Phase-2 rewrite (spawn batching
    # + deleting the CI-gate-duplicated full-corpus test) cut it to ~72s
    # local, still far past the ~40s keep-in-matrix bar.
    runs-on: ubicloud-standard-4-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 12
    steps:
      - id: checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
      - name: Check out again after a stalled first attempt
        if: steps.checkout.outcome == 'failure'
        uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262  # v4
        timeout-minutes: 3
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6  # v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.4.4
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: bun-cache-${{ runner.os }}-
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684  # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: |
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.tar
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot.version
          key: pglite-snapshot-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('src/core/**/*.ts', 'test/helpers/legacy-embedding-config.ts', 'scripts/build-pglite-snapshot.ts') }}
      - uses: actions/cache/restore@5a3ec84eff668545956fd18022155c47e93e2684 # v4.2.3
        with:
          path: |
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot-default.tar
            test/fixtures/pglite-snapshot-default.version
          key: pglite-snapshot-default-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('src/core/**/*.ts', 'test/helpers/legacy-embedding-config.ts', 'scripts/build-pglite-snapshot.ts') }}
      - name: Install dependencies (bounded, retried once)
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: bun scripts/ci-bun-install.ts --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Ensure PGLite snapshot (build-or-validate, non-fatal)
