[English](README.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [＋ 你的语言](https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Ai18n)
# MisakaNet mcp-name: io.github.Ikalus1988/misakanet > **The same failure, paid for twice.** > > A `pip install` times out behind a corporate proxy. An agent finds the fix. Days later the same > timeout appears on another machine, under another model — and is debugged from scratch, because the > fix was never written down anywhere the next agent looks. > > MisakaNet is that place: a git-backed **failure memory**. Every lesson is a Markdown file in this > repository — graded by evidence, reviewed like code, retrieved by an agent instead of guessed at. > You fail once; the next agent does not. Agent-native interfaces: [MCP server](https://misakanet.org/mcp) (8 tools), WebMCP, `llms.txt`, A2A discovery via `.well-known/agent-card.json`. The **local** stdio server (`pip install misakanet`) ships **11** — the hosted endpoint is a subset; [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md) has both rows.

Core   

Install   

Ecosystem   

--- ## Install (30 seconds) The point of an install is a first **successful search**, not the install. None of these needs an account or a token. | Your host | Command | |---|---| | **DeepSeek Harness** | `dsh plugin --profile web add misakanet` — or type `misakanet` in **Add plugin** | | **Claude Code** | `/plugin marketplace add Ikalus1988/MisakaNet` then `/plugin install misakanet@misakanet` | | **Cindy** | install the **MisakaNet** plugin (id `misakanet`) from Cindy's plugin list | | Installer-managed | Claude Code · Codex · Hermes · OpenClaw · codewhale · Cursor · Gemini CLI · Copilot CLI · OpenCode · Kiro · MiniMax Code · DeepSeek Harness · Cindy | | **Any other MCP client** | point it at `https://misakanet.org/mcp` — public endpoint, anonymous reads | | **Your own code** | `pip install misakanet-core` (library) · `pip install misakanet` (stdio server) | The installer-managed row is what `npx @misaka-net/misakanet-setup` writes into each host's config. For DeepSeek Harness that is the **rules half only** (`$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`): its tools come from the plugin in the row above, which the installer prints as the one manual step. Updates: `dsh plugin --profile web update misakanet@latest`. Installer updates: `npx @misaka-net/misakanet-setup@latest`. Full prerequisites and the two-package trap: [How to use it](#how-to-use-it). ## Your first five minutes **1. Ask it something you have actually broken.** No client installed? This `curl` is the whole interface: ```bash curl -sS https://misakanet.org/mcp \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json' \ -H 'MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-06-18' -H 'Origin: https://misakanet.org' \ -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call", "params":{"name":"misakanet_search","arguments":{"query":"database is locked","top":3}}}' ``` **2. Read what came back.** A hit returns the lesson, its `evidence_level`, and its path — open the file and read the fix before running any command in it. A miss returns `no_match` plus a ready-to-call intake: the corpus saying it does not know this one yet. **3. Check the trust signal, not the tone.** `E0`–`E3` say how far a lesson was verified; `E4` is the one nobody can write or vote into. ## What is MisakaNet? **Git-backed failure memory for AI coding agents.** An error shows up → the agent searches → it applies a fix somebody already verified → if nothing matches, the miss becomes an intake, and the intake becomes a lesson for the next agent. Every lesson is a Markdown file: reviewed like code, graded by evidence, retrieved with BM25 over the Python standard library. The hosted MCP endpoint adds an **optional semantic fallback** (bge-m3 + Vectorize) only when BM25 returns no match; `MISAKANET_SEMANTIC=0` disables it. No vector database is required locally, and no server unless you want one. | | | |---|---| | **Lessons** | failure-recovery knowledge base, open and auditable under `lessons/` | | **Domains** | rag · devops · fanuc · docker · feishu · mcp · network · ci · wsl · windows … | | **Evidence** | E0 intake → E1 reviewed → E2 reproduced → E3 CI verified → **E4 observed reuse by two or more distinct clients** | | It is not | It is | |---|---| | ❌ a general memory system | ✅ a failure-recovery knowledge layer | | ❌ an agent runtime | ✅ a searchable lesson database | | ❌ a mandatory vector database / RAG stack | ✅ BM25 first; optional, disable-able semantic fallback on the hosted endpoint | | ❌ a skill marketplace | ✅ debugging knowledge from real sessions | | ❌ a general-purpose benchmark platform | ✅ a corpus graded by evidence; a 267-query retrieval run is published, and the older recitation benchmark is paused | ### What it answers — and what it does not ![Four-panel comic: an agent asks about a failure, gets an indexed lesson back, or gets "no_match" and a ready-to-call intake form](promotional/misakanet-scope-comic.webp) MisakaNet answers for the failures it has indexed, and only those. When nothing matches the reply is `no_match` plus a ready-to-call `intake` — the corpus saying "not this one yet", not a dead end. ### Lesson vs Skill A **skill** teaches an agent how to do something; a **lesson** records what went wrong before and how not to fail again. MisakaNet is only the second thing. → [FAQ](FAQ.md) ## Where it is today - **The numbers that move are badges**, on purpose: the Lessons badge renders `data/badges/lessons.json`, regenerated by `update-badges.yml`, so it can lag a run but is never a hand-typed total. - **The top of the evidence ladder is observed, not declared.** `E4` needs an observation — two distinct clients actually retrieving a lesson — so no lesson file can carry it: the corpus declares none ([declared distribution](docs/trust-semantics.md), regenerated and checked by CI), and the number that exists is the worker's daily reading of `search_signals`, published in the [heartbeat](https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet/issues/3471). - **Search is BM25 first; the hosted endpoint can fall back to embeddings.** Local/offline remains stdlib BM25; the fallback runs only when BM25 returns no match, and `MISAKANET_SEMANTIC=0` turns it off. A corpus gap is still a miss: the reply is `no_match` plus an intake, not an empty page. - **Reported gaps arrive faster than they are triaged.** The intake queue is the honest bottleneck. - **The corpus is downloadable and citable.** `data.misakanet.org` publishes a versioned bundle — the full corpus, the benchmark query set, and every run artifact — with a per-file SHA-256 and an explicit license per file ([DATASET.md](DATASET.md)). The counts live in each version's `manifest.json`, not in prose. ## Retrieval benchmark: 267 queries, BM25 vs semantic fallback On 2026-10-27 the hosted endpoint's retrieval path was evaluated on **267 queries, one per lesson** generated by Workers AI 70B. Both arms used the same eval worker and corpus; only `MISAKANET_SEMANTIC` changed. | arm | R@1 | R@5 | no_match | |---|---|---|---| | BM25 | 0.210 | 0.225 | 0.712 | | semantic fallback | **0.446** | **0.472** | **0.453** | The fallback improves R@1 by **23.6 points** and cuts `no_match` by **25.9 points**. It does **not** meet the R@1 half of the target (`0.446 < 0.46`); `no_match` is within the target (`0.453 ≤ 0.50`). A 113-query subset reaches 0.460/0.460, while 250 reaches 0.404/0.504: the sample is large enough to show the fallback works, not large enough to call R@1 solved. This is 267 queries from the 300-entry pool, not the full 650; 33 pool entries yielded no query, 2 semantic requests errored, and the eval corpus was not refreshed. → [full report](docs/benchmarks/retrieval-l1-267-2026-10-27.md) ### What changed since: the gate, not the model The table above measures a configuration production no longer uses. Until 2026-10-28 the semantic path ran **only when BM25 returned nothing**, so a confident-but-wrong lexical hit suppressed it — 13 of the 20 recorded misses were exactly that. For queries containing CJK characters the two ranked lists are now **fused** (reciprocal-rank) instead of one gating the other. Measured on the live endpoint, 64 Chinese queries, 0 transport failures: | bucket | n | before | after | |---|---|---|---| | zh → zh | 31 | 0.710 | **0.774** | | **zh → en** | 33 | 0.455 | **0.697** | | zh → en, low overlap | 14 | 0.214 | **0.500** | For scale: `bge-m3` pure cosine already reached 0.636 on the cross-lingual bucket, and a `gemini` embedding 0.727 — so most of the gap was the decision to consult the vector path, not the model. English queries are untouched (the fuse is gated on CJK characters) and sit at 15/20 against a floor of 16, which is where they were before this change. → [full report](docs/benchmarks/cjk-fusion-2026-10-28.md) ## Recitation benchmark: what it measured, and why it is paused One narrow question: **when you hand a model a lesson, how much of that lesson comes back?** The metric is `lesson_hit_rate` — the share of the injected lesson's commands reproduced in the answer. Read the setup before the number: the scenario in this benchmark is each lesson's own title, the injected lesson is *that same lesson*, no retrieval call is made, and correctness is not checked. It measures the **recitation** half of RAG: necessary for MisakaNet to help, and **not evidence that search finds anything**. The run is **paused**. Two independent runs of ≈500 scenarios each on 2026-09-22: **46.1%** with the lesson pasted in, **23.3%** without. What remains is the last snapshot plus its dated record — [`docs/benchmarks/latest.json`](docs/benchmarks/latest.json). The table below is generated by [`scripts/update_readme_benchmark.py`](scripts/update_readme_benchmark.py); do not hand-edit it. | Date | with_lesson hit rate | plain hit rate | n | |---|---|---|---| | 2026-08-30 | 46.4% | 23.9% | 358 | | 2026-08-31 | 49.1% | 25.1% | 398 | | 2026-09-06 | 48.3% | 24.1% | 455 | | 2026-09-14 | 46.6% | 23.4% | 494 | | 2026-09-21 | 46.1% | 23.3% | 512 | | 2026-10-12 | 43.8% | 26.1% | 34 | _1155 run(s) in `latest.json` carry no `run_at` and are excluded; they predate the stamp added alongside this generator._ ``` with_lesson hit rate (per run date) 43.8% │ ▁ 46.1% │ ▄ 46.6% │ ▄ 48.3% │ ▆ 49.1% │ █ └────────────────── 08 09 09 09 10 31 06 14 21 12 ``` Per-run files: [`docs/benchmarks/`](docs/benchmarks/) · metric definition: `METRIC_DEFINITION` in [`scripts/benchmark_workers_ai.py`](scripts/benchmark_workers_ai.py). ## Take part **1. Report a failure the corpus does not have.** Search first, then call `misakanet_submit_intake` — no account, no email, no token, a five-line report is enough. It becomes a tracked issue. **2. Reuse a lesson and leave the trace.** A "this helped" vote is recorded as an `E3` hint, not as proof. The proof is quieter: your retrieval is counted, anonymously, as one more distinct client. **3. Translate this page.** The README ships in three languages; a fourth is one merged PR away — the open [i18n tasks](https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3Ai18n) carry the exact acceptance criteria. **What you get back: attribution.** A lesson cites the intake that produced it (`source:`, `provenance.issue:`), and the pipeline can emit a receipt naming the lesson and its evidence level. Nothing here is a bounty: this repository pays nothing and promises nothing. Some issues carry third-party reward banners added by our own automation; we do not administer them — see [Contributing](#contributing). ## How to use it `npx @misaka-net/misakanet-setup` installs MisakaNet into your assistant's own config — the same command for every client. The ten supported clients, and what each one gets, are in [the install page](https://misakanet.org/install/). Verify an install with `npx @misaka-net/misakanet-setup --verify`; undo it with `--uninstall`. Reads are anonymous and unlimited; registration is for writing ([why](AGENTS.md#33-注册与配额)). Node ≥ 18 for the installer, Python ≥ 3.11 for the library and stdio server. Python 3.10 reached end-of-life on 2026-10-01, so this release needs 3.11 or newer — upgrade the interpreter before upgrading the package. ### Other channels - **Claude Code, as a plugin** — `/plugin marketplace add Ikalus1988/MisakaNet`, then `/plugin install misakanet@misakanet`: the hosted MCP tools, no installer, no local process. - **DeepSeek Harness** — `dsh plugin --profile web add misakanet`: `mcp__misakanet__*` tools plus the session panel. The rules half (the "search before you act" block) is written by the installer into `$DSH_HOME/AGENTS.md`; dsh has no plugin extension point for it, so the two halves stay separate. - **Call the endpoint yourself** — the `curl` in [Your first five minutes](#your-first-five-minutes). - **The library in your own code** — `pip install misakanet-core`. ### The two-package trap (it cost a real install failure, #1849) - `@misaka-net/misakanet-setup` (npm) is the **installer** — it has a `bin`, no plugin entry. Use it to teach your assistant to search. - `misakanet` (npm) is the **DSH / Codex plugin** — `dsh plugin --profile web add misakanet`. - This repository (git) is also a **Claude Code plugin marketplace** — `/plugin marketplace add Ikalus1988/MisakaNet`. - `misakanet` (PyPI) is the stdio **MCP server** — `python3 -m misakanet.server`. - `misakanet-core` (PyPI) is the **library** (stdlib-only BM25; the hosted endpoint's semantic fallback is server-side) — `from misakanet.search import search_lessons`. ### Use it as a GitHub Action When a workflow fails, the action searches the lessons and comments the closest match on the pull request (optionally reporting the new error). Published on [GitHub Marketplace](https://github.com/marketplace/actions/misakanet-intake-bot). ```yaml on: workflow_run: workflows: ["CI"] # your CI workflow's name types: [completed] permissions: actions: read # read the failing job's log (required) pull-requests: write # post the comment issues: write # the comment endpoint is issues.createComment jobs: intake: if: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'failure' }} runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: Ikalus1988/MisakaNet@v1 with: mode: suggest-only # or suggest-and-intake, to report new errors too source: ${{ github.repository }} ``` → [inputs and outputs](docs/agents/external-usage.md) ## Documentation | Topic | Where | |---|---| | Install, verify, uninstall | [docs/quickstart.md](docs/quickstart.md) · | | MCP: protocol, tools, transports | [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md) · [API.md](API.md) | | CLI | [docs/cli-reference.md](docs/cli-reference.md) · `python3 search_knowledge.py "…"` | | Architecture | [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) · [docs/CONCEPTS.md](docs/CONCEPTS.md) | | Contributing a fix | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [label system](docs/label-system.md) | | Submitting an intake | [docs/mcp-intake-guide.md](docs/mcp-intake-guide.md) · [mcp-remote](docs/integrations/mcp-remote.md) | | Troubleshooting | [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md) | | Known limitations | [docs/LIMITATIONS.md](docs/LIMITATIONS.md) | | Benchmarks | [docs/benchmarks/](docs/benchmarks/) | | Dataset (corpus + query sets, downloadable) | [DATASET.md](DATASET.md) · | | Roadmap / changelog | [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) · [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | | Competitors, domains, crawler policy | [competitive](docs/competitive-analysis.md) · [domains](docs/domains/) · [robots](docs/cloudflare-robots-txt.md) | ## Contributing > **Zero bounty. Maximum rigor. Merge earns credit.** "Zero bounty" is a statement about *this repository*: MisakaNet pays nothing and promises nothing. It is not a statement about the issue you are looking at. Some issues carry an **Opire** banner advertising a third-party reward, added automatically by our own [`scripts/question_autopilot.py`](scripts/question_autopilot.py) — we do not administer those payouts, and Opire is not mentioned in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. **Verify any reward offer independently** before you plan work around it. The only thing this repository has ever honoured is a merged PR. ([#2903](https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet/issues/2903)) 1. Check the checkout: `python3 scripts/misakanet_cli.py smoke` 2. Search before writing: `python3 search_knowledge.py "your error here"` 3. Found nothing? [Share your failure lesson](https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet/issues/new?template=lesson-feedback.yml) — five lines is enough **This month's good first issue (Oct 26 – Nov 26):** [Bring one real failure](https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet/issues/3901) — no code; the MCP intake needs no account; we help with the format. → [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [good first issues](https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22) · [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) ## Security ⚠️ **Sandbox your agent before executing retrieved commands.** Lessons are community-contributed — review before running. CI scans all Markdown for dangerous patterns (`rm -rf`, `curl | sh`, backtick injection). See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and [LIMITATIONS.md](docs/LIMITATIONS.md). ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Where | |---|---| | DCO · leaked token · pip timeout · `database locked` · Windows/GBK · WSL permission · FANUC codes | [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md) | | MCP returns 403/405, or a client shows no tools | [docs/mcp.md](docs/mcp.md) · [FAQ.md](FAQ.md) | | Behind a corporate proxy | [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md#behind-a-corporate-proxy) | ## For Agents & Crawlers **Prefer MCP intake for missing or stale lessons; PRs are optional.** Search first; if nothing matches, call `misakanet_submit_intake` at `https://misakanet.org/mcp` — no account, no token. Never send secrets or raw private logs. Protocol: [docs/mcp-intake-guide.md](docs/mcp-intake-guide.md). ## Contributors *Built by the network, for the network. Zero bounties paid — only merge approval and eternal network gratitude.* ⚡ ## License [Apache-2.0](LICENSE) — Copyright 2026 Ikalus1988. Lessons are contributed under the same license, and every commit carries a DCO `Signed-off-by` (see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)).

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "misakanet"
version = "3.15.0"
description = "AI Agent 分布式经验知识共享系统 — 踩坑一次，全网受益"
readme = "README.md"
license = "Apache-2.0"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "misakanet-core>=2.7.0",
]
keywords = ["ai-agent", "knowledge-base", "bm25", "rag", "distributed"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet"
Repository = "https://github.com/Ikalus1988/MisakaNet"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
include = ["misakanet*"]

[project.scripts]
# Remote-first CLI, in the package, zero dependencies (2026-09-18, #1821). It replaced
# `misakanet = "search_knowledge:main"`, whose module is not in the wheel, so the command exited with
# `ModuleNotFoundError` right after a pip install — the defect this entry point's own docstring names.
# There is no `misaka-harvest`: that tool needs a repo checkout and is intentionally not shipped.
misakanet = "misakanet.cli.search:main"

# `misaka-harvest` is deliberately not declared (2026-09-18, #1821).
#
# The old declarations pointed at modules outside the wheel — `packages.find` ships `misakanet*` only —
# so `pip install misakanet` installed two commands that exit with `ModuleNotFoundError`. A declared
# entry point that cannot run is worse than none: it is a broken instruction the user has no way to
# diagnose, and the README printed it as a Quick Start.
#
# The working entries after an install are the package modules: `python -m misakanet.server` (stdio
# MCP, gated in CI by .github/workflows/pypi-wheel-smoke.yml) and `python -m misakanet` (help).
#
# Remember before re-adding one: an installed CLI cannot search today — `misakanet/search/engine.py`
# reads `lessons/` relative to a repo checkout and there is no remote path in the package, so the
# corpus question (ship it, or search misakanet.org/mcp) has to be answered first.

[project.optional-dependencies]
# NOTE (2026-09-05): chromadb was removed from hub extras — this repo has no
# chromadb imports (external hub package owns its own deps), and every
# published chromadb (<=1.5.9, the latest) is affected by 4 unfixed GHSAs
# (pre-auth code injection x2 critical, tenant/RBAC authz bypass x2 high).
# Re-add ONLY if the hub code returns to this repo and upstream ships a fix.
hub = [
    "aiohttp>=3.9",
    "websocket-client>=1.6",
    "networkx>=3.2",
    "PyYAML>=6.0",
    "numpy>=1.24",
    "keyring>=25",
]
feishu = ["requests>=2.28"]
semantic = [
    "sentence-transformers>=2.2",
    # filelock 4.2.1 fixes the ReadWriteLock advisories. It requires Python >= 3.11, so while this
    # project still declared a 3.10 floor the 3.10 branch had to take the last release *before* the
    # vulnerable 3.20.4 — a version that cannot receive the fix at all. The floor is 3.11 now, so the
    # fix is installable everywhere and is required rather than merely "whatever is newest".
    "filelock>=4.2.1",
]
harvest = [
    "scrapling>=0.4.9",
    "scrapling[fetchers]",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"
# `archive/` is where dead code is kept, and one file there (`archive/dead/scripts/_fix.py`) does not
# even parse — deliberately, as a recorded broken state. Excluding it here rather than inside the gate
# means a contributor running `ruff check .` inspects the same 436 maintained files the gate does.
extend-exclude = ["archive"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "N", "W", "UP"]

[tool.ruff.format]
quote-style = "double"

[tool.coverage.run]
# `scripts/` is deliberately outside the measured set — **accepted technical debt**, not an
# oversight. The scripts layer is long-tail maintenance code (54,527 LOC of non-test Python in
# total; `scripts/` is the bulk of it) and testing it to the `misakanet/` standard is a separate
# investment decision, not something to fake by passing `--cov=scripts` to a run that then omits
# the package. The CI command is `--cov=misakanet` only, and the debt is recorded here and in
# `docs/ci-gates.md`.
#
# Keep this `omit` even though the flag is gone: it is the belt to the command's braces, and it
# covers both depths because `*` in a coverage pattern crosses `/`.
omit = ["scripts/*"]

[tool.mypy]
python_version = "3.11"
warn_return_any = true
warn_unused_configs = true
disallow_untyped_defs = false
ignore_missing_imports = true

[[tool.mypy.overrides]]
module = "misakanet.*"
disallow_untyped_defs = true

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "hypothesis>=6.165.10",
    "pytest>=9.1.1",
]

[tool.uv]
# The constraints that pinned filelock for the 3.10 branch are gone with the 3.10 floor: the
# advisory fix (filelock 4.2.1) needs Python >= 3.11, so on 3.10 the only installable version was
# the last one *before* the vulnerable 3.20.4 — a version that could never receive the fix.
# `semantic` now requires the fixed version outright.

repository.readme:
## A benchmark for LLM trading agents, with news replayed by the minute it was published Most news backtests join headlines to prices by calendar date, so a headline published after the close is traded at that close. Here every headline arrives at the minute it was published and orders fill at the next open, through three frozen markets: the 2020 crash, the 2022 bear market and 2026. Llama, GPT, Claude and Gemini trade them blind and with names, three seeds each, scored apart before and after each model's training cutoff. **The same package is also a set of AI trading agents for US stocks that check the macro calendar, the fear index and verified news before they buy.** Market regimes from VIX and the FOMC / CPI calendar · dip buying with an earnings check · a 30% cash floor · cross-verified news · paper-trading agents ranked against SPY · news backtests that cannot see the future · a public leaderboard of LLM trading agents · frozen 2020, 2022 and 2026 markets for research · LLM agents over MCP · paper and live trading on 10 brokers. [🌐 Website](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/) · [🏆 LLM leaderboard](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/leaderboard.html) · [中文说明 → README_zh.md](README_zh.md) · [🚀 Quick start](#-quick-start) · [🆕 What's new](#-whats-new) · [🔬 Research kit](#-research-kit) · [🔗 MCP](#-mcp-server) · [📸 Screenshots](#-screenshots) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) [![CI](https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![PyPI 0.7.2](https://img.shields.io/badge/pypi-0.7.2-e5534b.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/risk-aware-trading-agents/) [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-3776ab.svg)](https://www.python.org/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2ea043.svg)](LICENSE) [![MCP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-server-24292f.svg)](#-mcp-server) [![Docker image](https://img.shields.io/badge/docker-ghcr.io-2496ed.svg)](https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents/pkgs/container/risk-aware-trading-agents) [![Dataset on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/dataset-Hugging%20Face-ffcc4d.svg)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/jacksonwangpro1/point-in-time-market-data-2026) [![English and Chinese](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-English%20%7C%20%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87-e3b341.svg)](README_zh.md) Screens from the dashboard and from riskaware research run on the bundled 2026 data. A backtest shows what a strategy would have done, not what it will do.
## 🚀 Quick start ```bash pip install "risk-aware-trading-agents[dashboard,mcp]" # Python 3.10+ riskaware dashboard # the web UI on http://localhost:8501, English and 中文 ``` Then, in another terminal: ```bash riskaware init # 2-minute wizard: language, risk profile, broker, watchlist riskaware regime # market regime, VIX, fear & greed, next FOMC / CPI / jobs report riskaware scan # today's signals, each with its reasons riskaware analyze NVDA # what every agent thinks about one stock riskaware news AAPL # cross-verified headlines riskaware backtest --compare buy_and_hold,ema_bounce riskaware run # one paper-trading cycle (built-in paper account) riskaware agents init # four starter paper-trading agents riskaware agents run # let them trade once now riskaware agents schedule --install # ...and every trading day from now on riskaware research run -s swing_trend # a strategy on the frozen 2026 market, with a look-ahead check riskaware research run -s swing_trend --period 2022 # the same in the 2022 bear market ``` No account or API key is needed for any of these. Add `--lang zh` to any command for Chinese output. For the newest code before it is released, use `pip install "risk-aware-trading-agents[dashboard,mcp] @ git+https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents"`; to change the code, clone the repository and run `pip install -e ".[dashboard,mcp]"`. **Docker**, for x86-64 and ARM: ```bash docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 ghcr.io/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents dashboard # http://localhost:8501 docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents mcp # MCP server over stdio ``` For the daily paper-trading scheduler as well, put `riskaware.yaml` (from `riskaware init`) and, if you use broker keys, `.env` in the repository root, then run `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d` (or `make docker`). **Nothing to install:** [![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents) opens the repository in your browser with every extra installed. Run `riskaware dashboard` there and port 8501 opens by itself. ## Is it for you? - You trade **US stocks over days to weeks** and want rules you can read: buy quality names on pullbacks, keep cash, and never sell in a panic. - You want **backtests that cannot cheat**: news replayed as it was published, orders at the next open, and a look-ahead check on every research run. - You **study LLM trading agents** and need data and a setup that others can repeat: three frozen markets (the 2020 crash, the 2022 bear market, 2026), a blind mode, a saved record of every run, and a [public leaderboard](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/leaderboard.html) you can submit to. - You use **Claude, Codex or Gemini** and want them to test a strategy you describe in words, on your own plan, with no API key. - You want to **paper trade first**: several strategies side by side on simulated money, ranked against SPY every trading day. - You read **English or Chinese**: the CLI, the dashboard, the reports and the docs come in both. --- ## 💡 The idea Most trading bots either chase every signal or need a quant team to configure. This one follows a simple, explainable discipline that long-term investors already use: buy quality stocks when they pull back to their moving averages, add when fear is high and the earnings still hold up, trim when prices run too far, never panic-sell into uncertainty, and always keep a cash reserve. Four agents check the market, the calendar, the company and the news; a deterministic risk manager has the final word on every order. **How it did.** On 2026 so far, reading the news that ships with the package, the agent made **+15.9%** against SPY's +12.1%, with a Sharpe ratio of 1.70 against 0.77, and its worst drop was **-5.3%** against SPY's -8.9% ([details](#2026-so-far-with-news)). From 2018 to 2026 it earned less than SPY in the long bull market, 10.4% a year against 14.1%, and fell about half as far, -18.2% against -33.7% ([details](#-backtest)). > Not financial advice. It starts in paper mode, and live trading needs three explicit switches. ## Four ways to use it | | **Dashboard** | **Command line** | **AI assistants (MCP)** | **Python** | |---|---|---|---|---| | Start with | `riskaware dashboard` | `riskaware scan` | `riskaware mcp-setup claude-desktop --apply` | `from riskaware.research import run_experiment` | | What you do | watch the regime, the signals, the agents and the backtests, in English or 中文 | scan, backtest, paper trade, and schedule the agents | describe a strategy in words; Claude, Codex or Gemini write it, test it and explain the result | run experiments on the frozen 2020, 2022 and 2026 markets and keep a record for a paper | | Needs | the `dashboard` extra | nothing else | the `mcp` extra; runs on your plan, no API key | nothing else | ```python from riskaware.research import Experiment, run_experiment r = run_experiment(Experiment(strategy="swing_trend", news=True, split="2026-07-01")) print(r.summary()["metrics"], r.leak, r.folder) ``` --- ## ✨ Feature tour The highlights. The guides in [docs/](docs/) cover every command and setting, and the [website](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/) has longer answers on news backtesting, point-in-time data and LLM agents. ### 🧠 How it works - **Macro-aware market regimes.** VIX and its term structure (VIX/VIX3M), sector breadth, credit appetite (HYG vs IEF), safe-haven demand, a fear-and-greed gauge computed from free data (and CNN's Fear & Greed for reference), and the **FOMC, CPI, jobs report, PPI, GDP and PCE** calendar put the market in one of four regimes: risk-on, neutral, uncertain, risk-off. - **Buy low, sell high.** Pullbacks to **EMA 50 / 100 / 200**, RSI(2) and z-score mean reversion, **quality dips that must pass an earnings check** (revenue growth, margins, free cash flow, leverage, EPS beats), breakouts and trend continuation in strong markets. Take-profit trims when a stock runs far above EMA50; trend exits after a break of a falling EMA50. - **No panic selling.** When the regime is uncertain or risk-off the agent holds, does not sell, and only buys at strong support. Only a disaster the company itself confirms (bankruptcy, delisting, restatement in its own 8-K or press release) or an optional hard stop can force an exit. - **Risk first.** A **30% cash + T-bill floor**, position, sector and speculative ("lottery ticket") caps, volatility-scaled sizes, buying in tranches, a Treasury sleeve for conservative profiles, idle cash parked in a T-bill ETF, a drawdown pause, a kill switch. - **Optional LLM review, per agent.** A bull analyst, a bear analyst and a risk judge (GPT, Claude, any OpenAI-compatible model such as DeepSeek or Qwen, or a free local model through Ollama) can nudge conviction by at most ±0.15 or veto a buy. They can never create a trade or change a limit. News reaches them only as quoted, untrusted text, and every prompt and reply is kept in the local journal so you can see how each decision was made. ```mermaid flowchart TB D["Prices · VIX · sectors · FOMC / CPI / NFP calendar · earnings · Finviz + RSS + SEC"] M["Macro agent
regime + fear/greed"] E["Event agent
FOMC, CPI, jobs"] T["Technical agent
EMA 50/100/200,
mean reversion, trend"] F["Fundamental agent
earnings quality"] N["News agent
cross-verified"] S["Strategy: built-in or yours"] L["Optional LLM
bull / bear / judge"] R["Risk manager: cash floor · caps · tranches · regime rules"] D --> M & E & T & F & N M & E & T & F & N --> S L -.->|"±0.15 at most"| S S --> R R --> G["Safety guards"] --> B["Paper or live broker"] R --> X["Backtester"] ``` #### What the agent does in each regime | Regime | Typical trigger | Buys | Sells | Size | |---|---|---|---|---| | 🟢 **Risk-on** | SPY above a rising EMA50 and EMA200, VIX < 20, most sectors above EMA200 | pullbacks, breakouts, dips | take profit, trend exits | 100% | | ⚪ **Neutral** | none of the others | EMA support, mean reversion, quality dips | take profit | 75% | | 🟡 **Uncertain** | 2 days before an FOMC decision, the day before CPI or the jobs report, VIX 20–30, fear gauge < 35, downtrend | EMA100 / EMA200 support only | **none: hold** | 50% | | 🔴 **Risk-off** | VIX ≥ 30, VIX backwardation below EMA200, credit stress | quality dips and broad ETFs, small tranches | **none: hold** | 35% | Emergency exits (a severe red flag the company itself confirms in its 8-K or its own press release, or the profile's hard stop) work in every regime. #### Risk profiles | | Conservative | Balanced | Aggressive | |---|---|---|---| | Cash + T-bill floor | 30% | 30% | 30% | | Treasury sleeve (IEF) | 15% | 5% | 0% | | Max single stock / sector | 5% / 20% | 7% / 25% | 10% / 35% | | Speculative sleeve (high-volatility names) | 0% | 3% (2 names) | 7% (3 names) | | Minimum conviction | 0.65 | 0.58 | 0.52 | | Earnings score needed for a dip buy | 70 | 60 | 50 | | Take-profit trigger | +20% | +25% | +30% | | Breakout entries | off | off | on | Every limit can be overridden in `riskaware.yaml`. Positions are built in tranches (50% / 25% / 25% of the target); a later tranche needs a deeper support touch or a winning position, and trimmed positions can be rebuilt on the next pullback. ### 📰 Cross-verified news - **Sources.** Finviz (free), Google News, Nasdaq, Seeking Alpha and Yahoo RSS, plus the company's own **SEC 8-K filings**. - **Confirmed means two sources.** A story only counts toward the company it names, and it is confirmed when two independent outlets, the company's own press release or its SEC filing carry it. A red flag on a confirmed story blocks new buys. - **Hard to fool.** Only the company's 8-K, or its own release confirming what independent outlets reported first, can force a sale, so a fake headline, a fake press release and the outlets that repeat it, or another company's bad news cannot. A denial clears the story it refutes instead of confirming it. The same check runs in backtests, on news replayed as it was published: see [News in backtests](#news-in-backtests). ### 🤖 Paper-trading agents An agent is a strategy with its own paper account. Pick a strategy (built-in or your own file), a risk profile, a stock list and the starting cash, and the agent trades that account once every trading day on free Yahoo Finance prices. Run several side by side and see which one beats SPY. Agents only ever use the built-in paper account, never a broker. ```bash riskaware agents init # steady, momentum, breakout, fear-buyer riskaware agents add dips --strategy rsi2 --universe tech --cash 25000 riskaware agents add mine --strategy my_dip.py:MyDip --profile aggressive riskaware agents add luna --strategy risk_aware --llm openai:gpt-5.6-luna # with an LLM review board riskaware agents add local --strategy risk_aware --llm ollama:qwen2.5:3b # a free local model riskaware agents run # trade every active agent now riskaware agents why luna # how it decided: setups, risk check, bull / bear / judge riskaware agents # the leaderboard riskaware agents schedule --install # every trading day, by itself ``` The daily job (a LaunchAgent on macOS, a crontab line on Linux, a scheduled task on Windows) wakes every 15 minutes on weekdays and trades each agent once per trading day after 15:40 New York time, before the close. It skips holidays, catches up after the laptop sleeps, and keeps going when one agent fails. Each agent keeps its account, journal and daily equity in `~/.riskaware/arena/NAME/`. The **Agents** page of the dashboard shows the leaderboard and lets you create, run, pause, reset and delete agents; its **Decisions** tab shows how each decision was made, including the LLM's bull case, bear case and verdict and the exact prompt it was sent. GPT needs `OPENAI_API_KEY` in your `.env`; a local model needs [Ollama](https://ollama.com) (`ollama pull qwen2.5:3b`); and `--llm claude-cli`, `codex-cli` or `gemini-cli` uses your Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini plan through its command-line tool, with no API key. More in [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md). ### 🔗 MCP server `riskaware mcp` serves the agents over the Model Context Protocol, so Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor or any MCP client can use them, on your plan and without an API key. `riskaware mcp-setup` prints (or, with `--apply`, runs) the one step that connects it: ```bash pip install risk-aware-trading-agents # the MCP server is part of the base install since 0.7.2 riskaware mcp-setup claude-desktop --apply # or: claude-code, codex (your ChatGPT login), gemini, antigravity ``` Other ways in: in Claude Desktop, download `risk-aware-trading-agents-.mcpb` from the [latest release](https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents/releases/latest) and open it. A client that starts servers by command can use `uvx risk-aware-trading-agents mcp` (nothing to install first) or `docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents mcp`. The server is listed on the official MCP Registry as `io.github.jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents`. Twenty-one tools: `market_regime`, `scan`, `analyze_stock`, `stock_news`, `list_strategies`, `backtest`, `strategy_guide`, `backtest_code`, `agents_leaderboard`, `agent_detail`, `agent_decisions`, `agents_create` and `agents_run`, and for research `research_guide`, `market_day`, `run_experiment`, `list_experiments`, `experiment_report`, `trading_session_start`, `trading_session_step` and `trading_session_status`. They are read-only or act on local paper accounts; no tool can send an order to a broker. Then just ask, for example "What regime is the market in, and what is coming up this week?" or "Backtest the wheel on megacap with $1M since 2018." ChatGPT itself only connects to remote servers, so on the OpenAI side use Codex, which runs on your ChatGPT login. More in [docs/agents.md](docs/agents.md#use-it-from-claude-chatgpt-or-gemini-mcp). ### 🧪 Strategy lab Describe a strategy in plain words and let the AI build it. Over MCP, Claude, Codex or Gemini read `strategy_guide`, write the strategy as a Python class and run it with `backtest_code`. Before the code runs, the lab refuses dates and stock tickers written into it (both let a backtest know the future), files, network and private attributes. Then it backtests the code in a separate process with no API keys and a time limit, and returns the metrics next to SPY and buy-and-hold, or the lines to fix. > Write a strategy that buys two-day pullbacks in uptrends when the recent news is positive, and sells after 10 days or at +8%. Backtest it on the tech list for 2026 with news. `save_as` keeps a strategy that works: it then shows up on the dashboard and can run as a paper agent. For code from anywhere else, `riskaware lab my_strategy.py --preset tech` does the same checks and backtest. More in [docs/strategy-lab.md](docs/strategy-lab.md). ### 🏆 LLM trading agent leaderboard [**rta-bench-1**](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/leaderboard.html) ranks LLMs as trading agents on the same game: the 56 large caps, after every fifth close, through 2026 to date, the 2022 bear market and the 2020 crash, each played blind and with real names, on news replayed by the minute it was published and with realistic fill costs. A model's training cutoff decides which scores count: periods after the cutoff are ranked, periods it may remember are listed apart. For each model the board shows how it made its money (market and style exposure against stock picking, sectors, holding periods, trades set off by news) and a memory score, next to the five rule strategies, SPY and the equal-weight list. An entry is one JSON file with the model's replies, so anyone can replay it without calling the model; to add a model, run `riskaware research submit` and open a pull request. More in [docs/leaderboard.md](docs/leaderboard.md). ### 🔬 Research kit Three very different years ship with the package, frozen, for experiments that anyone can repeat: **2026** to date (a rising market), **2022** (the rate-hike bear market: SPY -18.2%) and **2020** (the COVID crash: SPY -34% in 23 days, then a new high). Each has daily prices for the 64 stocks and 25 ETFs from two years before it, the VIX term structure, that year's headlines, and every indicator and regime reading the agents use, each as it was known at that day's close. | Period | Test window | News for the 64 stocks | |---|---|---| | `2026` (default) | 2026-01-02 to 2026-11-11 | 16,945 Benzinga headlines and SEC 8-K filings | | `2022` | the whole year | 29,300 Benzinga headlines | | `2020` | the whole year | 19,618 Benzinga headlines | They are cut from a local archive of about 3.2 million Benzinga headlines from 2011 to 2026 (about 202,000 in 2020, 270,000 in 2022 and 250,000 in 2026), enough to backtest agents that read the news and to look for news factors. The 2026 files are also on [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/jacksonwangpro1/point-in-time-market-data-2026), as Parquet with a data viewer and the original files. ```bash riskaware research day 2026-04-08 --symbols NVDA,TSLA # everything known at that close riskaware research run --strategy swing_trend --split 2026-07-01 riskaware research run --strategy swing_trend --period 2022 # the bear market riskaware research trade --llm ollama:qwen2.5:3b --universe core --blind --period 2020 ``` - **Point in time.** Signals at the close, orders at the next open: swing trading on daily bars. A headline counts only after it was published, and indicators only look back. - **A look-ahead check on every run.** The run is repeated with every price and headline after three cut days replaced by random ones, and the decisions before each cut must not change. For an LLM it replays the model's replies and checks that what the model was shown before each cut did not change, so the model is not asked twice. - **A record for papers.** Each run saves its data hashes, code, settings, metrics, bootstrap intervals, trades and every decision. - **Made for LLMs.** Over MCP, describe a strategy and Claude writes and tests it (`run_experiment`), looks at any day (`market_day`), or trades a period step by step (`trading_session_start`), blind if you like: no tickers, company names or dates. Five common swing strategies on the 56 megacaps, at most 10 equal positions; return without news / with news: | Strategy | 2026 (to Nov 11) | 2022 | 2020 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Trend following (EMA20 / EMA50 cross) | **+21.1%** / +19.6% | -6.0% / -5.0% | +36.6% / **+68.4%** | | Post-news drift (without news: the same trade on a price jump) | +15.7% / +4.4% | -13.3% / -14.1% | +9.4% / +28.4% | | Connors RSI(2) | +12.7% / +10.8% | -2.2% / -5.7% | +14.0% / +12.7% | | Pullback in an uptrend | +2.3% / +1.7% | **-4.7% / -4.0%** | +2.3% / +3.3% | | 20-day breakout | -0.3% / -3.5% | -12.8% / -13.7% | +33.1% / +30.4% | | SPY buy and hold | +12.1% | -18.6% | +17.2% | | Equal weight, the same 56 stocks | +11.4% | -12.4% | +40.1% | No rule wins every year. Trend following led in the two rising years; in 2022 every strategy lost money, all of them less than SPY, and the pullback rule lost least. The news filter cut returns in 2026 and seemed to help in 2020, but the 2020 gain is one position: with news, a free slot let trend following buy Tesla in April 2020 and hold it to the end of the year. The equal-weight row shows the survivorship bias of today's large caps, largest in 2020. Every interval overlaps, and every run passed the look-ahead check. Definitions, the full tables with 95% intervals, and advice for papers in [docs/research.md](docs/research.md). ### 📊 Backtest Built-in strategy, balanced profile, the 55-stock `megacap` list, $100k, signals at the close and fills the next day, 5 bps slippage, January 2018 to November 2026: | | risk_aware | SPY buy & hold | |---|---|---| | CAGR | 10.4% | 14.1% | | Volatility | 9.3% | 19.0% | | Sharpe | 0.84 | 0.66 | | Max drawdown | -18.2% | -33.7% | | Worst calendar year | -3.7% | -18.2% | | Average stocks / cash + T-bills | 57% / 39% | 100% / 0% | Read it honestly: in a long bull market the agent earns less than the index because it keeps at least 30% in cash, and it loses roughly half as much when markets fall. The list is today's large caps, so it carries survivorship bias; these numbers use neither news nor fundamentals (2026 with news is below), and past results do not predict future ones. Reproduce it with `riskaware backtest --compare buy_and_hold`. ```bash riskaware backtest --strategy risk_aware --compare buy_and_hold,ema_bounce,rsi2 --start 2018-01-01 --open riskaware backtest --preset etf --profile conservative riskaware backtest --symbols AAPL,MSFT,NVDA,COST --cash 25000 riskaware backtest --synthetic # offline demo, no download ``` Every run writes a self-contained HTML report (metrics, equity and drawdown charts with regime shading, monthly returns, every trade with its reason) plus CSV files. #### 2026 so far, with news The same agent and settings on 2026, from January 2 to November 11, now reading the news that ships with the package: 15,542 Benzinga headlines and 605 SEC filings for these 56 stocks, each day only what was out before its close. | January 2 – November 11, 2026 | risk_aware + news | risk_aware, no news | SPY buy & hold | |---|---|---|---| | Return | **+15.9%** | +15.4% | +12.1% | | Volatility | 8.2% | 7.8% | 14.0% | | Sharpe | 1.70 | 1.73 | 0.77 | | Max drawdown | **-5.3%** | -5.3% | -8.9% | | Average stocks / cash + T-bills | 60% / 35% | 61% / 34% | 100% / 0% | The agent beat SPY by 3.8 points while holding stocks with 60% of its money on average, and its worst drop was 60% of SPY's: in the March sell-off it fell 5.3% while SPY fell 8.9%. News added half a point of return this year. Ten months is a short test, so the 2018–2026 table above is still the better guide. Reproduce it with `riskaware backtest --preset megacap --start 2026-01-02 --end 2026-11-11 --news`. #### News in backtests A backtest may only use news it would have seen on that day, so it needs each item's publication time. News for 2020, 2022 and 2026 ships with the package for the 64 stocks of the built-in lists: 19,618, 29,300 and 16,945 items (Benzinga headlines, titles only; for 2026 also SEC 8-K filings, January 1 to November 11). For other years, `riskaware news-history` keeps an archive on your own machine (`~/.riskaware/news`, never in the repository). `--news` replays both through the same clustering and two-source check used in live trading. Each day sees only items published before its close (16:00 New York, 13:00 on early-close days), and orders fill the next day. ```bash riskaware backtest --strategy examples/strategies/news_earnings_drift.py --preset megacap --start 2026-01-02 --news # 2026: nothing to download riskaware news-history build --preset core --contact-email you@example.com # SEC 8-K filings since 2018 riskaware news-history build --symbols AAPL,NVDA --source benzinga # with your own BENZINGA_API_KEY riskaware news-history import my_news.csv --tz America/New_York # timestamp, symbol, headline[, source, url, sentiment] riskaware news-history status riskaware news-history show NVDA --date 2024-05-22 # what the backtest saw at that close riskaware backtest --strategy examples/strategies/news_earnings_drift.py --preset core --news --compare buy_and_hold ``` | Source | What goes into the archive | Cost | |---|---|---| | Bundled with the package | 2020, 2022 and 2026 Benzinga headlines (titles only), and 2026 SEC 8-K filings, for the 64 stocks of the built-in lists | free, already installed | | SEC EDGAR | every 8-K (earnings, officer changes, deals, impairments, restatements) with SEC's acceptance time | free; SEC asks for a contact email | | Benzinga | headlines from your own news API key | your Benzinga plan | | CSV | any news you have the right to use | — | The `core` preset is SPY, QQQ, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL, META and TSLA. SPY and QQQ are funds, not companies, so the SEC archive has little or nothing for them; the FOMC, CPI and jobs calendar already drives the regime in every backtest. Benzinga counts as one publisher, so a Benzinga-only story stays single-source until an SEC filing or a second publisher backs it. What you download or import stays on your machine. Details: [docs/news-history.md](docs/news-history.md). **More history.** We keep a much larger archive, about 3.2 million Benzinga headlines from 2011 to 2026 (about 200,000 to 300,000 a year). It is far too big to ship in the package, so the package carries 2020, 2022 and 2026 for the built-in lists. If you need more years or more stocks, open an issue and we will look at how to provide them, for example as a separate download. ### 📚 Strategy library Every built-in strategy runs through the same risk manager, so all of them keep the cash floor. Backtest any of them with `riskaware backtest --strategy NAME`; compare several with `--compare a,b,c`. | Strategy | Type | Idea | |---|---|---| | `risk_aware` | stocks (default) | the multi-agent strategy described above | | `momentum_rotation` | stocks | each month hold the strongest names by 6-month relative strength, above EMA200 | | `donchian_breakout` | stocks | Turtle-style: 55-day highs on volume, exit on a 20-day low | | `bollinger_reversion` | stocks | buy closes below the lower Bollinger band in uptrends, sell at the middle band | | `fear_greed_dca` | stocks / ETFs | buy in steps when fear is high, trim in extreme greed | | `ema_bounce`, `rsi2`, `golden_cross`, `buy_and_hold` | stocks | simple references and baselines | | `swing_trend`, `swing_rsi2`, `swing_breakout`, `swing_pullback`, `swing_news` | stocks | five textbook swing strategies with a news switch, the [research kit](#-research-kit)'s baselines | | `aggressive_calls` | options | buy ~0.6-delta calls 45–60 days out on pullbacks in strong uptrends; +100% take profit, -50% stop | | `wheel` | options | sell ~0.25-delta cash-secured puts near support; after assignment, sell covered calls above cost | Backtests from January 2018 to November 2026 on the `megacap` list: | Strategy | Profile, capital | CAGR | Sharpe | Max drawdown | Worst year | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `wheel` | aggressive, $1M | 14.1% | 1.12 | -21.7% | +5.8% | | `momentum_rotation` | balanced, $100k | 12.5% | 0.91 | -18.2% | -8.2% | | `risk_aware` | balanced, $100k | 10.4% | 0.84 | -18.2% | -3.8% | | `donchian_breakout` | balanced, $100k | 9.8% | 0.86 | -12.6% | -6.7% | | `aggressive_calls` | aggressive, $100k | 6.7% | 0.30 | -40.3% | -24.7% | | `bollinger_reversion` | balanced, $100k | 4.5% | 0.58 | -4.4% | +0.8% | | SPY buy & hold | | 14.1% | 0.66 | -33.7% | -18.2% | #### Options (backtest only) Option strategies open long calls or puts, cash-secured puts and covered calls. The risk manager caps the premium in long options (`options_sleeve`: 0% conservative, 3% balanced, 12% aggressive; `options_per_trade`: 0 / 1% / 3%), keeps put collateral out of the 30% cash floor and inside the single-stock cap, and never lets shares that back a written call be sold. Expiring options settle at intrinsic value; written puts are assigned into shares, covered calls are called away. There is no free archive of historical option quotes, so the backtester prices options with Black-Scholes on a modelled implied volatility (VIX for index ETFs; realized volatility, a 10% volatility premium and a VIX scaling for stocks) and pays half of a 4% bid-ask spread plus $0.65 per contract. The results move with these assumptions: without the 10% volatility premium the wheel drops to a 0.81 Sharpe and `aggressive_calls` ranges from 3% to 15% a year depending on spread and volatility, always with a drawdown near -40%. Treat option backtests as the shape of a strategy, not a forecast. `riskaware run` skips option orders in this version. Written puts need cash for 100 shares per contract inside the single-stock cap, so the wheel only trades names whose strike × 100 fits (about $10k per name on a $100k aggressive account); test it with `--cash 1000000` or a list of lower-priced names. ### 🧩 Write your own strategy Write one Python method, and the same strategy object runs in backtests, paper trading and live trading with the same risk engine. ```bash riskaware new-strategy my_dip # creates my_dip.py from a template riskaware backtest --strategy my_dip.py --compare risk_aware,buy_and_hold riskaware run --strategy my_dip.py # paper trade it ``` ```python from riskaware.strategy import Action, Signal, Strategy class MyDip(Strategy): name = "my_dip" default_params = {"rsi_entry": 30, "take_profit": 0.20} def on_bar(self, ctx): signals = [] for sym in ctx.universe: row = ctx.row(sym) # indicators at today's close if row is None: continue pos = ctx.position(sym) if pos is None and row["close"] > row["ema200"] and row["rsi14"] < self.params["rsi_entry"]: signals.append(Signal(sym, Action.BUY, strength=0.7, reason="oversold in an uptrend")) elif pos and pos.gain >= self.params["take_profit"]: signals.append(Signal(sym, Action.SELL, strength=0.8, fraction=0.5, reason="take profit")) return signals ``` A strategy only says what it wants and how sure it is; the risk manager decides the size and enforces the cash floor, caps and regime rules, so your strategy inherits the same protection. `ctx.market` has the regime, VIX and upcoming events; `ctx.quality(sym)` and `ctx.news(sym)` give the earnings verdict and the verified news in live runs; `ctx.news` also works in backtests run with `--news`. See [docs/custom-strategies.md](docs/custom-strategies.md). Or describe the strategy and let an AI write it in the [strategy lab](#-strategy-lab). --- ## 📸 Screenshots Every page of the dashboard (`riskaware dashboard`), in English and 中文. Click a picture to open it full size.

Market — the regime, fear and greed, VIX, breadth and the macro calendar
Agents — paper-trading agents ranked against SPY

How it decided — the setups, the risk check, and the LLM's bull case, bear case and verdict

Signals — what a strategy would buy or sell today: conviction and its technical (TA), earnings, news and macro parts, each with a ? that explains it

Cross-verified news — a story counts when two outlets, the company's own release or its SEC filing carry it
News the backtest saw — pick any trade and see the headlines the backtest had at that close, their verdict and the order it placed

value cap, a maximum number of orders per run, no trading on market holidays, and deterministic client order ids so a rerun on the same day cannot duplicate an order. - `riskaware halt` blocks all order submission until `riskaware resume`. - Every run, decision and order is written to a local SQLite journal (`~/.riskaware/journal.db`), visible in the dashboard. - API keys stay in `.env` (see [backtesting with news without look-ahead bias](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/news-backtesting.html) · [point-in-time market data for 2026](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/point-in-time-market-data.html) · [testing LLM trading agents](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/llm-trading-agents.html). ### How do I backtest a trading strategy with news, without look-ahead bias? Run `riskaware backtest --news`, or `riskaware research run` for a record you can cite. News is replayed point in time: each day the strategy sees only the headlines and SEC filings published before that day's 16:00 New York close, and its orders fill at the next open. Every research experiment is also run again with a random future after three cut days, and the decisions before each cut must not change. See [news in backtests](docs/news-history.md) and the [research kit](docs/research.md). ### Where can I get historical news data for backtesting? 2020, 2022 and 2026 ship with the package for 64 large-cap US stocks: 19,618, 29,300 and 16,945 items, Benzinga headlines (titles only; for 2026 also SEC 8-K filings), each with its publication time. For other years, `riskaware news-history build` downloads SEC 8-K filings for free, and Benzinga headlines with your own API key; a CSV with a time, a ticker and a headline works too. See [docs/news-history.md](docs/news-history.md). ### Is there a free point-in-time dataset of US stock prices, VIX and news? Yes. The research kit holds three frozen periods, 2026 to date, 2022 and 2020, each with daily bars for 64 stocks and 25 ETFs from two years before it, the VIX term structure (VIX9D, VIX, VIX3M, VVIX) and that year's news, with SHA-256 hashes so that a paper can cite the exact data. `riskaware research day 2022-06-13` shows everything that was known at that close. See [what ships](docs/research.md#what-ships). ### How do I evaluate an LLM trading agent fairly? Let it trade a frozen period (2026, 2022 or 2020) one decision at a time with `riskaware research trade --llm ...`, or with `trading_session_start` over MCP. Each observation holds only what was known at that close, orders fill at the next open, and the run is saved with every order and its metrics against SPY. Blind mode replaces tickers, company names and dates, so the model cannot recall how a stock did. See [LLM agents](docs/research.md#let-an-llm-trade-a-period). ### Can Claude, ChatGPT (Codex) or Gemini backtest my strategy? Yes, over MCP. Run `riskaware mcp-setup claude-desktop --apply` (or `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini`), then describe the strategy in words. The assistant writes it as code; the code is checked for dates, tickers and side effects, runs in a separate process, and comes back with metrics, confidence intervals and a look-ahead verdict. See the [MCP server](#-mcp-server) and the [strategy lab](docs/strategy-lab.md). ### Does news sentiment improve swing trading strategies? Not in our 2026 test with headline sentiment from one feed. A news filter made each of five common swing strategies (trend following, RSI(2) mean reversion, breakouts, pullbacks, post-news drift) slightly worse, and buying on positive headlines did worse than buying the same price move without them. Trend following made +21.1% against SPY's +12.1%. See the [results](#-research-kit). ### How do I paper trade before risking real money? Paper trading is the default. `riskaware run` trades the built-in paper account, `riskaware agents` runs several strategies on simulated money every trading day, and broker paper accounts such as Alpaca's work too. Live trading needs three explicit switches. See [safety](#-safety). ### Which brokers are supported? A built-in paper account, Alpaca, Interactive Brokers, Public.com, Charles Schwab, tastytrade, Tradier, Futu/moomoo, Tiger Brokers and Longbridge. See [brokers](#-brokers). ## 🧭 Roadmap - Point-in-time fundamentals from SEC XBRL for backtests - Live option orders (option chains from each broker), protective puts and collars - More brokers (Webull, E*TRADE) and crypto / HK / A-share markets - Walk-forward parameter studies ## 🤝 Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome: new brokers, data sources, strategies, translations. Run `pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest` before you open a PR, and see [CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md). Everyone here follows the [code of conduct](.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md). ## 📝 Citation [![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.24202496.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24202496) If you use the package or its frozen markets in your research, please cite it. Every release is archived on Zenodo; [10.5281/zenodo.24202496](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24202496) always resolves to the latest version, and each release page there has its own DOI. GitHub's **Cite this repository** button gives other formats ([CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff)); for the data, add the period, its version and the SHA-256 from its manifest in `src/riskaware/research/data/`. ```bibtex @software{risk_aware_trading_agents, title = {Risk-Aware Trading Agents: AI trading agents for US stocks with point-in-time news backtesting}, author = {{Risk-Aware Trading Agents contributors}}, year = {2026}, version = {0.7.2}, doi = {10.5281/zenodo.24202496}, url = {https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents} } ``` ## ❗ Disclaimer This software is for research and education. name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.12", "3.13"]
        exclude:
          - os: macos-latest
            python-version: "3.10"
          - os: windows-latest
            python-version: "3.10"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: pip
      - name: Install
        run: python -m pip install -e ".[dev,llm]"
      - name: Lint
        run: ruff check src tests
      - name: Test (offline)
        run: pytest

## A benchmark for LLM trading agents, with news replayed by the minute it was published Most news backtests join headlines to prices by calendar date, so a headline published after the close is traded at that close. Here every headline arrives at the minute it was published and orders fill at the next open, through three frozen markets: the 2020 crash, the 2022 bear market and 2026. Llama, GPT, Claude and Gemini trade them blind and with names, three seeds each, scored apart before and after each model's training cutoff. **The same package is also a set of AI trading agents for US stocks that check the macro calendar, the fear index and verified news before they buy.** Market regimes from VIX and the FOMC / CPI calendar · dip buying with an earnings check · a 30% cash floor · cross-verified news · paper-trading agents ranked against SPY · news backtests that cannot see the future · a public leaderboard of LLM trading agents · frozen 2020, 2022 and 2026 markets for research · LLM agents over MCP · paper and live trading on 10 brokers. [🌐 Website](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/) · [🏆 LLM leaderboard](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/leaderboard.html) · [中文说明 → README_zh.md](README_zh.md) · [🚀 Quick start](#-quick-start) · [🆕 What's new](#-whats-new) · [🔬 Research kit](#-research-kit) · [🔗 MCP](#-mcp-server) · [📸 Screenshots](#-screenshots) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) [![CI](https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![PyPI 0.7.2](https://img.shields.io/badge/pypi-0.7.2-e5534b.svg)](https://pypi.org/project/risk-aware-trading-agents/) [![Python 3.10+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-3776ab.svg)](https://www.python.org/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-2ea043.svg)](LICENSE) [![MCP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-server-24292f.svg)](#-mcp-server) [![Docker image](https://img.shields.io/badge/docker-ghcr.io-2496ed.svg)](https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents/pkgs/container/risk-aware-trading-agents) [![Dataset on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/dataset-Hugging%20Face-ffcc4d.svg)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/jacksonwangpro1/point-in-time-market-data-2026) [![English and Chinese](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-English%20%7C%20%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87-e3b341.svg)](README_zh.md) Screens from the dashboard and from riskaware research run on the bundled 2026 data. A backtest shows what a strategy would have done, not what it will do.
## 🚀 Quick start ```bash pip install "risk-aware-trading-agents[dashboard,mcp]" # Python 3.10+ riskaware dashboard # the web UI on http://localhost:8501, English and 中文 ``` Then, in another terminal: ```bash riskaware init # 2-minute wizard: language, risk profile, broker, watchlist riskaware regime # market regime, VIX, fear & greed, next FOMC / CPI / jobs report riskaware scan # today's signals, each with its reasons riskaware analyze NVDA # what every agent thinks about one stock riskaware news AAPL # cross-verified headlines riskaware backtest --compare buy_and_hold,ema_bounce riskaware run # one paper-trading cycle (built-in paper account) riskaware agents init # four starter paper-trading agents riskaware agents run # let them trade once now riskaware agents schedule --install # ...and every trading day from now on riskaware research run -s swing_trend # a strategy on the frozen 2026 market, with a look-ahead check riskaware research run -s swing_trend --period 2022 # the same in the 2022 bear market ``` No account or API key is needed for any of these. Add `--lang zh` to any command for Chinese output. For the newest code before it is released, use `pip install "risk-aware-trading-agents[dashboard,mcp] @ git+https://github.com/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents"`; to change the code, clone the repository and run `pip install -e ".[dashboard,mcp]"`. **Docker**, for x86-64 and ARM: ```bash docker run --rm -p 8501:8501 ghcr.io/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents dashboard # http://localhost:8501 docker run -i --rm ghcr.io/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents mcp # MCP server over stdio ``` For the daily paper-trading scheduler as well, put `riskaware.yaml` (from `riskaware init`) and, if you use broker keys, `.env` in the repository root, then run `docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d` (or `make docker`). **Nothing to install:** [![Open in GitHub Codespaces](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/jackson-cmd/risk-aware-trading-agents) opens the repository in your browser with every extra installed. Run `riskaware dashboard` there and port 8501 opens by itself. ## Is it for you? - You trade **US stocks over days to weeks** and want rules you can read: buy quality names on pullbacks, keep cash, and never sell in a panic. - You want **backtests that cannot cheat**: news replayed as it was published, orders at the next open, and a look-ahead check on every research run. - You **study LLM trading agents** and need data and a setup that others can repeat: three frozen markets (the 2020 crash, the 2022 bear market, 2026), a blind mode, a saved record of every run, and a [public leaderboard](https://jackson-cmd.github.io/risk-aware-trading-agents/leaderboard.html) you can submit to. - You use **Claude, Codex or Gemini** and want them to test a strategy you describe in words, on your own plan, with no API key. - You want to **paper trade first**: several strategies side by side on simulated money, ranked against SPY every trading day. - You read **English or Chinese**: the CLI, the dashboard, the reports and the docs come in both.
