![Olympus: a towering mountain crowned by a celestial palace, surrounded by cyborg gods, AI agents, and lobster adventurers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/main/assets/olympus-banner.png) # ⛰️ Olympus **Your machine, your memory. Keep your private things private.** Olympus keeps your email, files and messages on your own computer and decides, item by item, what each AI may see. ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and any app that speaks MCP can use it, while your private things stay private. On a Mac, and on [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org) and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS Linux. Free and open source. [![version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-1.4.2-534AB7)](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) [![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-0F6E56)](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/LICENSE) [![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-3400%2B%20passing-1D9E75)](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) [![openclaw](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenClaw-2026.7.1%2B-378ADD)](https://openclaw.ai) [![runtime](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime-Bun%20%2B%20TypeScript-B45309)](https://bun.sh) [olympusplugin.ai](https://olympusplugin.ai) · [Get started](#get-started) · [Olympus in ChatGPT](#olympus-for-chatgpt) · [Claude, Grok and other apps](#claude-grok-and-other-apps) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Sources](#supported-sources) · [Security model](#the-security-model) · [OpenClaw quickstart](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/QUICKSTART.md) · [Commands](#command-reference) --- > **🤖 Installing this as an AI agent for OpenClaw?** Stop and read > **[INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md)** before running any > command — it is the step-by-step runbook you must follow, including > exactly what to tell your operator after each step (your install report > must end with the Step 1→2 invitation, never a bare status line). Managed > `git:`, `clawhub:`, and `npm-pack:` installs intentionally hide their internal > package path; use the installed `olympus` CLI and this packaged runbook rather > than searching OpenClaw's managed storage. **Setting up Olympus for ChatGPT, > Claude or Grok instead?** Follow [Get started](#get-started), not this > runbook. --- Frontier AI models are the smartest, but using them means sending your life to someone else's cloud. Local models keep it home, but they are a step behind, and the best ones need an expensive computer under your desk. Olympus gives you both, on the laptop you already have. Every email, file and message is judged, one by one, as **Personal**, **Private** or **Secret**: on your own computer by default, or by Venice's private models if you choose a Venice-only setup. - **Personal:** ChatGPT, Claude or Grok can read the parts that answer your question, and cite them. - **Private:** only a model on your computer reads it (or Venice, if you turn it on); your AI app never gets the item itself. In ChatGPT, only you see the answer; other apps get an answer written from it, which can repeat what it says. - **Secret:** passwords, recovery codes and keys. Once Olympus recognizes a Secret, it is never sent or answered from. Labels are automatic and can be wrong. Everything is stored and searched on your computer: the search index is built there, by a model small enough for a computer with 8 GB of memory. There is no hosted copy of your things, no account and no subscription. Olympus's publisher runs only a relay that passes your AI app's requests to your computer without storing them. Google sign-in happens on your computer, directly with Google. For hard private questions you can reach stronger models: [Venice](https://venice.ai) runs private models that, under Venice's own terms, keep nothing you send, and zkAPI, from OpenAnonymity and the Ethereum Foundation, hides who is asking (see [Stronger models, privately](#stronger-models-privately)). ```text you › "What did I commit to this week, across email and Telegram?" agent › Three commitments: the tax documents to Maria by Friday (email, Tue), reviewing the lease amendment (email, Mon), and the Saturday ride logistics (Telegram, Wed). [3 citations] ``` Your agent saw a bounded, cited, policy-gated answer. It never saw your mailbox. ## Get started You need a Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) on macOS 13 Ventura or later, or an x86_64 computer running [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org) or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. Intel Macs, other Linux distributions and ARM Linux are not supported yet. You do not need OpenClaw, Tailscale, an API key or a new account. **1. Install Olympus on your computer.** On a Mac, open **Terminal** and run: ```bash curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/install.sh | sh ``` On Omarchy, first install the tools Olympus uses to read scans, photos and voice notes, then run the Linux installer: ```bash sudo pacman -S --needed tesseract tesseract-data-eng poppler libvips libheif ffmpeg curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/install-linux.sh | sh ``` On Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, install the prerequisites and run the Linux installer: ```bash sudo apt install curl ca-certificates tar unzip coreutils findutils gawk grep diffutils procps util-linux systemd python3 tesseract-ocr tesseract-ocr-eng poppler-utils libvips-tools libheif1 ffmpeg curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/install-linux.sh | sh ``` Each installer installs Olympus for your user only (the installer itself needs no administrator password; the package installation lines above do), checks every download against a pinned SHA-256 before using it, keeps Olympus running in the background (a LaunchAgent on a Mac, a systemd user service on Linux), adds the `olympus` command, and waits until the engine proves it is running. On Omarchy it also adds **Olympus** to the app launcher. Then Olympus downloads its built-in models once. Running it again updates or repairs the install; a failed update puts the previous version back. Details, folders and uninstall: . **2. Connect your AI.** Each app has a short guide: [ChatGPT](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/chatgpt/) · [Claude](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/claude/) · [Grok and Grok Bot](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/grok/) · [Dots](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/dots/) · [Claude Code](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/claude-code/) · [Codex](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/codex/) · [OpenClaw](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/openclaw/) · [Hermes](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/hermes/) · [any MCP app](https://olympusplugin.ai/install/other/). In ChatGPT, Claude and Grok you add Olympus's address as a connector (in ChatGPT, in Developer mode until Olympus is listed in its directory), then approve it with one click on a page Olympus opens on your own computer: there is no pairing code and no account to create. Grok Bot then uses the Grok connection. Apps on your computer, such as Claude Code, Codex and Hermes, connect with one command. **3. Connect your sources and ask.** Open the dashboard (in ChatGPT, ask *"Show my Olympus dashboard"*; on your computer, run `olympus dashboard`), connect Dropbox, Gmail or Google Drive, pick folders, and ask the way you normally would. ## Olympus for ChatGPT In ChatGPT, Olympus is a plugin. The Olympus engine runs on your computer and keeps your index there; ChatGPT asks it questions through one secure connection that you approve on that computer. ### 1. Add Olympus in ChatGPT Install Olympus on your computer first ([Get started](#get-started)). Olympus is on its way to ChatGPT's app directory. Until it is listed, add it yourself: in ChatGPT, open **Plugins**, choose **+**, then **Add custom MCP server**. Name it Olympus, choose OAuth, and paste `https://mcp.olympusplugin.ai/mcp` as the URL. If you don't see Add custom MCP server, turn on **Developer mode** in **Settings** first. OpenAI decides which accounts have Developer mode; in a work or school workspace, an admin may need to allow it. Step by step: . On Omarchy, ChatGPT may still say Olympus needs a Mac; it works on Omarchy too. ### 2. Approve ChatGPT on your computer The first time ChatGPT connects to Olympus, an Olympus page opens in your computer's browser asking *Connect ChatGPT to Olympus?* Click **Connect**. (If a page saying *Approve ChatGPT on your Mac* comes first, click **Continue on this Mac**; the page says Mac on Omarchy too.) Clicking Connect on your own computer is how Olympus knows the computer is yours: there is no code to copy and no account to create. To check on it later, run `olympus engine status` in a terminal. ### 3. Connect Dropbox and choose folders Open the **Olympus** dashboard in ChatGPT's sidebar (or ask *"Show my Olympus dashboard"*). Choose **Connect** next to Dropbox and sign in with your own Dropbox account; the sign-in link works once, for 10 minutes, from any device. Gmail and Google Drive connect the same way, except that you open their sign-in link on the computer where Olympus runs, not on a phone. Then pick folders. For each folder choose: - **Full**: Olympus reads the files and can answer from what they say. - **Names only**: Olympus keeps the file names and details such as dates, not what the files say. - **Skip**: Olympus leaves the folder alone. A folder follows its parent's choice unless you change it; **Mixed** means some folders inside it are set differently. Choose **Save and start**, and indexing begins on your computer. ### 4. Tell Olympus what's private Olympus sorts every item, one by one, into one of three tiers: - **Personal**: everyday mail, notes and files. ChatGPT can see the parts that answer your question, and cites them. - **Private**: things you keep to yourself, such as health, money or family matters. What they say is never sent to ChatGPT. Olympus answers from them on your computer, in the private answer panel (below). - **Secret**: passwords, recovery codes and keys. What Olympus recognizes as a Secret never reaches a model and is never answered from. Recognition looks for common forms (private keys, API keys, labeled passwords) and can miss others. Olympus decides on your computer. Once its built-in private model is ready, it checks every item it reads before treating it as Personal. Labels are automatic and can be wrong. In the dashboard, **Privacy** asks *"What's private for you?"*: answer in your own words. Once you do, only the kinds of things you call private are Private: health or family matters you leave out, or say are fine to share, can reach ChatGPT. You can also mark folders, Gmail labels or senders as always Private. ### 5. Ask Ask in ChatGPT the way you normally would: *"What did Sam say about the lease?"* ChatGPT searches Olympus and answers from your Personal items, with citations. Olympus also scores search matches with a built-in reranker on computers with 16 GB of memory or more (16 GiB measured RAM). Scoring runs only on this computer. Installing the search model adds one reranker download of about 136 MB; answers use the fused keyword and vector order until it is installed. The reranker is released after 10 idle minutes and loads again when needed. Set `OLYMPUS_SOURCE_RERANKER=off` to turn it off, or `built-in` to enable it on a computer with less memory. ### The private answer panel When some of the items that match your question are Private, a small Olympus panel appears on its own under ChatGPT's reply: **Private answer from your computer**, marked **Not sent to ChatGPT**. - Your computer writes the answer with its built-in private model (Qwen3.5, sized to its memory: 2B under 16 GB, 4B with more) and sends it to the panel sealed, so only the panel can open it. It goes around the ChatGPT conversation, not through it, and the Olympus relay cannot read it. - On an Apple silicon Mac it usually arrives within a minute; on Omarchy it depends on the computer's processor and can take a few minutes. Ask for *"all the details"* and Olympus reads the whole documents instead; that can take a few minutes. - **Sources** (closed at first) lists the items the answer used. Click one to open it on your computer, or in Dropbox on the web if it is not on this computer (ChatGPT opens that web link for you, so it sees the address). - **Hide** folds the answer away and **Show** brings it back. An answer expires after 10 minutes; ask again for a new one. - Ask follow-up questions in the chat as usual; each private answer appears in a new panel. Your computer needs to be awake and online. The panel runs inside ChatGPT's page, so it relies on the panel code ChatGPT loads; the [design](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/design/chatgpt-plugin.md#who-can-read-the-answer) states that limit plainly. ### What ChatGPT can and can't see ChatGPT **can** see: - The parts of your Personal items that answer a question: excerpts, titles, dates and links. - File names, including the names of some Private items. A file's name can be Personal while what it says is Private, so its name may show up in ChatGPT; its contents never do. - That some items matching a question are Private: ChatGPT's model learns just that, with no titles and no content. - Status: which sources are connected, how far indexing has got, and what needs you. The folder picker shows your folder names inside ChatGPT so you can choose; they pass through ChatGPT to reach the picker, but ChatGPT's model is not given them. ChatGPT **can't** see: - What your Private items say, or the private answers made from them. - Secret items Olympus recognizes. - Folders you skip, or what the files in Names-only folders say. - API keys or passwords: you never enter one in ChatGPT. Optional extras such as a Venice account are set up on your computer. The relay at `mcp.olympusplugin.ai` passes ChatGPT's requests to your computer. It stores and logs no questions, answers or tokens, but like any HTTPS service it handles them in transit. Full details: the [ChatGPT design](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/design/chatgpt-plugin.md) and the [trust model](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/TRUST_MODEL.md). ## Claude, Grok and other apps Claude (web, desktop and phone) and Grok connect through the same Olympus relay as ChatGPT, with one click to approve on your computer, and Grok Bot uses the Grok connection; apps on your computer, such as Claude Code, Codex and Hermes, connect there directly. Guides: . They search what is Personal, with citations, like ChatGPT. They never get your Private items themselves or the Secrets Olympus recognizes. For Private items they get at most an answer that the private model on your computer (or Venice, if you set it up) writes from them, checked for secrets, with each item's title, path, source and author. That answer can repeat what the items say. ChatGPT is stricter: it gets no answer from Private items at all, and shows one only in its private answer panel. When an agent is not given an answer, Olympus records the question and the model built into Olympus answers it on your computer; the agent is told only that the answer is in Olympus on your computer, with a link (`olympus://open/private/` and a random identifier) that opens it there. The answer waits in the dashboard's [Inbox](https://olympusplugin.ai/open/private/) (under **On this computer**), which Olympus gives no AI app a way to read, until you delete it, and **Needs you** counts the answers you have not read. More: [Connect other agents](#connect-other-agents). ## Stronger models, privately For hard private questions you can reach stronger models without giving yourself away. Both are off until you turn them on. - **[Venice](https://venice.ai)** runs private models that, under Venice's own terms, keep nothing you send. Add your Venice key under **Keys**, on your computer. In **Ask a question**, a Venice model reads the passages of your files it needs, and is available only if your privacy settings allow Private items to go to Venice; a key alone does not allow it. - **zkAPI**, from OpenAnonymity and the Ethereum Foundation, hides who is asking. It pays anonymously and sends the question over Tor (on unless you turn it off; without Tor, your network address shows): no account, no card, no name, just proof the question is paid for. In **Strict** mode your computer first rewrites the question into general questions; **Standard**, by default, takes out names, contact details and account numbers, or sends your words as written if you choose that. What you ask can still identify you. Turn on **Anonymous answers** under **Keys** on your computer, then ask from your agent or from **Ask a question** in the dashboard's [Inbox](https://olympusplugin.ai/open/private/); each question as sent, and its reply, stay in the Inbox on your computer until you delete them or the Inbox removes the oldest when full. Anonymous answers work on a Mac and on Omarchy and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (x64), once Olympus's network isolation checks pass. ## Uninstall On a Mac, run `curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/uninstall.sh | sh`; on Linux, `curl -fsSL https://olympusplugin.ai/uninstall-linux.sh | sh`. Both stop Olympus and remove the app, the runtime and the `olympus` command, and keep your settings and data. To delete those too, first run `olympus engine stop` and `olympus data delete --all`. To only stop Olympus and remove its login item or service, run `olympus engine uninstall`. The rest of this README covers how Olympus works and Olympus with OpenClaw, which stays supported and optional. ## How it works Olympus ingests your sources into local, trust-tiered indexes, then lets your frontier agent answer questions across all of them, with sensitive material handled only by lanes you approved: your own local models, privacy-approved private cloud inference, or not at all. Every item you ingest is judged on its own as Personal, Private, or Secrets (plus Public on installs made before 1.0; internally S0-S5): its names are Personal unless something raises them, and its content is raised to Private or Secrets on evidence. Each tier has its own index and routes only to the model lanes your sovereignty policy allows: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph sources["Your sources"] direction TB SRC1[Gmail · Drive · Dropbox] SRC2[Telegram · WhatsApp · X] end subgraph olympus["Olympus (local)"] direction TB ING[Ingest & classify
every item, locally] IDX[(Trust-tiered
local indexes)] POL{{Sovereignty policy
your rules, enforced}} ING --> IDX --> POL end subgraph lanes["Model lanes you approved"] direction TB CLOUD[Frontier cloud
everyday content] PRIVATE[Venice
Private content when routed] LOCAL[Your local models
Private content] end AGENT[Your agent
cited, bounded answers] sources --> ING POL --> CLOUD & PRIVATE & LOCAL CLOUD & PRIVATE & LOCAL --> AGENT ``` Olympus uses **Personal** (ordinary personal and work content), **Private** (sensitive material), and **Secrets** (once recognized, never model input). There is no Public tier on any new install, ChatGPT or OpenClaw, whichever posture you choose: anything that would have been Public is Personal. Installs made before 1.0 keep a **Public** tier. See the [tier mapping](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/docs/TRUST_MODEL.md#product-tier-names) for the unchanged storage identifiers. Four postures, chosen (and changeable) in setup — a config file, not a code fork: | Preset | Personal content | Private content: health, finance, legal, therapy, family | |---|---|---| | **Local models and private cloud** (`local-first`) | frontier cloud | approved secure pool with explicit local → [Venice](https://venice.ai) Private order | | **Local models only** (`local-only`) | frontier cloud | your own local models only | | **Private cloud only** (`private-cloud-only`) | frontier cloud | [Venice](https://venice.ai) Private model (`kimi-k3`) | | **Private meaning search on this computer** (`no-sensitive`) | frontier cloud | **stored and searched by meaning on this computer**: its search vectors come from the built-in model and are kept here; no Private agent answer lane | The engine sizes local answer prompts from the model's served context window when it can read it at startup (or the built-in model's manifest). Unknown windows keep the 13,500-byte fallback. Automatic sizing reserves answer tokens and framing space and caps prompts at 27,000 bytes, the size that kept every passage hit in measurement. `/health` lists each local answer route's `local_prompt_budget` source, so a fallback shows. `OLYMPUS_SOURCE_INDEX_LOCAL_ANALYST_PROMPT_BYTES` still overrides that size. “Private cloud only” describes **Private-data handling**: Venice answers Private questions. Search indexing for every tier uses EmbeddingGemma 2, Google's small embedding model, built into Olympus: it downloads once, runs on your computer, needs no account or key, and sends nothing anywhere. On a Mac it also reads pictures, so photos are searchable by what is in them. The embedding choices are built-in local EmbeddingGemma or Venice. Existing Gemini and local-server configurations remain compatible; see the [embedding migration guide](docs/SOVEREIGNTY_CONFIG.md#legacy-embedding-migration). Private content never goes to Gemini. Personal questions use OpenClaw's own configured default model. One question searches every tier. When it finds Private evidence, the private lane your posture approved answers it and your agent receives only the checked, cited answer. Secrets Olympus recognizes are never searched by content: it can tell you where one lives, never what it says. Some rules are not configurable, by design: secure content never routes to ordinary cloud models, recognized secrets are denied to every lane, and an exhausted policy chain refuses rather than silently downgrading. ## Get started with OpenClaw Using ChatGPT? The repo docs and commands should never require raw edits to OpenClaw runtime config. ## The security model Olympus is built on the assumption that the boundary *is* the product: - **Local-first ingestion.** Raw source content lands in local SQLite indexes before any model sees anything. Classification happens on your computer unless you choose Venice for it. - **Sanitized handoffs.** Agents receive answer text, excerpts of Personal items, citations, and audit counts — typed wire shapes with `raw_source_exposed: false`, re-validated client-side. Embeddings, cursors, and tokens never cross. Private items reach an agent only as answers written from them, which can repeat what they say; ChatGPT's model gets none. - **A hard membrane.** Any evidence pack containing sensitive material is barred from standard cloud lanes by two independent checks — policy validation at config load, and a runtime re-check on every request. - **Fail closed, everywhere.** No approved lane for a tier means a refusal with an honest error — never a silent fallback to a less-trusted model. - **Authenticated by default.** The worker binds loopback with bearer-token auth on every route; new installs generate the token during setup. Browser controls exchange it for a short-lived HttpOnly local session protected by same-origin and CSRF checks; the bearer is never stored by the page. - **A real exit.** `olympus data export` gives you your data; `olympus data delete --all` verifiably removes indexes, embeddings, configs, tokens, and service units. The onboarding flow, end to end: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Install
plugin] --> B[olympus setup
pick your posture] B --> C[olympus connect
OAuth IDs · session paths · API-key stdin] C --> D[Dashboard
watch it ingest] D --> E[Ask your agent
cited answers] ``` ## Command reference | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `olympus setup --preset --yes` | writes sovereignty policy and worker auth for the chosen posture | | `olympus connect ...` | records OAuth, session, or API-key credentials with source-specific flags | | `olympus worker foreground\|install\|start\|stop\|restart\|status\|upgrade\|uninstall` | one versioned lifecycle for the local engine, foreground or supervised | | `olympus dashboard` | opens the standalone dashboard with a short-lived authorization link; no worker-token copying | | `olympus dashboard --no-open` | generates an unused opening link for an agent to hand to you | | `olympus dashboard token` | advanced compatibility access to the worker bearer; never share it in chat | | `olympus source answer "…"` | ask across your sources from the terminal | | `olympus ask "…" [--level strict\|standard]` | one question to a frontier model anonymously through zkAPI (paid from your zkAPI balance; the question only) | | `olympus archive start --path \|status\|remove --archive-id ` | asks to import an old export (such as a mail `.mbox`) or to remove an imported one; you approve on the dashboard, and `status` shows progress without any message text | | `olympus tier explain\|set\|recheck\|rules\|classifier …` | why an item has its tier, owner overrides, checking one chat's or source's privacy again, rules, and the private classifier's approval | | `olympus tier migrate plan\|approve\|run\|rollback\|purge\|status` | moves an existing install's items into per-item tiers, each step owner-approved after a dry-run plan | | `olympus doctor` | diagnoses problems, each with a fix-it hint | | `olympus data export\|delete` | your data, out — or gone | | `olympus serve` | MCP stdio server for non-OpenClaw agents | `olympus worker install` and `upgrade` atomically reconcile the generated service unit and owner-only worker environment before activation. Interrupted install or upgrade transactions recover the previous managed files when the same command is rerun. `status` reports the observed service and transaction state; it never guesses that an unreadable manager or non-regular managed path is healthy. `uninstall` removes only the supervised service and intentionally retains credentials, source configuration, and indexed data. Use the separate data lifecycle when those bytes should also be removed. Credential, scope, pairing, Disconnect, partial-sync, and source-dependency repairs do not normally require a worker restart. Follow the source card or `olympus doctor` recovery action instead. It does not revoke provider-side access; the card links the provider revocation page. Local data deletion remains the deliberate CLI-only flow: preview `olympus data delete --source --dry-run`, Disconnect the source, then run the command without `--dry-run`. Telegram and WhatsApp are paired sessions rather than broker grants, so their cards carry **Unpair** instead: it stops new reads and deletes this computer's pairing session, keeping indexed messages and captured media, and leaves the linked device in place at the provider for you to remove there. ### Connect other agents Open the dashboard on this computer (`olympus dashboard`). Name the agent and choose **Create key**, then copy its setup line into the agent. It connects to this computer only, without reading your Olympus files or signing in. - **Agent on my tailnet**: for an agent on your Tailscale network. Keep Tailscale running on both computers, then create a key and copy the setup line. If Tailscale is not running here, the page says so. - The **Grok API** and other agents in the cloud need a tunnel you run yourself (below), unless the agent can use one of the private choices above. The private choices use a different key for each named agent. Each address starts listening only while it has an active key; revoking its last key stops it. The connection list shows which route each key uses. Keys and setup lines are shown once, so copy them before choosing **Done**. These connections use the same remote tools and privacy rules as the relay, with no question limits. They work independently of the remote access switch. Agents in the cloud reach Olympus only when remote access is on; the Agents page says whether it is. To turn it on, press **Turn on remote access** there. Olympus then connects through the Olympus relay (`mcp.olympusplugin.ai`): you create no account and run no tunnel. The relay passes requests between your agents and this computer; it stores and logs no questions, answers or tokens, but like any HTTPS endpoint it handles them in transit. The relay connects ChatGPT, Claude, Grok (grok.com) and Grok Bot, and approving one happens on this computer only, with one click on a page Olympus serves locally; there is no pairing code. A Claude connector approved on this computer then works in Claude on your phone too. **Turn off remote access** turns it off again. If the relay cannot be reached, the page says **Olympus relay unavailable** and Olympus keeps retrying on its own; agents on this computer are unaffected. Advanced: to use a tunnel you run yourself instead of the relay, set `plugins.entries.olympus.config.remote.publicBaseUrl` to its https origin (`openclaw config set …`) and turn remote access on. Through your own tunnel, Claude, ChatGPT and Grok approve Olympus on its approval page with a one-time pairing code from the Agents page, and the Grok API takes an address plus a key from **Create key** (shown once). Every connected agent gets the same privacy rules as your OpenClaw agent. It never gets Private items themselves or the Secrets Olympus recognizes. For Private items it receives only answers that Venice or a local model wrote from them, which can repeat what they say, with each item's title, path, source and author. The Agents page lists connected agents with when each was added and last used, and **Revoke** removes one. `olympus connections list|revoke|pair|add` does the same from a terminal. Each agent's steps end with a short instruction that tells it when to ask Olympus. Paste it into Claude project instructions, Grok's custom instructions or Grok Bot's skills, or load the packaged Agent Skills folder [`integrations/agent-skills/ask-olympus/`](https://github.com/jamiezigelbaum/Olympus/blob/main/integrations/agent-skills/ask-olympus/SKILL.md). ### Using Olympus from other agents (MCP) `olympus serve` exposes the same sanitized read operations — `source_answer`, `source_answer_result`, `source_index_status`, capability-gated `source_index_search`, `ask_anonymously`, `archive_import`, `privacy_item_find` and `privacy_item_set` — to any MCP-capable agent. The supported Hermes configuration narrows that server to exactly `source_answer`, `source_answer_result`, `source_index_status` and `ask_anonymously` through its per-server tool allowlist. `archive_import` (start, status, remove) lets an agent ask to import an old export the user wants searched, such as a mail `.mbox` from Google Takeout or Apple Mail. It only asks: `start` stores the path as text without opening it and returns `needs_approval`; the user approves on the Olympus dashboard on their computer (Sources, Archives), and `remove` works the same way. `status` reports each archive's progress, counts, date range and gaps, never message text. It is on the native, MCP and CLI surfaces only, not on Hermes, remote MCP or the ChatGPT relay. `privacy_item_find` and `privacy_item_set` let an agent act on "that email should be private": find the item by words from its title, sender or file name (items whose names are Private, and Secret items, are never listed), then make it Private. That is the user's decision on that one item, never a rule for its sender, chat or folder. An agent can only raise an item: making it Personal, or putting it back to the judge's label, is the user's on their own computer (`olympus tier set`). Same surfaces as `archive_import`. `ask_anonymously` sends one typed question to a frontier model through zkAPI (paid per question, anonymously, from the user's own balance; what the question says can still identify them). The first call with no `level` returns `needs_choice`: the agent asks the user once for Strict (their own model rewrites the question into general questions before it leaves) or Standard (their words, prepared as written, lightly cleaned up or by their saved instruction), then calls again with `level` and `remember: true`. Only the question goes out, never documents, and never to the provider that hosts the agent asking: a question from ChatGPT goes to Claude Sonnet by default, one from Claude Code or Claude Desktop to an OpenAI model, and a one-off `model` from the agent's own provider is refused. Setup (the zkAPI route, the writer model, the zkAPI models for questions from ChatGPT and from Claude, the spend limit) lives on the dashboard's Anonymous answers card, under Keys. Questions are asked through an agent, `olympus ask`, or **Ask a question** in the dashboard's Inbox; each question as sent, and its reply, are kept in the Inbox on your computer until you delete them or the Inbox removes the oldest when full. See [`docs/design/private-answers.md`](docs/design/private-answers.md). MCP clients cap how long one tool call may run, and an answer can take several minutes. So over MCP (local `olympus serve` and remote `/mcp` alike) and the OpenAPI tool paths, a `source_answer` that is not done by a hand-off threshold returns `{"status": "working", "job_id": …}` and keeps running. The threshold is 45 seconds for remote agents (`OLYMPUS_SOURCE_ANSWER_HANDOFF_MS`, under the MCP SDK's 60-second default request timeout) and for local `olympus serve` (`OLYMPUS_SOURCE_ANSWER_STDIO_HANDOFF_MS`, under Codex's 60-second default tool timeout); both are capped at 230000. `source_answer_result` with that `job_id` returns the answer, the same error the call would have raised, or `working` again after waiting up to a minute (never longer than the threshold). A slow `ask_anonymously` (a Tor route can take minutes) hands off the same way and is collected with the same tool. A job that runs past 20 minutes is stopped with `source_answer_deadline`, and revoking a connection drops its jobs. Remote answers share the analyst with your own assistant's answers; there is no priority lane. So the worker runs at most two remote answers at once (the analyst's lane count; `OLYMPUS_SOURCE_ANSWER_MAX_RUNNING` raises it for a multi-lane analyst) and refuses more with `source_answer_busy`, which bounds how much remote work can ever queue ahead of your own question. A caller that disconnects, or a job that reaches its deadline, stops the analyst call itself and frees the lane. A job id is readable only by the connection (or `olympus serve` process) that asked, lives in memory, and expires 15 minutes after its answer is ready. There are no operator agent tools. Index maintenance — sync, extraction, embedding, retries — is the worker's own scheduler, and what a person drives by hand goes through the `olympus` CLI. The whole agent tool surface is sixteen tools — `argus_ping`, `argus_list_models`, `argus_complete`, `source_answer`, `source_answer_result` (MCP and remote only), `source_index_status`, `source_index_search`, `source_watch_create`, `source_watches`, `source_watch_cancel`, `olympus_doctor`, `olympus_setup_status`, `ask_anonymously`, `archive_import`, `privacy_item_find`, `privacy_item_set` — declared in [`src/core/public-surface.ts`](src/core/public-surface.ts); Hermes over MCP sees the subset above, and worker bearer auth is enforced throughout. Operational note for connector-store corpora: a source with an account folder (Gmail, Drive, Dropbox, local files, Readwise, X, Telegram, WhatsApp, imported archives) keeps its stores where Olympus places them, and its `OLYMPUS_SOURCE_INDEX_CONNECTOR_STORES_JSON` entry names no path: it only adds a principal to the store its lane opened. A store only the mount list places (Reflect, Roam) is mounted with the same corpus id, `family`, `trustDomain` and `dbPath` its sync script writes, and that corpus id must be in the corpus registry — a store mounted for an unregistered corpus fills but is never read. Chat-family mounts must also declare their exact principal identity with `principalProvider` and `principalAccountScope` (for example, `whatsapp` and `personal`). Structured scopes use the stored account scope as their prefix, so the shipped WhatsApp identity is `personal:chat:` while Telegram remains `telegram.personal:chat:`. A chat mount without both fields remains available for non-`chat_scope` reads, but `chat_scope` filtering fails closed as not configured; mounted rows never establish account authority. The migration-era indexes, replay/import utilities, read-authority switches, and retired store writers were removed in Slice 2. Canonical connector stores are now the only source read/write authority. Compatibility aliases that remain at input boundaries do not select another runtime or store. ## Development Olympus is TypeScript on Bun: one plugin package, stable versioned architecture contracts (`SourceConnector` / `EvidencePack` / `Analyst` — only the connector is per-source), and 3,400+ tests including an architecture guard that keeps per-source answer logic out of the shared spine. ```bash bun install bun run test:focus -- test/example.test.ts ``` Use focused local proof while editing; GitHub requires each substantive CI lane and runs the complete suite in parallel before merge. repository.readme:
# pathiel

**An AI trading agent for Hyperliquid: Claude trades perps from Claude Code, with an exact stop and target on every order.**

[![Claude Code plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Code-plugin-d97757.svg)](#install-in-30-seconds)
[![pathiel MCP server – quality and maintenance score on Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Julian-dev28/pathiel/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Julian-dev28/pathiel)
[![Listed on mcpservers.org](https://mcpservers.org/badge.svg)](https://mcpservers.org/servers/julian-dev28/pathiel)
[![Version 0.7.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.7.1-informational.svg)](CHANGELOG.md)
[![MCP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-30_tools-6f42c1.svg)](docs/overhaul/MCP.md)
[![CI](https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)


> **Real money.** A public install runs on Hyperliquid mainnet. With no key
> it only reads; once you add a key, orders are real. Read
> [Before you trade](#before-you-trade) first. Practice on testnet with one
> line: `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet`.

## What it does

pathiel is a free, open-source Hyperliquid MCP server and Claude Code plugin: 30 tools that read Hyperliquid perpetual futures (perps) markets and your account, and place orders, from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP client.
Every trade is one bracket order: an entry, a stop-loss and a take-profit target, sized from your risk profile (3x and 1% of equity per trade by default).
Desk briefs for crude oil (Brent and WTI) and metals (gold and silver) on Hyperliquid's HIP-3 markets give Claude a written call to trade from; nothing trades unless you ask.

## Install in 30 seconds

In Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Julian-dev28/pathiel
/plugin install pathiel@pathiel
/pathiel:setup
```

From a shell instead:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Julian-dev28/pathiel
claude plugin install pathiel@pathiel
```

Claude Code v2.1.275 or later also takes the first two lines as one:
`/plugin install pathiel --marketplace Julian-dev28/pathiel`. If Claude Code
says `Run /reload-plugins to apply`, do that, then run `/pathiel:setup`.

`/pathiel:setup` shows the network and the risks, builds a private Python
environment, creates `~/.pathiel/.env.local` (mode 600) for your keys, seeds
the default risk profile, checks the install without printing any key, and
connects the MCP server. The steps are in `commands/setup.md`.

You need Claude Code, Python 3.11 or later, and for trading a Hyperliquid
account and a browser wallet (or an API wallet you make in the Hyperliquid
app). Reading markets needs no account.
[docs/GETTING_STARTED.md](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) walks through the
account setup.

<!-- bundle:omit -->
### Other MCP clients

Cursor, Claude Desktop, Pathiel Agent and any other MCP client register the
launcher `scripts/pathiel-mcp` from a clone as the server command, or run the
published container (amd64 and arm64). It is listed in the official MCP
registry as `io.github.Julian-dev28/pathiel`.

```bash
docker run -i --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$HOME/.pathiel:/data" \
  ghcr.io/julian-dev28/pathiel-mcp:0.7.1
```

To build it yourself: `docker build -f Dockerfile.mcp -t pathiel-mcp .`

Both are the public install: keys and config come from `~/.pathiel`, with
the same default network, profile and fee rules as the plugin. Starting
`scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` directly, or accepting the repo `.mcp.json`
when you open a clone in Claude Code, is the maintainer path (see
[Maintainer setup](#maintainer-setup)).
<!-- /bundle:omit -->

## First prompts to try

Paste these into Claude Code once `/mcp` shows `pathiel` connected.

| you type | what answers |
|---|---|
| What's the oil desk's call right now? | `get_desk_brief`: direction, entry, stop, target, the R it pays, and "Your size" |
| Show me BTC's order book and funding. | `get_order_book`, `get_market` |
| What's my balance and what's open? | `get_account`, `get_positions` |
| What are my risk limits? | `get_risk_limits` |
| Size a long on gold with the stop under today's low. | `size_trade` |
| Dry-run that as a bracket. | `place_bracket` with `dry_run: true`: judged and sized, nothing sent |
| Place it. | `place_bracket`: **live money**, Claude Code asks you first |
| Run one oil desk tick. | `/pathiel:desk-tick oil`: brief, sweep, levels, one decision |

## What Claude can do

`scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` lists 30 tools over stdio to a plugin
install: one tool per job, verb_noun names (`contracts/mcp_public`). The
maintainer's own checkout lists the 60 only, the operator set the live desks
use. Every older tool name still answers when called; it is just no longer
listed. The full table, generated from the server's own tool lists, is
[docs/overhaul/MCP.md](docs/overhaul/MCP.md).

| group | tools | names |
|---|---|---|
| Market data (no key) | 5 | `get_market`, `list_markets`, `get_candles`, `get_order_book`, `get_funding_regime` |
| Account reads | 4 | `get_account`, `get_positions`, `get_orders`, `get_history` |
| Risk and sizing | 2 | `get_risk_limits`, `size_trade` |
| Orders (live money) | 7 | `place_bracket`, `set_stop` (tighter only), `set_target`, `cancel_order`, `close_position`, `set_leverage`, `sweep_brackets` |
| Desks | 5 | `list_desks`, `get_desk_brief`, `refresh_desk`, `submit_desk_call`, `get_desk_record` |
| Setup | 4 | `get_status`, `get_config`, `update_config`, `connect_wallet` (approve an API wallet with one signature) |
| Research pool | 3 | `get_pool_status`, `join_pool`, `leave_pool` |

`get_account`, `get_positions`, `get_orders` and `get_history` take an
`address` to read any other wallet, and only read it. The server signs with
one key, yours, so it has no path to place, close or resize an order on any
other account.

The oil desk is the one active desk on a fresh install. It trades Brent
(`xyz:BRENTOIL`) on mainnet, and WTI (`xyz:CL`) on testnet, where Brent is
not listed. The metals desk (gold, silver) is registered and off by default;
`get_desk_brief` still reads it. The rules each bracket must pass are in
[docs/strategy/OIL_RULES.md](docs/strategy/OIL_RULES.md).

## Before you trade

### Networks and modes

The mode follows from what is in `~/.pathiel/.env.local`:

| you have | mode | what works |
|---|---|---|
| no key | read-only, mainnet (the default) data | every read tool; order tools answer that no key is configured |
| an [API wallet](https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/API) key | mainnet (the default) | everything, with real money |
| a key and `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` | testnet | everything, with test funds; the oil desk trades WTI (`xyz:CL`) |

**Connect your wallet** is the quick way to a key: `/pathiel:setup` (or
asking Claude to connect your wallet) runs `connect_wallet`. It makes a new
API wallet key on your machine and opens a local page where your browser
wallet approves it with one signature, on the network you run. The key goes
into `~/.pathiel/.env.local` (mode 600) and nowhere else: it can trade, never
withdraw, and your main key never leaves the wallet. Pasting an API wallet
from the Hyperliquid app by hand still works.

State (theses, journals, caches) is kept per network, so testnet and mainnet
never share it. Testnet needs its own API wallet, created and approved in the
[testnet app](https://app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz/API). How to create one,
step by step: [Connect your Hyperliquid account](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md#connect-your-hyperliquid-account).
The network is read once when the server starts: after editing the env file,
reconnect pathiel in `/mcp`.

### How the safety works

- **An exact stop on every order.** `place_bracket` is the one entry path:
  entry, stop and target together. It refuses a bracket that pays under 2R,
  and a stop that sits outside half the distance to liquidation. A market
  entry fills first and its stop goes on right after; if the venue refuses
  that stop, the output says `FILLED WITHOUT A STOP` and `sweep_brackets`
  checks every open position for one.
- **Default profile: 3x, 1%, one position.** At most 3x leverage, 1% of
  equity at the stop per trade (up to 2% only when the venue's minimum order
  size forces it), one position at a time. `set_leverage` refuses above the
  cap. You change the profile with `update_config` or in
  `~/.pathiel/.agent-config.json`; nothing raises it for you.
- **Read-only without a key.** No key, no orders. The API wallet key can
  trade and can never withdraw.
- **Testnet when you want it.** `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` in
  `~/.pathiel/.env.local` switches to test funds.
- **Claude Code asks before each live-money call.** The seven order tools,
  and `update_config`, are marked destructive, so Claude Code asks you before each
  call unless you allow the tool for good. Nothing runs in the background:
  no bot, no scheduler. The `/loop` desk tick trades only while your session runs it.

### Builder fee

None. pathiel is free: no order it places carries a Hyperliquid builder fee,
so you pay only Hyperliquid's own trading fee. There is nothing to approve.

### If a fee ever comes back

It would ship as a new version with the rate in the changelog, and it could
not touch your orders on its own: Hyperliquid charges a builder fee only
after you approve that exact rate with your master wallet, and rejects any
order whose builder fee is above the max you approved. Hyperliquid caps a
perp builder fee at 0.1%. If you approved the 0.01% fee of pathiel 0.4.0,
it is no longer charged; [docs/BUILDER_FEE.md](docs/BUILDER_FEE.md) shows
how to revoke it anyway.

### Risk

Leveraged perps can lose the whole account, fast. The default profile limits
how much one trade can lose at its stop; it does not limit gaps, slippage or
a run of losses. The profile's daily loss figure is shown, not enforced.
There is no demonstrated edge and no return is promised. This is software,
not financial advice. You decide every trade and carry its result.

### Restricted jurisdictions

Hyperliquid's terms bar use from restricted jurisdictions, including by US
persons. The current list is in Hyperliquid's terms. pathiel does not check
where you are; staying within the rules where you live is on you.

### Your data

pathiel runs on your computer and the project runs no server, so nothing is
sent to the maintainer. No analytics, no telemetry. What does leave your
machine:

- **Hyperliquid API** (api.hyperliquid.xyz, or the testnet API): market and
  account reads, the orders you ask for, the API wallet approval you sign.
- **Public data feeds** the desk briefs read: EIA, FRED, CFTC, Congress and
  the Federal Register, prediction markets and news. An optional API key
  for one of them goes only to that feed.
- **GitHub**, only if you join the research pool: the signed statement you
  submit as a pull request.

Keys, theses, the desk journal and your config stay in `~/.pathiel`.
Details: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## Research pool (opt-in)

pathiel can grade your trades alongside everyone else's. You register your
Hyperliquid address with one signed statement; you upload nothing, since
pathiel only reads fills Hyperliquid already makes public. From the time
you join, your public fills on the pool coins (`xyz:BRENTOIL`, `xyz:CL`,
`xyz:SILVER`, `xyz:GOLD`) are graded with the same harness the project runs
on its own trades, and published on a public scoreboard at least 24 hours
late.

What you get: your own graded report (fluke or edge on your trades, with
ranges, through `get_pool_status` with `report: true`), and pool-level stats on which desks and
setups hold up across members.

What it is not: not a fee waiver, since pathiel charges no fee to anyone,
member or not, and joining never changes what you pay. No payout, refund or reward is ever
tied to your returns. Not a copy-trading feed: results are published at
least 24 hours late, never live. No edge is demonstrated by joining, or by
anything the pool's stats show.

Run `/pathiel:share` to join or leave. It shows you the exact statement
before it signs anything, and the pull request it opens for you.

Scoreboard: https://julian-dev28.github.io/pathiel/scoreboard/

### Privacy

What is public: your account address (shortened, with an explorer link),
the date you joined, your closed and graded trade counts, your graded row
(win rate, mean result in R, a label, a luck score), and pool totals that
include your trades. What is never public: anything closed in the last 24
hours, any open position, single trades, prices, sizes, dollar results,
account value, leverage, or any key.

Leaving is one more signed statement, or a request in a GitHub issue with
no signature. Coming back takes a new signed join; only trades after the
new join count, and deleting a leave file never brings an account back on
its own.

Full details, including the exact text you sign: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## FAQ

**How do I connect Claude to Hyperliquid?**
Install pathiel as a Claude Code plugin with the three lines in
[Install in 30 seconds](#install-in-30-seconds). Market data works at once
with no key; add an API wallet key to `~/.pathiel/.env.local` to trade.
Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients use the launcher or the
container described in [Other MCP clients](#other-mcp-clients). No
Anthropic API key is needed: the one model step, the desk thesis behind
`refresh_desk`, runs through your local Claude Code CLI.

**Is pathiel a Hyperliquid trading bot?**
No, and it never trades on its own. It is an MCP server that gives Claude
tools: Claude places an order when you ask for one in the session, and
Claude Code asks before each live-money call. `/loop 15m /pathiel:desk-tick oil`
re-prompts Claude on a timer, only while that session stays open.

**Can it withdraw my money?**
No. pathiel signs with an API wallet, which Hyperliquid lets trade and never
withdraw. Your master key is never stored, and pathiel needs it for nothing:
the only script that takes it revokes a builder fee approval, at a hidden
prompt in your own terminal.

**Does pathiel charge a fee?**
No. Orders carry no builder fee; you pay Hyperliquid's own trading fee
only.

**How do I practice without real money?**
Add `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` to `~/.pathiel/.env.local`, create an API
wallet in the testnet app (app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz), and reconnect
pathiel in `/mcp`. The oil desk trades WTI (`xyz:CL`) there.

**Is there an edge?**
None is demonstrated. The desk briefs are a structured, written call with
levels, not a forecast. `get_desk_record` grades every call in the open.

**How do I remove it?**
Revoke the API wallet in the Hyperliquid app (More, API), then
`claude plugin uninstall pathiel@pathiel` and delete `~/.pathiel` if you want
the keys and state gone.

| [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) | where keys live, what pathiel never does, how to report a problem |
| [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | dev setup, the test gate, style rules |
| [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | what changed per version |

<!-- bundle:omit -->
## Maintainer setup

> Maintainer path: this runs mainnet with the tracked repo config (20x, whole-equity sizing). It is not the public install.

This is how the maintainer runs pathiel on his own account, from a checkout.
It is not the public install and its numbers are not the defaults.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel
cd pathiel
cp .env.local.example .env.local
scripts/restart.sh          # FastAPI Desk page on http://localhost:8000/ and the log rotator
scripts/restart.sh status
```

- **MCP server.** The repo `.mcp.json` starts
  `scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` directly, with no install marker, so it
  runs mainnet on the tracked `.agent-config.json`. Opening a clone in
  Claude Code offers that server; accepting it is the maintainer path, not
  the public install. Other clients that want the public path register
  `scripts/pathiel-mcp`.
- **Risk profile.** The tracked config sets 20x, the whole equity per
  position less the opening fee, one position. The rules `place_bracket`
  enforces (2R minimum, stop inside half the distance to liquidation, one
  slot) hold on both paths.
- **Desk loop.** `.claude/skills/desk-tick/SKILL.md` on `/loop 15m /desk-tick oil`.
  `scripts/build_plugin_skill.py` generates the plugin copies under
  `skills/` and `agents/`; the gate fails when a copy is stale.
- **Gate.** `PATHIEL_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`,
  offline, run by `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` (`scripts/install_hooks.sh`
  wires it in). `scripts/mcp_tool_table.py` regenerates the tool table;
  `.venv/bin/python scripts/mcp_smoke.py` is a live, read-only MCP smoke.
- **Keys.** `scripts/preflight_secrets.py` checks the env file without
  printing it; `docs/SECRETS.md` lists every secret and how to rotate it.

More: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the code layout,
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the hardening checks.

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

# The job reads the repo and nothing else. Without this block GITHUB_TOKEN gets
# the repository's default, which can be read/write on every scope: a step
# compromised through a dependency could then push, tag or open releases.
permissions:
  contents: read

# Actions are pinned to a full commit SHA, not a tag. A tag is a pointer the
# action's owner (or whoever holds their token) can move; tj-actions/changed-
# files (March 2025, CVE-2025-30066) moved every tag to a payload that printed
# runner secrets. The comment names the release the SHA was taken from;
# tests/test_supply_chain.py fails on any `uses:` that is not a 40-hex SHA.

jobs:
  test:
    name: Tests (Python ${{ matrix.python-version }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # 3.13 is what the desk runs on (the operator's .venv, 2026-10-25);
        # 3.11 is the floor pyproject declares. A green matrix that skips the
        # production interpreter is not evidence about production.
        python-version: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1

      - name: Set up Python ${{ matrix.python-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0  # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: requirements.lock

      # Install the EXACT pinned set, not a fresh resolve of the ranges in
      # pyproject.toml. A green CI against a different dependency set than
      # production runs is not evidence about production.
      - name: Install (pinned)
        run: |
          pip install -r requirements.lock
          pip install -e . --no-deps

      # This repo was green locally and red on CI for weeks because 50 files
      # hardcoded /Users/julian_dev/... Cheap check, runs before the suite so
      # the failure names the actual cause instead of a FileNotFoundError.
      - name: No machine-bound absolute paths
        run: python scripts/check_no_absolute_paths.py

      # pytest's addopts deselects the `online` and `live` markers, so this runs
      # only the offline suite — no network, no real-money orders, CI-safe.
      # -rs prints the reason for every skip. Without it the summary says
      # "18 skipped" and nothing else, so a guard that quietly stopped running
      # in this environment looks exactly like a green build.
      - name: Run offline test suite
        run: pytest -rs
sampled_files.Dockerfile:
# Base image pinned by digest (the multi-arch index for python:3.11-slim,
# Debian 13, resolved 2026-10-25). A tag is a pointer Docker Hub can move; the
# digest is the bytes. Bump it on purpose:
#   docker buildx imagetools inspect python:3.11-slim | grep Digest
FROM python:3.11-slim@sha256:07d4824036af339fa1b6ef769cc99d9c10a141769538b52b3b597c84f7a7b535 AS base

ENV PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 \
    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PIP_DISABLE_PIP_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
    PIP_NO_CACHE_DIR=1

# The app runs as this user, never as root (security review 2026-10-25).
# docker-entrypoint.sh starts as root only where it has to (a Fly volume is
# mounted root-owned), hands /data to this user, and drops to it with setpriv
# before exec. k8s sets runAsUser to the same uid, so there not even the
# entrypoint has root.
RUN groupadd --system --gid 10001 pathiel \
 && useradd --system --uid 10001 --gid pathiel --home-dir /app --shell /usr/sbin/nologin pathiel

WORKDIR /app

# Install deps first so `pip install` is cached across code changes.
#
# From requirements.lock, hash-checked, then the package itself with
# --no-deps. Until 2026-10-25 this was a bare `pip install -e .`, which
# resolved the RANGES in pyproject.toml fresh on every build: the image ran
# whatever PyPI served that day, not the set CI tested, and nothing checked a
# single file's hash. (requests and websocket-client still arrive as
# transitive deps of hyperliquid-python-sdk; the lock lists them.) The lock
# also carries the dev extras (pytest, ruff); they cost a few MB and keep one
# lock for CI and prod. No compiler needed: every pin ships a manylinux wheel.
COPY requirements.lock ./
RUN pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.lock
COPY pyproject.toml ./
COPY pathiel/__init__.py pathiel/__init__.py
RUN pip install --no-deps -e .

# Copy every top-level source package a managed process actually imports at
# runtime. `scripts/restart.sh` is the source of truth for what runs:
#   pathiel/              core package — server, dashboard, agents, client
#                                (imported by every process below)
#   scripts/                    the MCP server, log_rotate.py, the desk-tick
#                                tools (desk_slot.py, oil_levels.py), CLI tooling
#   services/intel/             desk news/policy/catalyst/odds/positioning
#                                packet (services.intel.api.build_packet —
#                                imported by services/strategies)
# `services/pathiel_data_api` is its OWN deploy unit — own Dockerfile, own
# Postgres, own requirements.txt (sqlalchemy/psycopg2, never installed here)
# — deliberately NOT bundled into this image. `docs/`, `tests/`, and
# `skills/` are excluded via .dockerignore; see that file for the full list
# and why. (`services/trend_engine` and `research/` were deleted 2026-10-25.)
COPY pathiel/ pathiel/
# The shared pydantic contracts every service imports at module load
# (pathiel.agents.config_store -> contracts.risk.models on the server's
# first import). Missing until 2026-10-25: the image built fine and
# `python -m pathiel.server` died with ModuleNotFoundError.
COPY contracts/ contracts/
COPY scripts/ scripts/
# Auth is on the request path for every gated route, so a missing copy here is
# not a degraded feature, it is a server that 500s on the first page load.
COPY services/auth/ services/auth/
# server.py mounts this router unconditionally (/api/desks, /desks/...) —
# same "500 on first import" reasoning as auth above.
COPY services/strategies/ services/strategies/
# Zero-LLM news/policy/catalyst/odds/positioning packet services/strategies
# imports (services.intel.api.build_packet) — same reasoning again.
COPY services/intel/ services/intel/
# LLM gateway (local Claude Code CLI only) and the desk thesis writer on top
# of it. The image has no claude CLI, so in a container write_thesis degrades
# to the previous thesis or a flat placeholder instead of crashing.
COPY services/llm/ services/llm/
COPY services/thesis/ services/thesis/
# Account registry, vault and credentials (the connect flow). server.py mounts
# services.accounts.api, so it must ship: same reasoning as auth above.
COPY services/accounts/ services/accounts/
# server.py mounts services.risk.api (risk_limits/risk_size_trade and the
# place_bracket feasibility check both derive through it).
COPY services/risk/ services/risk/
# The trade review (python3 -m services.review run): read-only ledger, stats
# and backtest proposals. Not on the request path; shipped so the image can
# run the daily review against its own state volume.
COPY services/review/ services/review/
# The research pool's CODE only (python3 -m services.pool). Not on the request
# path, and this image cannot run the scoreboard build: it does not hold pool/
# (the signed member files) or docs/scoreboard/ (the output, a tracked file
# the maintainer commits). The build runs from the maintainer's checkout. The
# line is here because tests/test_deploy_config.py wants a COPY for every
# services package that code under pathiel/, scripts/ or services/ imports.
COPY services/pool/ services/pool/
COPY conftest.py ./

# ── Runtime state ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# State lives on a persistent volume mounted at /data (k8s
# volumeClaimTemplates, or `docker run -v`) so `web` keeps one source of truth
# across restarts and redeploys.
#
# Almost every state path in this app routes through PATHIEL_STATE_DIR (see
# pathiel/state.py:state_file — backup receipts and other process-local
# state files all resolve relative to it; also services/*/env.py).
# Pointing that ONE var at /data/.state redirects all of them together.
# docker-entrypoint.sh creates the real /data/.state directory at container
# start (the volume is empty/fresh at that point, not at image-build time).
#
# 2026-10-23 (wave 2): PATHIEL_DSL_STATE_FILE and PATHIEL_AGENT_MEMORY_FILE
# are dropped — pathiel.agents.dsl_exit and pathiel.agents.memory, their only
# readers, are retired with the rest of the autonomous engine. The
# scripts/scheduler.py symlink workaround this section used to carry is
# dropped the same wave: scheduler.py itself is deleted. 2026-10-25:
# PATHIEL_POSITIONS_SNAPSHOT_FILE goes too — the loop that wrote the snapshot
# is gone, so the dashboard reads positions live (cached) and the module
# that read the file is deleted.

# HOME on the volume: pathiel/client/universe.py caches under ~/.pathiel and
# scripts/backup_state.py defaults to ~/pathiel-backups. As root HOME was
# /root; the app user may not write there, and on k8s the root filesystem is
# read-only, so the one writable, persistent place is /data.
ENV HOME=/data/home

ENV SESSION_LOG_PATH=/data/session-log.jsonl \
    PATHIEL_AGENT_CONFIG_FILE=/data/.agent-config.json \
    PATHIEL_STATE_DIR=/data/.state

# ── Networking ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# pathiel/server.py defaults PATHIEL_BIND to 127.0.0.1 (a 2026-07-10
# security fix for running bare on an operator's Mac, so the dashboard isn't
# reachable from the LAN by default). Inside a container that default makes
# the process unreachable from anywhere OUTSIDE its own network namespace —
# `docker run -p` and k8s probes/Services all connect from outside it, so the
# request never lands and every health check times out. 0.0.0.0 is correct
# and safe here: the container/pod boundary is the actual security perimeter
# (the k8s Service, or whatever fronts `docker run`), not the loopback
# interface.
ENV PATHIEL_BIND=0.0.0.0

# No LLM credential is baked in or expected. The one LLM step (the desk thesis
# writer, services/thesis via services/llm) shells out to a LOCALLY
# AUTHENTICATED Claude Code CLI session: an operator's desktop subscription,
# not a credential that can be passed as a secret. In a container
# desk_refresh degrades to the previous thesis or a flat placeholder; the
# operator refreshes theses from their own machine through the MCP server.
# (The AI_BRAIN_PROVIDER / OPENROUTER_API_KEY pair this section used to set
# left with pathiel/agents/ai_brain.py on 2026-10-25.)

# Every managed process shares this one bootstrap step (see the script for
# why) before running its real command.
COPY docker-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod 0755 /usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh \
 && mkdir -p /app/logs /data/.state /data/home \
 && chown -R pathiel:pathiel /app/logs /data
# Source stays root-owned and read-only to the app user: code that is
# compromised at runtime cannot rewrite itself for the next restart. Only
# /app/logs (log_rotate.py) and /data (state) are the app's to write.
ENTRYPOINT ["docker-entrypoint.sh"]

EXPOSE 8000

# Default command runs the FastAPI server (dashboard + API). The log rotator
# runs as a second k8s container sharing this same image — see
# k8s/statefulset.yaml. (There is no trading loop or scheduler process since
# 2026-10-23; Claude is the trader, via the MCP server on the operator's
# machine. Fly.io was dropped as a target 2026-10-25.)
CMD ["python3", "-m", "pathiel.server"]
