sampled_files.README.md:
# pathiel

**An AI trading agent for Hyperliquid: Claude trades perps from Claude Code, with an exact stop and target on every order.**

[![Claude Code plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude_Code-plugin-d97757.svg)](#install-in-30-seconds)
[![pathiel MCP server – quality and maintenance score on Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Julian-dev28/pathiel/badges/score.svg)](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/Julian-dev28/pathiel)
[![Listed on mcpservers.org](https://mcpservers.org/badge.svg)](https://mcpservers.org/servers/julian-dev28/pathiel)
[![Version 0.7.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.7.1-informational.svg)](CHANGELOG.md)
[![MCP server](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-30_tools-6f42c1.svg)](docs/overhaul/MCP.md)
[![CI](https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)


> **Real money.** A public install runs on Hyperliquid mainnet. With no key
> it only reads; once you add a key, orders are real. Read
> [Before you trade](#before-you-trade) first. Practice on testnet with one
> line: `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet`.

## What it does

pathiel is a free, open-source Hyperliquid MCP server and Claude Code plugin: 30 tools that read Hyperliquid perpetual futures (perps) markets and your account, and place orders, from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor or any MCP client.
Every trade is one bracket order: an entry, a stop-loss and a take-profit target, sized from your risk profile (3x and 1% of equity per trade by default).
Desk briefs for crude oil (Brent and WTI) and metals (gold and silver) on Hyperliquid's HIP-3 markets give Claude a written call to trade from; nothing trades unless you ask.

## Install in 30 seconds

In Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Julian-dev28/pathiel
/plugin install pathiel@pathiel
/pathiel:setup
```

From a shell instead:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Julian-dev28/pathiel
claude plugin install pathiel@pathiel
```

Claude Code v2.1.275 or later also takes the first two lines as one:
`/plugin install pathiel --marketplace Julian-dev28/pathiel`. If Claude Code
says `Run /reload-plugins to apply`, do that, then run `/pathiel:setup`.

`/pathiel:setup` shows the network and the risks, builds a private Python
environment, creates `~/.pathiel/.env.local` (mode 600) for your keys, seeds
the default risk profile, checks the install without printing any key, and
connects the MCP server. The steps are in `commands/setup.md`.

You need Claude Code, Python 3.11 or later, and for trading a Hyperliquid
account and a browser wallet (or an API wallet you make in the Hyperliquid
app). Reading markets needs no account.
[docs/GETTING_STARTED.md](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md) walks through the
account setup.

<!-- bundle:omit -->
### Other MCP clients

Cursor, Claude Desktop, Pathiel Agent and any other MCP client register the
launcher `scripts/pathiel-mcp` from a clone as the server command, or run the
published container (amd64 and arm64). It is listed in the official MCP
registry as `io.github.Julian-dev28/pathiel`.

```bash
docker run -i --rm --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" -v "$HOME/.pathiel:/data" \
  ghcr.io/julian-dev28/pathiel-mcp:0.7.1
```

To build it yourself: `docker build -f Dockerfile.mcp -t pathiel-mcp .`

Both are the public install: keys and config come from `~/.pathiel`, with
the same default network, profile and fee rules as the plugin. Starting
`scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` directly, or accepting the repo `.mcp.json`
when you open a clone in Claude Code, is the maintainer path (see
[Maintainer setup](#maintainer-setup)).
<!-- /bundle:omit -->

## First prompts to try

Paste these into Claude Code once `/mcp` shows `pathiel` connected.

| you type | what answers |
|---|---|
| What's the oil desk's call right now? | `get_desk_brief`: direction, entry, stop, target, the R it pays, and "Your size" |
| Show me BTC's order book and funding. | `get_order_book`, `get_market` |
| What's my balance and what's open? | `get_account`, `get_positions` |
| What are my risk limits? | `get_risk_limits` |
| Size a long on gold with the stop under today's low. | `size_trade` |
| Dry-run that as a bracket. | `place_bracket` with `dry_run: true`: judged and sized, nothing sent |
| Place it. | `place_bracket`: **live money**, Claude Code asks you first |
| Run one oil desk tick. | `/pathiel:desk-tick oil`: brief, sweep, levels, one decision |

## What Claude can do

`scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` lists 30 tools over stdio to a plugin
install: one tool per job, verb_noun names (`contracts/mcp_public`). The
maintainer's own checkout lists the 60 only, the operator set the live desks
use. Every older tool name still answers when called; it is just no longer
listed. The full table, generated from the server's own tool lists, is
[docs/overhaul/MCP.md](docs/overhaul/MCP.md).

| group | tools | names |
|---|---|---|
| Market data (no key) | 5 | `get_market`, `list_markets`, `get_candles`, `get_order_book`, `get_funding_regime` |
| Account reads | 4 | `get_account`, `get_positions`, `get_orders`, `get_history` |
| Risk and sizing | 2 | `get_risk_limits`, `size_trade` |
| Orders (live money) | 7 | `place_bracket`, `set_stop` (tighter only), `set_target`, `cancel_order`, `close_position`, `set_leverage`, `sweep_brackets` |
| Desks | 5 | `list_desks`, `get_desk_brief`, `refresh_desk`, `submit_desk_call`, `get_desk_record` |
| Setup | 4 | `get_status`, `get_config`, `update_config`, `connect_wallet` (approve an API wallet with one signature) |
| Research pool | 3 | `get_pool_status`, `join_pool`, `leave_pool` |

`get_account`, `get_positions`, `get_orders` and `get_history` take an
`address` to read any other wallet, and only read it. The server signs with
one key, yours, so it has no path to place, close or resize an order on any
other account.

The oil desk is the one active desk on a fresh install. It trades Brent
(`xyz:BRENTOIL`) on mainnet, and WTI (`xyz:CL`) on testnet, where Brent is
not listed. The metals desk (gold, silver) is registered and off by default;
`get_desk_brief` still reads it. The rules each bracket must pass are in
[docs/strategy/OIL_RULES.md](docs/strategy/OIL_RULES.md).

## Before you trade

### Networks and modes

The mode follows from what is in `~/.pathiel/.env.local`:

| you have | mode | what works |
|---|---|---|
| no key | read-only, mainnet (the default) data | every read tool; order tools answer that no key is configured |
| an [API wallet](https://app.hyperliquid.xyz/API) key | mainnet (the default) | everything, with real money |
| a key and `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` | testnet | everything, with test funds; the oil desk trades WTI (`xyz:CL`) |

**Connect your wallet** is the quick way to a key: `/pathiel:setup` (or
asking Claude to connect your wallet) runs `connect_wallet`. It makes a new
API wallet key on your machine and opens a local page where your browser
wallet approves it with one signature, on the network you run. The key goes
into `~/.pathiel/.env.local` (mode 600) and nowhere else: it can trade, never
withdraw, and your main key never leaves the wallet. Pasting an API wallet
from the Hyperliquid app by hand still works.

State (theses, journals, caches) is kept per network, so testnet and mainnet
never share it. Testnet needs its own API wallet, created and approved in the
[testnet app](https://app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz/API). How to create one,
step by step: [Connect your Hyperliquid account](docs/GETTING_STARTED.md#connect-your-hyperliquid-account).
The network is read once when the server starts: after editing the env file,
reconnect pathiel in `/mcp`.

### How the safety works

- **An exact stop on every order.** `place_bracket` is the one entry path:
  entry, stop and target together. It refuses a bracket that pays under 2R,
  and a stop that sits outside half the distance to liquidation. A market
  entry fills first and its stop goes on right after; if the venue refuses
  that stop, the output says `FILLED WITHOUT A STOP` and `sweep_brackets`
  checks every open position for one.
- **Default profile: 3x, 1%, one position.** At most 3x leverage, 1% of
  equity at the stop per trade (up to 2% only when the venue's minimum order
  size forces it), one position at a time. `set_leverage` refuses above the
  cap. You change the profile with `update_config` or in
  `~/.pathiel/.agent-config.json`; nothing raises it for you.
- **Read-only without a key.** No key, no orders. The API wallet key can
  trade and can never withdraw.
- **Testnet when you want it.** `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` in
  `~/.pathiel/.env.local` switches to test funds.
- **Claude Code asks before each live-money call.** The seven order tools,
  and `update_config`, are marked destructive, so Claude Code asks you before each
  call unless you allow the tool for good. Nothing runs in the background:
  no bot, no scheduler. The `/loop` desk tick trades only while your session runs it.

### Builder fee

None. pathiel is free: no order it places carries a Hyperliquid builder fee,
so you pay only Hyperliquid's own trading fee. There is nothing to approve.

### If a fee ever comes back

It would ship as a new version with the rate in the changelog, and it could
not touch your orders on its own: Hyperliquid charges a builder fee only
after you approve that exact rate with your master wallet, and rejects any
order whose builder fee is above the max you approved. Hyperliquid caps a
perp builder fee at 0.1%. If you approved the 0.01% fee of pathiel 0.4.0,
it is no longer charged; [docs/BUILDER_FEE.md](docs/BUILDER_FEE.md) shows
how to revoke it anyway.

### Risk

Leveraged perps can lose the whole account, fast. The default profile limits
how much one trade can lose at its stop; it does not limit gaps, slippage or
a run of losses. The profile's daily loss figure is shown, not enforced.
There is no demonstrated edge and no return is promised. This is software,
not financial advice. You decide every trade and carry its result.

### Restricted jurisdictions

Hyperliquid's terms bar use from restricted jurisdictions, including by US
persons. The current list is in Hyperliquid's terms. pathiel does not check
where you are; staying within the rules where you live is on you.

### Your data

pathiel runs on your computer and the project runs no server, so nothing is
sent to the maintainer. No analytics, no telemetry. What does leave your
machine:

- **Hyperliquid API** (api.hyperliquid.xyz, or the testnet API): market and
  account reads, the orders you ask for, the API wallet approval you sign.
- **Public data feeds** the desk briefs read: EIA, FRED, CFTC, Congress and
  the Federal Register, prediction markets and news. An optional API key
  for one of them goes only to that feed.
- **GitHub**, only if you join the research pool: the signed statement you
  submit as a pull request.

Keys, theses, the desk journal and your config stay in `~/.pathiel`.
Details: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## Research pool (opt-in)

pathiel can grade your trades alongside everyone else's. You register your
Hyperliquid address with one signed statement; you upload nothing, since
pathiel only reads fills Hyperliquid already makes public. From the time
you join, your public fills on the pool coins (`xyz:BRENTOIL`, `xyz:CL`,
`xyz:SILVER`, `xyz:GOLD`) are graded with the same harness the project runs
on its own trades, and published on a public scoreboard at least 24 hours
late.

What you get: your own graded report (fluke or edge on your trades, with
ranges, through `get_pool_status` with `report: true`), and pool-level stats on which desks and
setups hold up across members.

What it is not: not a fee waiver, since pathiel charges no fee to anyone,
member or not, and joining never changes what you pay. No payout, refund or reward is ever
tied to your returns. Not a copy-trading feed: results are published at
least 24 hours late, never live. No edge is demonstrated by joining, or by
anything the pool's stats show.

Run `/pathiel:share` to join or leave. It shows you the exact statement
before it signs anything, and the pull request it opens for you.

Scoreboard: https://julian-dev28.github.io/pathiel/scoreboard/

### Privacy

What is public: your account address (shortened, with an explorer link),
the date you joined, your closed and graded trade counts, your graded row
(win rate, mean result in R, a label, a luck score), and pool totals that
include your trades. What is never public: anything closed in the last 24
hours, any open position, single trades, prices, sizes, dollar results,
account value, leverage, or any key.

Leaving is one more signed statement, or a request in a GitHub issue with
no signature. Coming back takes a new signed join; only trades after the
new join count, and deleting a leave file never brings an account back on
its own.

Full details, including the exact text you sign: [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md).

## FAQ

**How do I connect Claude to Hyperliquid?**
Install pathiel as a Claude Code plugin with the three lines in
[Install in 30 seconds](#install-in-30-seconds). Market data works at once
with no key; add an API wallet key to `~/.pathiel/.env.local` to trade.
Claude Desktop, Cursor and other MCP clients use the launcher or the
container described in [Other MCP clients](#other-mcp-clients). No
Anthropic API key is needed: the one model step, the desk thesis behind
`refresh_desk`, runs through your local Claude Code CLI.

**Is pathiel a Hyperliquid trading bot?**
No, and it never trades on its own. It is an MCP server that gives Claude
tools: Claude places an order when you ask for one in the session, and
Claude Code asks before each live-money call. `/loop 15m /pathiel:desk-tick oil`
re-prompts Claude on a timer, only while that session stays open.

**Can it withdraw my money?**
No. pathiel signs with an API wallet, which Hyperliquid lets trade and never
withdraw. Your master key is never stored, and pathiel needs it for nothing:
the only script that takes it revokes a builder fee approval, at a hidden
prompt in your own terminal.

**Does pathiel charge a fee?**
No. Orders carry no builder fee; you pay Hyperliquid's own trading fee
only.

**How do I practice without real money?**
Add `PATHIEL_NETWORK=testnet` to `~/.pathiel/.env.local`, create an API
wallet in the testnet app (app.hyperliquid-testnet.xyz), and reconnect
pathiel in `/mcp`. The oil desk trades WTI (`xyz:CL`) there.

**Is there an edge?**
None is demonstrated. The desk briefs are a structured, written call with
levels, not a forecast. `get_desk_record` grades every call in the open.

**How do I remove it?**
Revoke the API wallet in the Hyperliquid app (More, API), then
`claude plugin uninstall pathiel@pathiel` and delete `~/.pathiel` if you want
the keys and state gone.

## Maintainer setup

> Maintainer path: this runs mainnet with the tracked repo config (20x, whole-equity sizing). It is not the public install.

This is how the maintainer runs pathiel on his own account, from a checkout.
It is not the public install and its numbers are not the defaults.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Julian-dev28/pathiel
cd pathiel
cp .env.local.example .env.local
scripts/restart.sh          # FastAPI Desk page on http://localhost:8000/ and the log rotator
scripts/restart.sh status
```

- **MCP server.** The repo `.mcp.json` starts
  `scripts/pathiel-mcp-server.py` directly, with no install marker, so it
  runs mainnet on the tracked `.agent-config.json`. Opening a clone in
  Claude Code offers that server; accepting it is the maintainer path, not
  the public install. Other clients that want the public path register
  `scripts/pathiel-mcp`.
- **Risk profile.** The tracked config sets 20x, the whole equity per
  position less the opening fee, one position. The rules `place_bracket`
  enforces (2R minimum, stop inside half the distance to liquidation, one
  slot) hold on both paths.
- **Desk loop.** `.claude/skills/desk-tick/SKILL.md` on `/loop 15m /desk-tick oil`.
  `scripts/build_plugin_skill.py` generates the plugin copies under
  `skills/` and `agents/`; the gate fails when a copy is stale.
- **Gate.** `PATHIEL_STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q`,
  offline, run by `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` (`scripts/install_hooks.sh`
  wires it in). `scripts/mcp_tool_table.py` regenerates the tool table;
  `.venv/bin/python scripts/mcp_smoke.py` is a live, read-only MCP smoke.
- **Keys.** `scripts/preflight_secrets.py` checks the env file without
  printing it; `docs/SECRETS.md` lists every secret and how to rotate it.

More: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the code layout,
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) for the hardening checks.

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "pathiel"
dynamic = ["version"]
description = "Autonomous quant trading agent for Hyperliquid perpetual markets"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.115,<1",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30,<1",
    "httpx>=0.27,<1",
    "pydantic>=2.0",
    "pydantic_settings>=2.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
    "hyperliquid-python-sdk>=0.23.0",
    "eth-account>=0.13.0",
    "msgpack>=1.1.0",
    "prometheus-client>=0.20",
    "finlight-client==2.4.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "ruff>=0.4",
]

[project.scripts]
pathiel = "pathiel.__main__:main"

[tool.hatch.version]
path = "pathiel/__init__.py"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["pathiel"]

[tool.ruff]
# research/ (exploratory scratch, 175MB with caches) was deleted 2026-10-25;
# the vendored .agents/.forge/.qwen skill copies went 2026-10-17.
exclude = [".venv"]
line-length = 100

[tool.ruff.lint]
# Gate on pyflakes only, and mean it. F is the rule class that finds bugs rather
# than opinions: undefined names, unused imports, duplicate dict keys. It earned
# the slot on 2026-09-02, when a first run found `stop_ws_mids()` in the
# exchange client using a lock that is defined nowhere — an exported function
# that could only ever raise NameError — plus a test fixture whose duplicate
# "unlock_short" key silently dropped a live book's stop_pct.
#
# The E (pycodestyle) rules are deliberately NOT gated. Every one of them fires
# on a convention this codebase uses on purpose: E402 on the import-order
# comments that exist because `rebalancer_owned` freezes the state directory at
# import time, and E741 on `h, l, c` — which is OHLC, not an ambiguous name.
# A gate that cries wolf gets bypassed, and --no-verify is banned here.
select = ["F"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["."]
# services/*/tests too: a service whose suite is not collected is a service
# whose suite does not exist. services/auth is on every request path.
testpaths = ["tests", "services", "contracts"]
addopts = "-m 'not online and not live and not browser'"
markers = [
    "browser: drives a real Chromium via Playwright and boots a server; too slow for the commit gate, deselected by default (run with: pytest -m browser)",
    "online: exercises the live Hyperliquid public API (read-only); deselected by default (run with: pytest -m online)",
    "live: real-money e2e — places orders and calls the billable LLM; deselected by default and additionally requires PATHIEL_E2E=1 (run with: PATHIEL_E2E=1 pytest -m live)",
]

# World Monitor [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | [日本語](README.ja-JP.md) | [Русский](README.ru.md) **Real-time global intelligence dashboard** — AI-powered news aggregation, geopolitical monitoring, and infrastructure tracking in a unified situational awareness interface. [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/koala73/worldmonitor?style=social)](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/stargazers) [![License: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-AGPL%20v3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0) [![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-007ACC?style=flat&logo=typescript&logoColor=white)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/koala73/worldmonitor)](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/commits/main) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/koala73/worldmonitor?style=flat)](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/releases/latest) [![npm: worldmonitor](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/worldmonitor?logo=npm&label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/worldmonitor) [![skills.sh](https://skills.sh/b/koala73/worldmonitor)](https://skills.sh/koala73/worldmonitor)

         

       

     

Documentation  ·  Releases  ·  Contributing

![World Monitor Dashboard](docs/images/worldmonitor-7-mar-2026.jpg) ## Ways to Use It | Surface | Get it | Docs | |---------|--------|------| | **Web app** | [worldmonitor.app](https://www.worldmonitor.app) and the tech, finance, commodity, happy and energy variants | [Getting Started](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/getting-started) | | **Desktop app** (Tauri) | Windows, macOS and Linux downloads above | [Desktop App](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/desktop-app) | | **Terminal dashboard** | `npx worldmonitor` | [Terminal Dashboard](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli-dashboard) | | **CLI** | `npm install -g worldmonitor` or `brew install worldmonitor` | [Command-Line Client](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli) | | **SDKs** | Python `worldmonitor-sdk`, Ruby `worldmonitor`, Go `sdk/go` | [SDKs](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks) | | **MCP server** | `https://worldmonitor.app/mcp` | [MCP Overview](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/mcp-overview) | The terminal dashboard runs the same live data in your shell: world map, news, markets, conflict, military flights, cyber, climate, prediction markets and live TV, with mouse support and colour themes. No API key needed. ![World Monitor terminal dashboard](docs/images/tui/overview.webp) --- ## What It Does - **Curated news feeds** across global and regional categories, AI-synthesized into briefs - **Dual map engine** — 3D globe (globe.gl) and WebGL flat map (deck.gl) with a shared map-layer catalog - **Panel inventory** — concrete panel implementations across specialized variants - **Cross-stream correlation** — military, economic, disaster, and escalation signal convergence - **[Country Instability Index (CII)](https://www.worldmonitor.app/country-instability-index/)** — live CII v14 scores, bands, and approximate 24-hour movement for 31 Tier-1 countries - **Finance radar** — stock exchanges, commodities, crypto, and a market composite - **Local AI** — run everything with Ollama, no API keys required - **Site variants** from a single codebase (world, tech, finance, commodity, happy, energy) - **Native desktop app** (Tauri 2) for macOS, Windows, and Linux - **Multilingual UI** with native-language feeds and RTL support For the full feature list, architecture, data sources, and algorithms, see the **[documentation](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/documentation)**. --- ## Support Status All site variants and desktop binaries are built from a single codebase and ship from the same release process. The table below clarifies maintenance status so you know which surfaces are safe to depend on. | Surface | Status | Notes | |---------|--------|-------| | `worldmonitor.app`, `tech.`, `finance.`, `commodity.`, `happy.`, `energy.` | Stable | Public deployments built from this repo, actively maintained | | Desktop binaries (Windows / macOS Apple Silicon / macOS Intel / Linux AppImage x64 and ARM64) | Stable | One Tauri binary for every variant — install World Monitor and switch to tech, finance, commodity, energy, or happy in-app. There is deliberately no per-variant download | | `worldmonitor` npm package (terminal dashboard and CLI) | Stable | Published from [`cli/`](cli/) on every `cli-v*` tag | Issues filed against any of the above are triaged from the same backlog — see the [issues board](https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/issues) for currently-open work. --- ## Quick Start **One-line install** (self-host the full stack with Docker — dashboard, Redis, AIS relay, seeded public data): ```bash curl -fsSL https://www.worldmonitor.app/install.sh | bash ``` This clones into `./worldmonitor` (or reuses your checkout), generates the required secrets, starts the stack, and seeds data. Then open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000). Options: `--dir`, `--port`, `--no-seed`, `--no-build`, passed after `bash -s --` (see `scripts/install.sh --help`). API keys are optional. Details, production notes, and uninstall: [SELF_HOSTING.md](./SELF_HOSTING.md). **Local development** (hot-reload Vite server): Requires Node.js 24, the version pinned in `.nvmrc`. Distribution packages are often older. Debian 12 and Raspberry Pi OS ship Node.js 18 with npm 9.2.0, where `npm install` stops with `Invalid comparator: file:vendor/braces`. Install Node.js 24 with [nvm](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm) (`nvm install` inside the checkout reads `.nvmrc`) or from [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org/en/download). ```bash git clone https://github.com/koala73/worldmonitor.git cd worldmonitor npm install npm run dev ``` Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) (override the port with `DEV_PORT` in `.env.local`). The app runs with no environment variables. Feature-specific data sources may require credentials. See `.env.example` for the full list. For variant-specific development: ```bash npm run dev:tech # tech.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:finance # finance.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:commodity # commodity.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:happy # happy.worldmonitor.app npm run dev:energy # energy.worldmonitor.app ``` See the **[self-hosting guide](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/getting-started)** for deployment options (Vercel, Docker, static). --- ## Tech Stack | Category | Technologies | |----------|-------------| | **Frontend** | Vanilla TypeScript, Vite, globe.gl + Three.js, deck.gl + MapLibre GL | | **Desktop** | Tauri 2 (Rust) with Node.js sidecar | | **AI/ML** | Ollama / OpenRouter, Transformers.js (browser-side) | | **API Contracts** | Protocol Buffers and sebuf HTTP annotations | | **Deployment** | Vercel Edge Functions, Railway relay, Tauri, PWA | | **Caching** | Redis (Upstash), 3-tier cache, CDN, service worker | Full stack details in the **[architecture docs](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/architecture)**. --- ## Programmatic Access World Monitor is built for agents and scripts as well as browsers: - **MCP server** — `https://worldmonitor.app/mcp` (Streamable HTTP). Public `tools/list`; `tools/call` authenticates with a `X-WorldMonitor-Key` header or OAuth. The server also publishes its Agent Skills through the draft `io.modelcontextprotocol/skills` extension (`skills/list`, `skills/get`, and `skill://…` resource reads). - **Google Antigravity and Gemini listing preparation** — install the bundled Antigravity plugin (`.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json` + `mcp_config.json`) with `agy plugin install ./worldmonitor`. Gemini custom apps and Connected Apps sign in through Google's OAuth callbacks. See [Gemini and Antigravity](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/gemini-antigravity). - **REST API** — base `https://api.worldmonitor.app`, described by the [OpenAPI spec](https://worldmonitor.app/openapi.yaml). - **CLI** — the official [`worldmonitor`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/worldmonitor) npm package (source in [`cli/`](cli/)). Run it with no arguments in a terminal for the [terminal dashboard](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/cli-dashboard): ```sh npx worldmonitor tools # run ad-hoc — list every MCP tool (no key needed) npm install -g worldmonitor # or install the `worldmonitor` (alias `wm`) command brew install worldmonitor # or install it with Homebrew worldmonitor risk IR --api-key wm_xxx ``` - **SDKs** — official zero-dependency client libraries mirroring the CLI: Python [`worldmonitor-sdk`](https://pypi.org/project/worldmonitor-sdk/) (source in [`sdk/python/`](sdk/python/)), Ruby [`worldmonitor`](https://rubygems.org/gems/worldmonitor) ([`sdk/ruby/`](sdk/ruby/)), Go [`github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go`](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/koala73/worldmonitor/sdk/go) ([`sdk/go/`](sdk/go/)). Guide: [worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/sdks). Agent discovery files: [`llms.txt`](https://worldmonitor.app/llms.txt) · [agent-skills manifest](https://worldmonitor.app/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json) · [api-catalog](https://worldmonitor.app/.well-known/api-catalog). Get an API key at [worldmonitor.app/pro](https://www.worldmonitor.app/pro). --- ## Flight Data Flight data provided graciously by [Wingbits](https://wingbits.com?utm_source=worldmonitor&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=worldmonitor), the most advanced ADS-B flight data solution. --- ## Supported By World Monitor's web app and API run on [Vercel](https://vercel.com?utm_source=worldmonitor&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=worldmonitor). Thank you to Vercel for their generous support of the project. --- ## Data Sources WorldMonitor aggregates attributed upstream sources across geopolitics, finance, energy, climate, aviation, cyber, military, infrastructure, and news intelligence. Curated feeds and freshness-tracked source groups are published in the full [data sources catalog](https://www.worldmonitor.app/docs/data-sources), with provider, feed-tier, license-posture, and collection-method details. --- ## Contributing Contributions welcome! name: Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

# A superseded PR run owes nobody a verdict. Branch protection and
# deploy-gate.sh both evaluate the head SHA only. Letting it finish burned
# 59% of this workflow's runs on dead commits and queued the live commit
# behind them. Cancellation is pull_request-only. A push to main still owes
# the deploy gate a verdict, and `github.run_id` gives it a group of one so
# nothing can evict it (#8443).
concurrency:
  group: test-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      code: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.code }}
      browser: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.browser }}
      digest: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.digest }}
      validation: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.validation }}
      umami: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.umami }}
      consumer_prices: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.consumer_prices }}
      desktop_config: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.desktop_config }}
      desktop_rust: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.desktop_rust }}
      zapier: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.zapier }}
      durations_key: ${{ steps.durations.outputs.cache-matched-key }}
    steps:
      # The newest shard duration estimates CI has measured, found once per run
      # so every unit shard partitions the inventory from the same file: each
      # shard computes the whole partition and keeps its part, so two shards
      # reading different estimates would drop or repeat test files. The shards
      # save new entries as they finish. A PR run finds its own newest entry or
      # main's. No entry, or a failed lookup, leaves the key empty and every
      # shard falls back to scripts/shared/data-test-durations.json.
      - name: Find the newest measured test durations
        id: durations
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/data-test-durations/durations.json
          # A key nothing is saved under: actions/cache prefix-matches the
          # primary key before restore-keys, so a run_id here would make a
          # re-run of an old run prefer its own stale entry over the newest.
          key: data-test-durations-v1-lookup
          restore-keys: data-test-durations-v1-
          lookup-only: true
      - id: diff
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          # Specialized jobs (desktop-rust, umami, digest, …) are path-filtered
          # on PRs. Do the same on push to main. Forcing them true here used to
          # compile the Tauri crate and rebuild Umami images on every merge —
          # weather, news, embed — which is not a desktop or analytics gate.
          # Fail open (run everything) only when we cannot see the file list:
          # a zero parent SHA, a compare error, or GitHub's 300-file cap.
          emit_all_true() {
            echo "browser=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "code=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "digest=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "validation=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "umami=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "consumer_prices=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "desktop_config=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "desktop_rust=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "zapier=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          }
          ZERO=0000000000000000000000000000000000000000
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "push" ]; then
            BEFORE="${{ github.event.before }}"
            if [ -z "$BEFORE" ] || [ "$BEFORE" = "$ZERO" ]; then
              echo "No usable parent SHA; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
            if ! COMPARE_JSON=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/compare/${BEFORE}...${{ github.sha }}"); then
              echo "Compare API failed; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
            if ! FILES_JSON=$(jq -ce '.files | arrays' <<< "$COMPARE_JSON"); then
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
            FILE_COUNT=$(jq 'length' <<< "$FILES_JSON")
            if [ "$FILE_COUNT" -ge 300 ]; then
              echo "Compare listing is truncated at 300 files; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            if ! PR_JSON=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ github.event.number }}") ||
               ! FILES_JSON=$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/pulls/${{ github.event.number }}/files" --paginate --slurp | jq -ce 'add | arrays'); then
              echo "PR file lookup failed; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
            FILE_COUNT=$(jq 'length' <<< "$FILES_JSON")
            if ! jq -e --arg head "${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}" \
              --arg base "${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}" --argjson count "$FILE_COUNT" \
              '.head.sha == $head and .base.sha == $base and .changed_files == $count and $count < 3000' <<< "$PR_JSON" >/dev/null; then
              echo "PR metadata moved or its file list is incomplete; running every Test job."
              emit_all_true
              exit 0
            fi
          fi
          # Include both sides of renames. A deleted file is still an input.
          # Refuse line-delimiter characters before passing paths to awk.
          if [ "$FILE_COUNT" -eq 0 ] || ! FILES=$(jq -er '
            [.[] | .filename, (.previous_filename // empty)]
            | if all(.[]; type == "string" and length > 0 and (explode | all(. != 0 and . != 10 and . != 13)))
              then .[] else error("invalid path listing") end
          ' <<< "$FILES_JSON"); then
            echo "Unusable file list; running every Test job."
            emit_all_true
            exit 0
          fi
          CODE=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^docs\/research\/seo-ai-visibility\// { count++; next }
            # Committed resilience acceptance artifacts are docs-path data that
            # tests/dry-run-resilience-education-flip.test.mts validates —
            # recomputing gates, checking provenance, and rejecting a
            # self-declared verdict. That validator lives in the `unit` job, so
            # without this rule the guard skips on exactly the PR that commits
            # an artifact and can only ever fire on unrelated changes.
            /^docs\/snapshots\/resilience-.*-acceptance-.*\.json$/ { count++; next }
            # Per-service OpenAPI specs are generated machine artifacts consumed
            # by tests/openapi-filter-param-schemas.test.mjs, which enumerates
            # every JSON spec. Keep the JSON/YAML siblings on the same `unit`
            # job when a PR changes only docs/api output (#6650).
            /^docs\/api\/[^\/]+Service\.openapi\.(json|yaml)$/ { count++; next }
            # The generated OpenAPI bundle sits under docs/ but is the INPUT to
            # the served public/openapi.json. Its <= 950,000-byte scanner guard
            # (tests/openapi-json-dedup.test.mjs) and the capacity report that
            # tracks the approach to it both run in `unit`, so without this
            # carve-out a PR that only regenerates the bundle sets code=false
            # and skips the one gate that measures the artifact it changed
            # (#6558).
            /^docs\/api\/worldmonitor\.openapi\.yaml$/ { count++; next }
            # The Data Coverage block in public/ai-search.md is generated from
            # the inventory registries, and the docs-stats volatile-claim gate
            # exempts that block precisely because
            # tests/ai-search-product-facts.test.mjs fails when it drifts from
            # the generator. That test lives in the `unit` job, so without this
            # rule the only gate on a fabricated figure skips on exactly the PR
            # that edits the file (#6038). NOTE: no apostrophes in this awk
            # program - it is single-quoted in the shell, so one would end it.
            /^public\/ai-search\.md$/ { count++; next }
            # A published ranking snapshot is the source of the ranked-country
            # figure and captured date in public/ai-search.md. A snapshot-only
            # PR would otherwise set code=false, skip the byte test, and land a
            # snapshot whose figures the committed page no longer matches -
            # surfacing later as a confusing failure on an unrelated PR.
            /^docs\/snapshots\/resilience-ranking-[0-9-]+\.json$/ { count++; next }
            /^blog-site\/src\/content\/blog\/.*\.md$/ { count++; next }
            /^blog-site\/src\/content\/guides\/.*\.md$/ { count++; next }
            # public/home.md is the agent-mode homepage and the residue guard
            # asserts it links the comparison hub (#7746). Without this rule a
            # home.md-only PR sets code=false and that guard never runs.
            /^public\/home\.md$/ { count++; next }
            /\.md$/ { next }
            /^docs\// { next }
            # A src-tauri node suite is run by sidecar and policed by
            # tests/package-test-command-paths.test.mjs inside unit; both are
            # gated on code, so the exclusion below must not swallow it (#7772).
            /^src-tauri\/.*\.test\.(mjs|mts|cjs|js|ts|tsx)$/ { count++; next }
            /^src-tauri\// && $0 !~ /^src-tauri\/sidecar\// && $0 !~ /^src-tauri\/.*\.json$/ { next }
            /^CHANGELOG\.md$/ { next }
            /^LICENSE$/ { next }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/docker-publish\.yml$/ { next }
            { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "code=$( [ "$CODE" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          ZAPIER=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^integrations\/zapier\// { count++; next }
            /^shared\/event-triggers\.json$/ { count++; next }
            /^tests\/package-test-command-paths\.test\.mjs$/ { count++; next }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/test\.yml$/ { count++; next }
            /^\.github\/scripts\/deploy-gate\.sh$/ { count++; next }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "zapier=$( [ "$ZAPIER" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Only proven non-browser inputs may skip this job. New paths run it
          # until their owner can establish that they cannot affect the smoke.
          BROWSER=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^(src\/|api\/|server\/|shared\/|public\/|pro-test\/|e2e\/)/ { count++; next }
            /^docs\// { next }
            /^tests\/.*\.test\.(mjs|mts)$/ { next }
            /^scripts\/(audit-railway-watch-paths|run-railway-registry-sync|railway-services)\.(mjs|json)$/ { next }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/(railway-registry-sync|seed-freshness)\.yml$/ { next }
            /^\.husky\// { next }
            /\.md$/ || /^LICENSE$/ { next }
            /^src-tauri\// { next }
            { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "browser=$( [ "$BROWSER" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # digest-image job: build Dockerfile.digest-notifications when a PR
          # touches its inputs (scripts/, shared/, server/_shared/, api/, the
          # Dockerfile itself, or the root package manifest). Catches the
          # cross-directory-import + native-dep breakage class documented in
          # tests/dockerfile-digest-notifications-imports.test.mjs.
          DIGEST=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^(scripts\/|shared\/|server\/_shared\/|api\/|\.dockerignore$|Dockerfile\.digest-notifications|package\.json|package-lock\.json)/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "digest=$( [ "$DIGEST" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # resilience-validation-smoke job: run the no-secrets artifact/schema
          # and script-contract gate when the validation bundle, its Dockerfile,
          # its committed artifacts, or its focused tests change.
          VALIDATION=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^Dockerfile\.seed-bundle-resilience-validation$/ { count++ }
            /^docs\/methodology\/country-resilience-index\/validation\// { count++ }
            /^package\.json$/ || /^package-lock\.json$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/benchmark-resilience-external\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/backtest-resilience-outcomes\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/validate-resilience-sensitivity\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/seed-bundle-resilience-validation\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^scripts\/_bundle-runner\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            /^tests\/(resilience-validation-artifacts-schema|benchmark-resilience-external|backtest-resilience-outcomes|resilience-sensitivity-v2|seed-bundle-resilience-validation)\.test\.(mjs|mts)$/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "validation=$( [ "$VALIDATION" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Umami's database race cannot be covered by the normal no-Docker
          # unit suite. Run a real PostgreSQL gate only when its managed image,
          # migration, patch, or focused tests change. Do not trigger on every
          # Test workflow edit: unit already pins the job shape, and rebuilding
          # two Umami images is the cost that made this look like a per-PR tax.
          UMAMI=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^\.dockerignore$/ { count++ }
            /^Dockerfile\.umami$/ { count++ }
            /^Dockerfile\.umami-retention$/ { count++ }
            /^docker\/umami\// { count++ }
            /^scripts\/umami-retention\.sql$/ { count++ }
            /^tests\/umami-(runtime-remediation\.test|postgres-integration|runtime-write-probe)\.mjs$/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "umami=$( [ "$UMAMI" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Consumer-prices-core has its own lockfile and Vitest suite, so run
          # it whenever package code, tests, or its CI definition changes.
          CONSUMER_PRICES=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^consumer-prices-core\// { count++ }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/test\.yml$/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "consumer_prices=$( [ "$CONSUMER_PRICES" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Desktop drift gates (#5902). The `code` filter above deliberately
          # skips src-tauri/ (non-sidecar), so before these outputs existed a
          # Rust/Tauri-config change ran zero PR CI and desktop breakage
          # surfaced only at the next release build — months later.
          # Any `src-tauri/**/*.json` is carved back into `code`:
          # tests/desktop-one-binary-model.test.mjs asserts on the set of Tauri
          # bundle configs (#5908) and runs in `unit`. Without the carve-out,
          # adding a per-variant config would skip its own gate — and the
          # carve-out covers every JSON path, not just `tauri*.conf.json`, so a
          # config parked at e.g. `src-tauri/profiles/commodity.json` cannot
          # sneak past it either.
          # The sidecar handler bundle build lives in the `unit` job (gated on
          # `code`), NOT here: the bundled api/{domain}/v1/[rpc].ts handlers
          # import from src/ and server/ via the @/ alias, so the bundle's
          # real input graph is the whole code surface, and `code` is the
          # filter that already tracks it.
          DESKTOP_CONFIG=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^src-tauri\// { count++; next }
            /^package\.json$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/repack-linux-appimage\.sh$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/prefetch-appimage-tools\.sh$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/fetch-with-retry\.sh$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/check-desktop-build-env\.mjs$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/sync-desktop-version\.mjs$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/check-rust-security-floors\.mjs$/ { count++; next }
            /^scripts\/download-node\.sh$/ { count++; next }
            /^\.github\/workflows\/.*\.ya?ml$/ { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "desktop_config=$( [ "$DESKTOP_CONFIG" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          # Compile the Tauri crate only when the crate itself changes.
          # Workflow edits are covered by desktop-config (cheap) and by the
          # unit contract that pins this job's shape — they must not pay
          # cargo test --locked (45 min budget) the way test.yml used to.
          DESKTOP_RUST=$(printf '%s\n' "$FILES" | awk '
            /^src-tauri\/sidecar\// { next }
            /^src-tauri\// { count++ }
            END { print count + 0 }
          ')
          echo "desktop_rust=$( [ "$DESKTOP_RUST" -gt 0 ] && echo true || echo false )" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  zapier:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.zapier == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    defaults:
      run:
        working-directory: integrations/zapier
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: integrations/zapier/package-lock.json
      - run: npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
      - run: npm test

  docs-stats:
    # Always-on: derives build-owned inventory facts and validates fixed or
    # semantic documentation contracts. Runs on every PR/push (docs-only PRs
    # set changes.code=false and skip `unit`, so this must not gate on it).
    # Docs date generation uses the existing YAML parser for OpenAPI pages.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          # Docs page dates derive from git history; a shallow checkout would
          # resolve every file to HEAD instead of its last content change.
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - uses: ./.github/actions/install-root-deps
      - name: Generate and validate build-owned inventory facts
        run: |
          node scripts/generate-inventory-facts.mjs
          node scripts/generate-inventory-facts.mjs --check
      - name: Doc claims match code
        run: node scripts/docs-stats.mjs --check
      - name: Generate and validate docs page dates for this revision
        run: |
          node scripts/generate-docs-page-dates.mjs
          node scripts/generate-docs-page-dates.mjs --check
          node --test tests/docs-page-dates.test.mjs
      - name: Every English docs page has a zh translation
        # Docs-only PRs skip the unit shards, so without this step a missing
        # docs/zh mirror surfaces only as a red main after merge (#8968).
        run: node --test tests/docs-i18n-parity.test.mjs
      - name: Published internal links resolve without redirects
        run: node --import tsx --test tests/internal-link-redirects.test.mjs
      - name: Derived files are current (npm run generate)
        # Every committed generated file with a freshness check: product facts,
        # llms.txt, AI search, source attribution, the homepage teaser strip,
        # the entitlement crosswalk (exit 2 there means a missing source, and
        # its output is printed), catalogs and notices. Always-on because a
        # docs-only PR skips `unit`, yet docs feed several of these. zh-TW is
        # skipped here (no OpenCC) and checked in unit-built-output.
        run: node scripts/generate-derived.mjs --check

  unit-shards:
    name: unit-shard (${{ matrix.shard }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # Three shards, not two (#7805): after #7769 split the browser job,
        # unit-shard (2) became the Test wall at 5m45s, of which ~2 min is
        # setup and builds every shard repeated and ~3 min is test:data. The
        # builds now run once in unit-built-output. Four, not three: the
        # test:data step saturates the runner's CPU, so a fourth runner is the
        # cheapest way to get more parallelism. Three paired benchmark runs took
        # the slowest shard from 236-269s to 176-186s. Five, not four: after
        # the other Test jobs got faster the unit shards (~207s) were the
        # slowest job again; on the same runner image the slowest test:data
        # step took 123s at five shards and 138-155s at four (bench run
        # 40083951067), and raising concurrency to 6 or 8 did not help. The
        # sharder balances by measured durations and is generic in the count,
        # so the denominator on the test:data step below is the only other
        # place this number lives. tests/ci-test-selection.test.mjs pins that
        # denominator to this matrix's length, and tests/data-test-shards.test.mjs
        # reads the matrix and proves the shards together run the inventory
        # exactly once.
        shard: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          # Suites such as crawlable-corpus and docs-page-dates read commit
          # history (last-modified dates, base drift), so the graph stays
          # complete. Blobless: file contents outside the checked-out tree are
          # fetched only if a suite asks for one, which cuts the clone ~3x.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      # tests/pizzint-history-redis.test.mjs is the only place the PizzINT
      # archive's Lua runs against a real server: the relay harness stubs the
      # EVAL and the proxy command-gate test only matches the script TEXT. That
      # suite self-skips when the binaries are absent, so without this step the
      # capacity refusal, newest-capture-wins compare, EXPIREAT and atomic
      # seed-meta update were verified by nothing in CI. ubuntu-latest does not
      # ship redis-server, so every shard installs it. The action installs
      # from a package cache with dpkg (a slow mirror used to put 24-58s on
      # the slowest shard), refreshes the stale index only on a miss, and
      # fails the shard if the binaries are missing.
      #
      # It runs before install-root-deps, not beside it: both composite actions
      # use actions/cache, and when a job does not reference it at the top
      # level, a parallel group made the runner download it twice at once and
      # one copy failed ("Could not find file .../actions/cache/<sha>/examples.md",
      # run 39936254975). This job now references actions/cache/restore and
      # save directly, so the runner fetches them at setup; keep the steps
      # sequential anyway.
      - name: Install Redis for the archive Lua suite
        uses: ./.github/actions/install-redis
      - uses: ./.github/actions/install-root-deps
      # The two nested trees are restored whole, like the root tree. Restoring
      # setup-node's npm download cache for them cost 4-9s per shard, and the
      # two installs another 7-10s. The key hashes every file that decides
      # their contents; bump the version when an install command below (or
      # ci:blog-site in package.json) changes.
      - name: Restore blog-site and scripts/ dependencies
        id: nested-deps
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: |
            blog-site/node_modules
            scripts/node_modules
          key: nested-deps-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-node24-${{ hashFiles('blog-site/package.json', 'blog-site/package-lock.json', 'blog-site/.npmrc', 'scripts/package.json', 'scripts/package-lock.json', 'scripts/.npmrc', '.npmrc', 'vendor/http-cache-semantics/**') }}
      - name: Install blog-site deps for SEO contract tests
        # Unit-only nested install; keeps postinstall free of blog-site.
        # tests/dependency-backports.test.mjs checks the patched source Astro
        # installs, and skips that check when blog-site/node_modules is absent.
        if: steps.nested-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm run ci:blog-site
      - name: Install scripts/ deps for the seeder link check
        # Railway seeders install scripts/package-lock.json, not the root tree.
        # tests/nixpacks-seeder-import-graph.test.mjs links their named package
        # imports against this install (#9608 shipped an undici 8 import to an
        # undici 7 container with every suite green). WM_EXPECT_SCRIPTS_DEPS
        # below fails the shard if a restored tree is missing it.
        if: steps.nested-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm ci --prefix scripts --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund
      - name: Save blog-site and scripts/ dependencies
        if: steps.nested-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: |
            blog-site/node_modules
            scripts/node_modules
          key: ${{ steps.nested-deps.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      # The exact entry the changes job found, with no fallback key: a shard
      # that read anything else would partition differently from the others,
      # so a miss fails the shard instead.
      - name: Restore the newest measured durations
        if: needs.changes.outputs.durations_key != ''
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/data-test-durations/durations.json
          key: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.durations_key }}
          fail-on-cache-miss: true
      - name: Data tests without built output
        # No build here: the unit-built-output job builds dist/ and public/pro/
        # once and runs every suite that names them. The marker stays set, so a
        # guarded suite that lands in a shard fails instead of skipping.
        env:
          WM_EXPECT_BUILT_OUTPUT: '1'
          WM_EXPECT_SCRIPTS_DEPS: '1'
          DURATIONS_KEY: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.durations_key }}
        run: npm run test:data -- --built-output=exclude --shard=${{ matrix.shard }}/5 --concurrency=4 --timings=${{ runner.temp }}/data-test-timings.jsonl ${DURATIONS_KEY:+--durations="$HOME/data-test-durations/durations.json"}
      # The next run's estimates, saved whether the tests passed or not: a cache
      # saved only by green runs goes stale exactly while main is red. The next
      # run reads only the newest entry, so if every shard saved, whichever
      # finished last would win and the same shard could win every run. One
      # shard saves per run instead: the one after the shard that saved the
      # entry this run restored (the key ends in its number), so the turn
      # rotates within each cache scope, a PR's or main's. It moves its own
      # files halfway to what they measured; if its tests failed it saves the
      # estimates unchanged, so a red shard passes the turn on instead of
      # holding it. Neither step can fail the shard.
      - name: Blend this shard's timings into the estimates
        id: blend-durations
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        continue-on-error: true
        env:
          DURATIONS_KEY: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.durations_key }}
          SHARD: ${{ matrix.shard }}
          SHARD_TOTAL: ${{ strategy.job-total }}
        run: |
          last=0
          [[ "$DURATIONS_KEY" =~ -([0-9]+)$ ]] && last=${BASH_REMATCH[1]}
          saver=$(( last % SHARD_TOTAL + 1 ))
          if (( saver != SHARD )); then
            echo "Shard $saver saves this run's estimates, not this one."
            exit 0
          fi
          previous=scripts/shared/data-test-durations.json
          [ -n "$DURATIONS_KEY" ] && previous="$HOME/data-test-durations/durations.json"
          next="$RUNNER_TEMP/next-durations.json"
          node scripts/refresh-data-test-durations.mjs --blend --previous "$previous" --output "$next" "$RUNNER_TEMP/data-test-timings.jsonl" || true
          [ -f "$next" ] || cp "$previous" "$next"
          mkdir -p "$HOME/data-test-durations"
          mv "$next" "$HOME/data-test-durations/durations.json"
          echo "updated=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - name: Save the estimates for the next run
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.blend-durations.outputs.updated == 'true' }}
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: ~/data-test-durations/durations.json
          key: data-test-durations-v1-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-${{ matrix.shard }}
      - name: Upload data test timings
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6
        with:
          name: data-test-timings-${{ matrix.shard }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/data-test-timings.jsonl
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14

  # Everything the shards would otherwise repeat three times: the /pro and
  # dashboard builds, the bundle budgets that read them, the suites that need
  # built output (scripts/run-data-tests.mjs --built-output=only), and the
  # tree-wide checks that do not depend on a shard.
  unit-built-output:
    timeout-minutes: 15
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
        with:
          # The health-probe cutover gate compares the exact PR base with the
          # candidate tree. A shallow checkout would make that gate vacuous.
          # Blobless like the unit shards: the gate reads one blob
          # (api/health.js at the base), fetched on demand.
          fetch-depth: 0
          filter: blob:none
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - uses: ./.github/actions/install-root-deps
      # Like the unit shards' nested-deps cache: the two nested trees are
      # restored whole. Before, setup-node restored the npm download cache for
      # all three lockfiles (6-9s, most of it the root's), and the two installs
      # still took 3s (blog-site) and 12s (pro-test). The key hashes every
      # file that decides their contents (both trees link packages from
      # vendor/); bump the version when an install command below, ci:blog-site,
      # or the install half of build:pro in package.json changes.
      - name: Restore blog-site and pro-test dependencies
        id: built-output-deps
        uses: actions/cache/restore@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: |
            blog-site/node_modules
            pro-test/node_modules
          key: built-output-deps-v1-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-node24-${{ hashFiles('blog-site/package.json', 'blog-site/package-lock.json', 'blog-site/.npmrc', 'pro-test/package.json', 'pro-test/package-lock.json', 'pro-test/.npmrc', '.npmrc', 'vendor/**') }}
      - name: Install blog-site deps
        if: steps.built-output-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm run ci:blog-site
      - name: Install /pro deps
        # The install half of build:pro; the build step below runs the other.
        if: steps.built-output-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        env:
          npm_config_allow_scripts: ''
        run: npm --prefix pro-test ci --prefer-offline
      - name: Save blog-site and pro-test dependencies
        if: steps.built-output-deps.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: |
            blog-site/node_modules
            pro-test/node_modules
          key: ${{ steps.built-output-deps.outputs.cache-primary-key }}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0 # v7.1.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: zh-TW catalogues reproduce from their Simplified source (#6555)
        # The zh-TW catalogues are generated from zh.json, not translated from
        # en.json, so the EN baseline in translate-locales.mjs is the wrong
        # instrument for them and reports them separately. That leaves this as
        # the only check that fails when zh.json moves and nobody reran the
        # generator — without it, key-existence stays green while the values
        # rot, which is the #5645 blindspot on this catalogue.
        #
        # Version-pinned deliberately: a different OpenCC build shifts terms no
        # override pins, and reporting both catalogues stale at once is the
        # intended loud failure rather than a silent reformat.
        run: |
          pip install opencc-python-reimplemented==0.1.7
          python3 scripts/convert-zh-tw.py --check
      - name: Enforce health-probe cutovers
        env:
          # NOT github.event.pull_request.base.sha. GitHub pins that SHA when the
          # PR is opened and never advances it as main moves, but actions/checkout
          # builds refs/pull/N/merge — this PR merged onto main's CURRENT tip. So
          # the pinned SHA diffs today's tree against a base that can be weeks old,
          # and every probe added to main after the PR opened reads as brand-new
          # on every run, re-litigating a cutover the PR never touched. That stays
          # invisible until the probe's acknowledgement is legitimately pruned —
          # then the PR fails outright demanding an entry nobody should restore,
          # owned by an issue that is already closed (#7021 on tpsMci/#7035).
          #
          # The merge commit's FIRST parent is the base tip this tree was merged
          # onto, so it tracks what is actually under test. The pre-push hook
          # compares against origin/main for the same reason.
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          PUSH_BEFORE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$BASE_REF" ]; then
            if git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD^2 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              base="$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)"
            else
              # Unmergeable PR: checkout fell back to the head commit, whose
              # first parent is the PR's own history, not the base branch.
              base="origin/$BASE_REF"
            fi
          else
            base="$PUSH_BEFORE"
          fi
          echo "health-probe cutover base: $base"
          node --import tsx scripts/check-health-probe-cutovers.mts "$base"
      - name: OpenAPI bundle capacity (#6558)
        # The <= 950,000-byte scanner guard lives in
        # tests/openapi-json-dedup.test.mjs and stays the gate. This step
        # publishes what that guard is silent about on the way to the wall:
        # served bytes, remaining headroom, and how many more operations fit.
        # The last three crossings were each discovered by a red build on
        # whichever PR happened to be last in line; the number belongs in front
        # of a reviewer before that.
        #
        # Exits nonzero only when the artifact is over budget or could not be
        # measured at all — a breached reserve warns, because a second hard
        # failure at the same wall would just be the same red build one commit
        # earlier. Placed before the suite on purpose: an over-budget artifact
        # fails test:data anyway, and failing here costs 30s instead of 10min
        # while the upload step below still publishes the breakdown.
        #
        # Written to RUNNER_TEMP, not the workspace: a CI-only artifact dropped
        # in the repo root is untracked state that a later `git status` gate
        # would trip over.
        run: node scripts/openapi-capacity-report.mjs --out "$RUNNER_TEMP/openapi-capacity.json"
      - name: Upload OpenAPI capacity report
        # `!cancelled()` rather than `always()`: an over-budget run is exactly
        # when the breakdown is worth reading, and a cancelled job has nothing
        # to say. run_attempt in the name because upload-artifact v6 rejects a
        # duplicate name within a run, which collides on the re-run someone
        # starts to chase the failure.
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6
        with:
          name: openapi-capacity-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/openapi-capacity.json
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Build and verify buying guides
        run: |
          npm --prefix blog-site run build
          npm --prefix blog-site run verify:guides
      - name: Build /pro artifacts for built-output tests
        # public/pro/ stopped being committed in #6898, so the suites that read
        # it need the same treatment dist/ already gets. Ordered before the
        # dashboard build to mirror production: root `vite build` copies
        # public/ into dist/, so /pro must exist by then. This is the build
        # half of build:pro; its install half is the cached step above.
        run: npm --prefix pro-test run build
      - name: Build dashboard artifacts for built-output tests
        run: VITE_VARIANT=full ./node_modules/.bin/vite build
      - name: Client bundle size budget (#7111, #7119)
        # The dashboard JS payload grew +151 KB in five weeks with no CI
        # signal. Compares the build above against the committed snapshots in
        # scripts/shared/bundle-budgets*.json; on an intended size change run
        # the matching `npm run bundle:budgets*` command against the same build
        # and commit the diff. Ordered before the suite so a budget breach costs
        # seconds, not the full test:data run.
        run: |
          npm run bundle:check
          npm run bundle:check:pro
          npm run bundle:check:embed
      - run: WM_EXPECT_BUILT_OUTPUT=1 npm run test:data -- --built-output=only --concurrency=4 --timings=${{ runner.temp }}/data-test-timings.jsonl
      - name: Upload data test timings
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@b7c566a772e6b6bfb58ed0dc250532a479d7789f # v6
        with:
          name: data-test-timings-built-output-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/data-test-timings.jsonl
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 14
      - name: Edge function bundle check
        # Shared checker with caller-specific profiles. Tracked files are the
        # deployable contract, so ignored Node sidecar bundles left by local
        # builds are never inputs.
        run: node scripts/check-edge-function-bundles.mjs --caller=ci
      - name: Sidecar handler bundles build (#5902)
        # The desktop sidecar loads esbuild-bundled api/{domain}/v1/[rpc].js
        # handlers whose import graph spans src/ and server/ (via the @/
        # alias) — before this step, that build ran only inside release
        # builds, so a bundle-breaking change surfaced months later. The
        # count assertion guards the vacuous-pass case: the build script
        # exits 0 when its glob finds zero entry points, so "green" must
        # also mean "every discovered domain actually produced a bundle".
        run: |
          node scripts/build-sidecar-sebuf.mjs
          node scripts/build-sidecar-handlers.mjs
          node -e '
            const { readdirSync, existsSync } = require("node:fs");
            const domains = readdirSync("api", { withFileTypes: true })
              .filter((d) => d.isDirectory() && !["[domain]", "[[...path]]"].includes(d.name))
              .filter((d) => existsSync(`api/${d.name}/v1/[rpc].ts`))
              .map((d) => d.name);
            const missing = domains.filter((d) => !existsSync(`api/${d}/v1/[rpc].js`));
            if (domains.length === 0) {
              console.error("::error::sidecar handler build found ZERO api/{domain}/v1/[rpc].ts entry points — the discovery glob is broken (vacuous pass)");
              process.exit(1);
            }
            if (missing.length > 0) {
              console.error(`::error::sidecar handler build produced no bundle for: ${missing.join(", ")}`);
              process.exit(1);
            }
            console.log(`sidecar handler bundles ok: ${domains.length} domains`);
          '
      - name: Desktop build env parity (#5905)
        # Twin of the desktop-config leg: here it fires when src/ gains a new
        # import.meta.env.VITE_ read (code=true), forcing the author to
        # classify it for desktop builds before it can silently miss them.
        run: node scripts/check-desktop-build-env.mjs

  unit:
    needs: [changes, unit-shards, unit-built-output]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 2
    steps:
      - name: Require every selected unit shard
        env:
          CHANGES_RESULT: ${{ needs.changes.result }}
          CODE_CHANGED: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.code }}
          SHARDS_RESULT: ${{ needs.unit-shards.result }}
          BUILT_OUTPUT_RESULT: ${{ needs.unit-built-output.result }}
        run: |
          if [ "$CHANGES_RESULT" = success ] && {
            { [ "$CODE_CHANGED" = true ] && [ "$SHARDS_RESULT" = success ] && [ "$BUILT_OUTPUT_RESULT" = success ]; } ||
            { [ "$CODE_CHANGED" = false ] && [ "$SHARDS_RESULT" = skipped ] && [ "$BUILT_OUTPUT_RESULT" = skipped ]; }
          }; then
            echo "All selected unit shards passed."
          else
            echo "Unit shards did not satisfy the change selection."
            exit 1
          fi

  consumer-prices:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.consumer_prices == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: 'npm'
          cache-dependency-path: consumer-prices-core/package-lock.json
      - uses: ./.github/actions/install-redis
      - run: npm ci --prefix consumer-prices-core
      - run: npm test --prefix consumer-prices-core

  umami-postgres:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.umami == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17-alpine@sha256:742f40ea20b9ff2ff31db5458d127452988a2164df9e17441e191f3b72252193
        env:
          POSTGRES_DB: umami_integration
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready --username=postgres --dbname=umami_integration"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - name: Install PostgreSQL client
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install --yes postgresql-client
      - name: Build managed Umami images
        run: |
          docker build --file Dockerfile.umami --tag worldmonitor/umami:ci .
          docker build --file Dockerfile.umami-retention --tag worldmonitor/umami-retention:ci .
      - name: Exercise Umami migration and concurrent upserts
        env:
          UMAMI_TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/umami_integration
        run: node tests/umami-postgres-integration.mjs
      - name: Probe the running image's write path (identify, concurrent upsert, event)
        env:
          UMAMI_TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/umami_integration
        run: node tests/umami-runtime-write-probe.mjs

  sidecar:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.code == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - uses: ./.github/actions/install-root-deps
      - run: npm run test:sidecar

      # The downloader verifies the release signature and checksum. The cache
      # holds only a runtime that passed that check, keyed on the script that
      # pins the version, so a hit skips three uncached, unretried fetches
      # (one failed run 40668904151).
      - name: Restore the shipped Node.js runtime
        id: shipped-node
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        with:
          path: src-tauri/sidecar/node
          key: shipped-node-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-${{ hashFiles('scripts/download-node.sh') }}

      - name: Download the shipped Node.js runtime
        if: steps.shipped-node.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: |
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            bash scripts/download-node.sh --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu && exit 0
            echo "::warning::shipped runtime download failed (attempt $attempt)"
            sleep $((attempt * 10))
          done
          exit 1

      # The desktop app loads these bundles, not the api/ sources the suite
      # imports. Build them so the shipped-route check below reads what ships.
      - name: Build the sidecar handler bundles
        run: |
          node scripts/build-sidecar-sebuf.mjs
          node scripts/build-sidecar-handlers.mjs

      - name: Test sidecar with the shipped Node.js runtime
        run: |
          export PATH="$PWD/src-tauri/sidecar/node:$PATH"
          node --version
          npm run test:sidecar
          # Every route the app ships must load from the shipped files alone
          # on this runtime (#9906).
          node scripts/check-sidecar-shipped-routes.mjs

  # Desktop drift gates (#5902): path-conditional so unrelated PRs skip them
  # (deploy-gate counts "skipped" as passing). desktop-config is the cheap
  # install-free surface — version consistency, release packaging script
  # syntax, and Tauri config/capability parse (the sidecar bundle build lives
  # in `unit`, whose `code` filter tracks the bundle's real src/server/api
  # import graph).
  # desktop-rust compiles and unit-tests the Tauri crate, which was
  # previously untested until a release build.
  desktop-config:
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.desktop_config == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
      - name: Desktop version consistency
        run: |
          node scripts/sync-desktop-version.mjs --check || {
            echo '::error::Desktop versions out of sync — run `npm run version:sync` and commit the result.'
            exit 1
          }
      - name: Linux AppImage build scripts parse
        run: |
          bash -n scripts/repack-linux-appimage.sh
          bash -n scripts/prefetch-appimage-tools.sh
          bash -n scripts/fetch-with-retry.sh
      - name: Desktop build env parity (#5905)
        # A VITE_ key missing from the Tauri build steps silently disables the
        # capability in every shipped build (sign-in, Pro, Cyber Threats were
        # all dark this way). Also runs in `unit`: this leg is the one that
        # fires for src-tauri/ Rust and capability edits, which the `code`
        # filter skips (it carves back only `tauri*.conf.json`), while the unit
        # leg covers new import.meta.env.VITE_ reads added under src/.
        run: node scripts/check-desktop-build-env.mjs
      - name: Tauri config and capability files parse
        # One desktop binary ships (#5908), so there is exactly one tauri conf —
        # the per-variant `tauri.tech/finance.conf.json` files were retired with
        # the build legs that never published them. The floor still guards the
        # vacuous-pass case where a broken glob finds nothing to validate.
        run: |
          node -e '
            const { readFileSync, readdirSync } = require("node:fs");
            const confs = readdirSync("src-tauri").filter((f) => /^tauri.*\.conf\.json$/.test(f));
            const capabilities = readdirSync("src-tauri/capabilities");
            const files = [
              ...confs.map((f) => `src-tauri/${f}`),
              ...capabilities.map((f) => `src-tauri/capabilities/${f}`),
            ];
            if (confs.length !== 1 || capabilities.length < 3) {
              console.error(`::error::expected exactly 1 tauri conf file (one published binary, #5908) and at least 3 capability files, found ${confs.length} conf + ${capabilities.length} capabilities: ${files.join(", ")}`);
              process.exit(1);
            }
            let failed = false;
            for (const f of files) {
              try {
                JSON.parse(readFileSync(f, "utf8"));
                console.log(`ok ${f}`);
              } catch (e) {
                console.error(`::error file=${f}::invalid JSON in ${f}: ${e.message}`);
                failed = true;
              }
