repository.readme:
# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description ``` Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.
## Project files and git Impeccable writes its working files under `.impeccable/`. A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: `config.json`, `live/config.json`, `design.json`, `surfaces/*.md`, and `critique/*.md`. Keep `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.
Copy the .gitignore entries ```gitignore # impeccable-ignore-start # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides. # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace. # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json, # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md. **/.impeccable/config.local.json **/.impeccable/hook.cache.json **/.impeccable/hook.pending.json **/.impeccable/*.png **/.impeccable/review/ **/.impeccable/questions/ **/.impeccable/live/server.json **/.impeccable/live/sessions/ **/.impeccable/live/previews/ **/.impeccable/live/annotations/ **/.impeccable/live/cache/ **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/ **/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json **/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json **/.impeccable/live/*.png # impeccable-ignore-end ```
The folders that hold decision-round state (`.impeccable/questions/`, `.impeccable/mocks/worlds/`) also ignore themselves. A `.gitignore` can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run `git rm --cached `. ## Good to know **Build path.** For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. `init` asks once and saves the answer as `buildPath` in `.impeccable/config.json`; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. [Image generation](https://impeccable.style/docs/image-generation) · [Configuration](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **Native apps.** Set `## Platform` in `PRODUCT.md` to `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive` (one Flutter or React Native codebase that follows each OS), and the design commands work from Apple's HIG or Material 3 instead of web conventions. `init` asks when it can't tell. `audit` and `adapt` switch to native versions, and the native audit reads SwiftUI, Compose, React Native, or Flutter source directly. The detector, live mode with its `generate` shortcut, and the edit hook stay web-only, because they work on HTML and CSS in a browser. **Hooks run outside model approval.** In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone. **Something broken?** `/impeccable doctor` finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. [Fix setup problems](https://impeccable.style/docs/doctor). **Telemetry.** When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and `PRODUCT.md` are never sent. Disable telemetry with `npx impeccable telemetry off`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or `"telemetry": false` in `.impeccable/config.json` for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the [privacy page](https://impeccable.style/privacy). ## Community - [Issues](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/issues) for bugs, questions, and ideas. Outside contributions start with an issue; see [DEVELOP.md](docs/DEVELOP.md). - [Changelog](https://impeccable.style/changelog) for what shipped. - Follow [@pbakaus](https://x.com/pbakaus) for release notes and new rules. ## Sponsors [![CI powered by Namespace](https://namespace.so/oss/badge.svg)](https://namespace.so/github-actions/?utm_source=oss&utm_campaign=impeccable) Thanks to [Namespace](https://namespace.so) for sponsoring Impeccable's CI with fast Linux and Windows runners. ## License Apache 2.0. sampled_files..github/workflows/ci.yml:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      skill_workflow:
        description: 'Run billed, browser-backed Claude workflow completion tests'
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Nightly full live-e2e matrix. The smoke groups already gate every PR; the
  # full sweep is too slow for that, so it runs once a day against main.
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 7 * * *'

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # Scheduled runs get their own group: the 07:00 UTC nightly and a push to
  # main share github.ref, and cancel-in-progress would let them kill each
  # other mid-run.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'nightly' || github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Any request a job makes to the roll API is tagged as test traffic
# (X-Impeccable-Client carries the channel), so CI never lands in the
# choice dataset.
env:
  IMPECCABLE_TELEMETRY_CHANNEL: test

jobs:
  changes:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.core }}
      rust: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.rust }}
      detector: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.detector }}
      live: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.live }}
      framework: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.framework }}
      cli_remote_e2e: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.cli_remote_e2e }}
      live_e2e: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.live_e2e }}
      new_work_e2e: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.new_work_e2e }}
      live_e2e_accept_cleanup: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.live_e2e_accept_cleanup }}
      skill_behavior: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.skill_behavior }}
      live_svelte_adapter_deepseek: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.live_svelte_adapter_deepseek }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Detect test plan
        id: plan
        env:
          GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE: ${{ github.event.before }}
        run: node scripts/ci-test-plan.mjs

  test-matrix:
    name: test (Node ${{ matrix.node-version }})
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: changes
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        # The workspace's floor (package.json devEngines); the published shim's is held by cli-shim-floor (#850).
        node-version: [22.18.0, 24]
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bun

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install

      - name: Run core tests
        run: bun run test:core

      - name: Install Puppeteer browser
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        run: bunx puppeteer browsers install chrome

      - name: Run detector tests
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        run: bun run test:detector

      - name: Run live unit tests
        if: needs.changes.outputs.live == 'true'
        run: bun run test:live

      - name: Run framework fixture tests
        if: needs.changes.outputs.framework == 'true'
        run: bun run test:framework

      - name: Build
        run: bun run build

      - name: Validate VS Code package
        run: bunx --package @vscode/vsce@3.9.2 vsce package --no-dependencies
        working-directory: dist/vscode

      # `bun run build:extension` runs `cargo xtask bundle`: the rule core
      # compiled to wasm plus the page JS in browser-bundle/.
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        run: rustup show && rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown

      - name: Cache Rust on the Namespace cache volume
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        with:
          cache: rust

      - name: Install wasm-pack
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        run: cargo install wasm-pack --locked

      # wasm-pack fetches wasm-bindgen and binaryen (wasm-opt) from GitHub
      # releases on first use; cached, a GitHub release outage cannot fail the build.
      - name: Cache wasm-pack tools
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/.wasm-pack

      - name: Build extension
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        run: bun run build:extension

      - name: Lint Firefox extension (web-ext)
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        # Pinned for reproducible CI. Fails on AMO errors; innerHTML style
        # warnings in the panel renderer are non-blocking and not promoted to
        # errors here.
        run: npx --yes web-ext@10 lint --source-dir dist/extension-firefox

      # Only meaningful right after the bundle was rebuilt, so it carries the
      # same condition as that step rather than running unconditionally and
      # comparing a committed artifact against an untouched tree. Every input
      # `cargo xtask bundle` reads is in the detector trigger
      # (scripts/test-suites.mjs), so a change to the registry rows or to how
      # they are serialized lands here. The in-page bundle beside it is
      # deliberately not checked: its bytes carry a wasm module built by
      # whatever wasm-pack and wasm-opt the runner installed, so diffing it
      # would fail on toolchain drift rather than on a real change.
      - name: Verify the tracked rule registry is current
        if: needs.changes.outputs.detector == 'true'
        run: git diff --exit-code -- crates/live/assets/antipatterns.json

      - name: Verify generated tracked outputs
        # What `bun run build` writes, which runs on every PR.
        # extension/detector/ is gitignored (built by `cargo xtask bundle`);
        # it stays listed so a stray tracked copy shows up here.
        run: git diff --exit-code -- .agents .claude .cursor .dsh .gemini .github/skills plugin extension/detector

      - name: Upload build artifacts
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: impeccable-build-node-${{ matrix.node-version }}
          # Ship the packaged zips, not the unpacked Firefox staging tree.
          path: |
            dist/
            !dist/extension-firefox/
          retention-days: 7

  # The Rust workspace: the engine binary, the rule core, and every crate
  # behind them. Everything builds from source with no downloads.
  rust:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # rust-toolchain.toml names the channel; `rustup show` installs it.
      # Never override the toolchain here.
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show

      - name: Cache Rust on the Namespace cache volume
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          cache: rust

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --workspace --all-targets

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --workspace

  # The engine ships a windows-x64 binary (release-engine.yml), so the
  # workspace has to build and pass its own tests there. Tests that need a
  # browser or the oracle skip when those are absent.
  rust-windows:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable-windows
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@d1527c8f67ef9af357290475d4af4b0fab8f12e0 # v2.9.3
      - run: cargo build --workspace --all-targets
      # The default TEMP is on the image's C: drive. Every browser test starts
      # Chrome on a new profile there, and with several starting at once that
      # disk queues 30 to 40 requests deep for 20 s at a stretch: profile
      # stores took up to 27 s to load and a page load of fourteen requests
      # took 14 s. The runner's own temp directory is on the work drive, where
      # the same loads stay under 3 s.
      - name: Keep temporary files on the work drive
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $temp = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'tmp'
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $temp | Out-Null
          "TEMP=$temp" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8 -Append
          "TMP=$temp" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8 -Append
      # The first Chrome start after boot reads the browser off that same C:
      # drive and has taken 25 s to open its DevTools port, against the
      # launcher's 30 s limit. Pay that once here, where no test is timing it.
      # The step has taken 4 to 38 s; a start that never returns ends after
      # three minutes and the tests run anyway.
      - name: Start the browser once before the tests
        shell: pwsh
        timeout-minutes: 3
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          $chrome = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe'
          if (Test-Path $chrome) {
            $profile = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'browser-warmup'
            & $chrome --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu "--user-data-dir=$profile" --dump-dom about:blank | Out-Null
          }
          exit 0
      - run: cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast

  launcher-windows:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable-windows
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Exercise Windows launcher downloads and verification
        run: node --test tests/launcher-download.test.mjs
      - name: Exercise Windows plugin hook commands
        run: node --test tests/hook-build-windows.test.mjs

  # The npm package ships only the shim (cli/bin/cli.js), and npm skips
  # `latest` for a Node its engines reject, serving the newest version that
  # admits it instead. So engines.node in package.json is the shim's floor, not
  # the workspace's (that one is devEngines): raising it sends everyone below
  # it to an older CLI that can no longer install (#361, #850). SHIM_FLOOR is
  # the version this job proves, and engines.node must match it.
  cli-shim-floor:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'
    env:
      SHIM_FLOOR: 18.19.0
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Check the published Node floor
        run: |
          floor=$(jq -r .engines.node package.json)
          [ "$floor" = ">=$SHIM_FLOOR" ] || { echo "::error::package.json engines.node is $floor, but the shim is proven on >=$SHIM_FLOOR. Raise SHIM_FLOOR only when the shim itself needs a newer Node."; exit 1; }
      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.SHIM_FLOOR }}
      - name: Exercise the npm shim on its Node floor
        run: node --test tests/cli-shim.test.mjs

  # Behavior gate: replays the tests/oracle/ goldens against a release build
  # of the engine from THIS checkout (so a PR is judged on its own source,
  # not on the last published binary). Without this job the oracle only ever
  # runs on developer laptops: tests/oracle.test.mjs skips cleanly when no
  # binary is present, so the default suite is silent about it on CI.
  oracle:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.oracle == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.rust == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.new_work_e2e == 'true'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bun

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install

      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show

      - name: Cache Rust on the Namespace cache volume
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          cache: rust

      - name: Build the engine from source
        run: cargo build --release -p impeccable

      - name: Replay oracle goldens
        env:
          IMPECCABLE_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/target/release/impeccable
        run: node tests/oracle/run.mjs

      - name: Install review test browser
        run: bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium

      - name: Verify review workflows and system themes
        env:
          IMPECCABLE_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/target/release/impeccable
        run: node --test --test-timeout=180000 tests/new-work-e2e.test.mjs tests/review-theme.test.mjs

  # Release-order guard (triage decision D4). Verifies that the engine release for
  # the pinned ENGINE_VERSION is fully published — the five dist binaries + .sha256
  # AND the five @impeccable/cli-<os>-<arch> npm platform packages — before a skill
  # release/merge that depends on them. The launcher, npm shim, and
  # `impeccable install` all dead-end without those assets.
  #
  # A hard gate since engine-v0.1.0 shipped: the assets for the pinned
  # ENGINE_VERSION must exist before a skill/CLI release or a merge that bumps the
  # pin, or the launcher, the npm shim and `impeccable install` dead-end.
  # release.mjs hard-fails `release:skill`/`release:cli` on the same check.
  engine-release-ready:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Check engine release assets for pinned ENGINE_VERSION
        id: check
        run: node scripts/check-engine-release.mjs

      - name: Annotate missing engine release
        # Only when the check itself failed, so a checkout or setup failure keeps its own error.
        if: failure() && steps.check.outcome == 'failure'
        run: |
          echo "::error title=Engine release not ready::The engine release for v$(cat ENGINE_VERSION) is not fully published (engine-v$(cat ENGINE_VERSION) release assets and/or the @impeccable/cli-<os>-<arch> npm platform packages). Publish the engine (bun run release:engine) and the platform packages (bun run release:platform-packages) before bumping ENGINE_VERSION on main or releasing the skill/CLI. If only engine-checksums.txt is named, run node scripts/check-engine-release.mjs --record and commit it."

  test:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: test-matrix
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify Node test matrix
        run: |
          if [ "${{ needs.test-matrix.result }}" != "success" ]; then
            echo "test-matrix result: ${{ needs.test-matrix.result }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "test matrix passed"

  cli-remote-e2e:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.cli_remote_e2e == 'true'
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bun

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install

      # The live verbs are the engine binary; build it from this checkout so the
      # suite tests the branch, not the last published release.
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show

      - name: Cache Rust on the Namespace cache volume
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          cache: rust

      - name: Build the engine
        run: cargo build --release -p impeccable

      - name: Run remote CLI E2E smoke
        run: bun run test:cli-remote-e2e

  live-e2e-smoke:
    name: live-e2e smoke (${{ matrix.group }})
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.live_e2e == 'true' && github.event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event_name != 'schedule'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        include:
          - group: platform
            fixtures: astro-vite7,monorepo-nested-vite,nextjs-app-router,vite7-vue,vite8-sveltekit
          - group: svelte
            fixtures: vite8-sveltekit-stateful
          - group: react
            fixtures: vite8-react-css-modules,vite8-react-insert,vite8-react-plain,vite8-react-pricing-cards
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bun

      - name: Cache fixture npm downloads
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          path: ~/.npm

      - name: Cache Playwright Chromium
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium
        run: npx playwright install chromium

      # The live verbs are the engine binary; build it from this checkout so the
      # suite tests the branch, not the last published release.
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show

      - name: Cache Rust on the Namespace cache volume
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          cache: rust

      - name: Build the engine
        run: cargo build --release -p impeccable

      - name: Run live E2E tests
        run: bun run test:live-e2e
        env:
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_ONLY: ${{ matrix.fixtures }}
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_SCENARIOS: core,agent-target
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS: 180000
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS: 120000
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_DEV_READY_TIMEOUT_MS: 60000
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR: test-results/live-e2e/${{ matrix.group }}

      - name: Upload live E2E failure artifacts
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: live-e2e-smoke-${{ matrix.group }}-artifacts
          path: test-results/live-e2e
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  live-e2e-full:
    name: live-e2e full (${{ matrix.group }})
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.live_e2e == 'true' && (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    timeout-minutes: 25
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        include:
          - group: platform
            fixtures: astro-vite7,monorepo-nested-vite,nextjs-app-router,nuxt-vite7,vite7-vue
          - group: svelte
            fixtures: vite8-sveltekit,vite8-sveltekit-stateful
          - group: react-a
            fixtures: vite8-https,vite8-react-base-path,vite8-react-csp-meta,vite8-react-css-modules,vite8-react-emotion
          - group: react-b
            fixtures: vite8-react-insert,vite8-react-mapped-list,vite8-react-modal,vite8-react-plain,vite8-react-pricing-cards
          - group: stateful
            fixtures: vite8-react-radix-dialog,vite8-react-router-spa,vite8-react-styled-components,vite8-react-tabs
          - group: styling
            fixtures: vite8-react-tailwindv3,vite8-react-tailwindv4,vite8-react-ts,vite8-react-tsx-repeated-aside,vite8-react-unocss,vite8-react-vanilla-extract
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bun

      - name: Cache fixture npm downloads
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          path: ~/.npm

      - name: Cache Playwright Chromium
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium
        run: npx playwright install chromium

      # The live verbs are the engine binary; build it from this checkout so the
      # suite tests the branch, not the last published release.
      - name: Install the pinned toolchain
        run: rustup show

      - name: Cache Rust on the Namespace cache volume
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          cache: rust

      - name: Build the engine
        run: cargo build --release -p impeccable

      - name: Run live E2E tests
        run: bun run test:live-e2e
        env:
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_ONLY: ${{ matrix.fixtures }}
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_TEST_TIMEOUT_MS: 300000
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS: 180000
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_DEV_READY_TIMEOUT_MS: 120000
          IMPECCABLE_E2E_ARTIFACT_DIR: test-results/live-e2e/${{ matrix.group }}

      - name: Upload live E2E failure artifacts
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: live-e2e-full-${{ matrix.group }}-artifacts
          path: test-results/live-e2e
          if-no-files-found: ignore

  live-e2e-accept-cleanup:
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    needs: changes
    if: needs.changes.outputs.live_e2e_accept_cleanup == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - name: Skip without provider key
        if: ${{ env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY == '' && env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY == '' }}
        run: echo "Skipping provider-backed accept-cleanup regression because no provider API key is configured."

      - name: Checkout repository
        if: ${{ env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY != '' || env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY != '' }}
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Node
        if: ${{ env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY != '' || env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY != '' }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:

      - name: Setup Bun

        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          path: ~/.npm

      - name: Cache Playwright Chromium
        if: ${{ env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY != '' || env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY != '' }}
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/ms-playwright

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: ${{ env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY != '' || env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY != '' }}
        run: bun install

      - name: Install Playwright Chromium
        if: ${{ env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY != '' || env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY != '' }}
        run: npx playwright install chromium

      # The live verbs are the engine binary; build it from this checkout so the

        run: rustup show

      - name: Cache Rust on the Namespace cache volume
        uses: namespacelabs/nscloud-cache-action@1124a6f3ce44e5cf84cc22111530961f4d2a15f9 # v1.7.0

    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable

    timeout-minutes: 25

        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bun

        run: bun install

        run: bun run fetch:engine

        run: bun run test:skill-behavior

    # Expensive, manually opted-in completion diagnostics. This does not
    # replace the multi-family skill-behavior protocol suite above.
    runs-on: namespace-profile-impeccable
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.skill_workflow
    timeout-minutes: 70
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Setup Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-bun
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Prepare engine and browser before billing
        run: |
          test -n "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" || { echo 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is required'; exit 1; }
          bun run fetch:engine
          bunx playwright install --with-deps chromium
      - name: Run completed skill workflows
        env:
          IMPECCABLE_SKILL_BEHAVIOR_TRACE_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/skill-workflow-traces

        with:
          name: skill-workflow-traces
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/skill-workflow-traces
          retention-days: 7

# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. Apply sends staged copy edits to your chat agent while a live session is polling. If none has polled in the last minute, it runs the `codex` CLI from your PATH instead (or `claude` when codex is missing), with approvals, permission checks, and sandboxing off (`--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` or `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`) and your environment inherited. Its prompt carries the staged edits, the edited elements' HTML and nearby text, the page URL, and candidate source paths. Set `IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat` in the environment that starts live mode to keep Apply in your chat session, or `off` to disable Apply. The server reads it once at startup. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description ``` Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.
## Project files and git Impeccable writes its working files under `.impeccable/`. A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: `config.json`, `live/config.json`, `design.json`, `surfaces/*.md`, and `critique/*.md`. Keep `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.
Copy the .gitignore entries ```gitignore # impeccable-ignore-start # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides. # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace. # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json, # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md. **/.impeccable/config.local.json **/.impeccable/hook.cache.json **/.impeccable/hook.pending.json **/.impeccable/*.png **/.impeccable/review/ **/.impeccable/questions/ **/.impeccable/live/server.json **/.impeccable/live/sessions/ **/.impeccable/live/previews/ **/.impeccable/live/annotations/ **/.impeccable/live/cache/ **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/ **/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json **/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json **/.impeccable/live/*.png # impeccable-ignore-end ```
The folders that hold decision-round state (`.impeccable/questions/`, `.impeccable/mocks/worlds/`) also ignore themselves. A `.gitignore` can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run `git rm --cached `. ## Good to know **Build path.** For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. `init` asks once and saves the answer as `buildPath` in `.impeccable/config.json`; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. [Image generation](https://impeccable.style/docs/image-generation) · [Configuration](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **Native apps.** Set `## Platform` in `PRODUCT.md` to `ios`, `android`, or `adaptive` (one Flutter or React Native codebase that follows each OS), and the design commands work from Apple's HIG or Material 3 instead of web conventions. `init` asks when it can't tell. `audit` and `adapt` switch to native versions, and the native audit reads SwiftUI, Compose, React Native, or Flutter source directly. The detector, live mode with its `generate` shortcut, and the edit hook stay web-only, because they work on HTML and CSS in a browser. **Hooks run outside model approval.** In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone. **Something broken?** `/impeccable doctor` finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. [Fix setup problems](https://impeccable.style/docs/doctor). **Telemetry.** When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and `PRODUCT.md` are never sent. Disable telemetry with `npx impeccable telemetry off`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or `"telemetry": false` in `.impeccable/config.json` for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the [privacy page](https://impeccable.style/privacy). ## Community - [Issues](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/issues) for bugs, questions, and ideas. Outside contributions start with an issue; see [DEVELOP.md](docs/DEVELOP.md). - [Changelog](https://impeccable.style/changelog) for what shipped. - Follow [@pbakaus](https://x.com/pbakaus) for release notes and new rules. ## Sponsors [![CI powered by Namespace](https://namespace.so/oss/badge.svg)](https://namespace.so/github-actions/?utm_source=oss&utm_campaign=impeccable) Thanks to [Namespace](https://namespace.so) for sponsoring Impeccable's CI with fast Linux and Windows runners. ## License Apache 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Impeccable started from Anthropic's [frontend-design](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/frontend-design) skill. --- Created by [Paul Bakaus](https://www.paulbakaus.com)

# Awesome MCP servers

Best MCP servers for Cursor, Claude, and VS Code
Ranked from PlugMCP · official and remote called out · skills included

Directory · Skills · Submit · Contribute

Ranked MCP servers you can install in Cursor, Claude, and VS Code, checked against the PlugMCP directory. This repo keeps the usable shelf (~250 servers in markdown, 900 in the machine catalog, 400 skills). Search the full index at [plugmcp.ai/mcp](https://plugmcp.ai/mcp). Updated 2026-11-14. Submit on PlugMCP first, then open a catalog PR — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Start here Servers people actually search for. [![LinkedIn](https://img.shields.io/badge/LINKEDIN-connect-0B1220?style=for-the-badge&logo=linkedin&logoColor=white&labelColor=0A66C2&color=0B1220)](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rudymizrahi/) [![Gradia](https://img.shields.io/badge/GRADIA-AI_research_%26_implementation_lab-0B1220?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=13B8A6&color=0B1220)](https://www.gradiahq.com) [![ORCID](https://img.shields.io/badge/ORCID-research_record-0B1220?style=for-the-badge&logo=orcid&logoColor=white&labelColor=A6CE39&color=0B1220)](https://orcid.org/0009-0000-7043-3766) [![Follow](https://img.shields.io/github/followers/rudycelekli?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&label=FOLLOW&labelColor=7C3AED&color=0B1220)](https://github.com/rudycelekli?tab=followers)

**Charlotte-based Forward Deployed AI Researcher · Agentic AI Engineer** Building verifiable, long-horizon agent systems · Research, implementation, and open source [Gradia](https://www.gradiahq.com) · [Snorkel AI](https://snorkel.ai/) · [AxiomConsulting.ai](https://axiomconsulting.ai/) · [Agentics Foundation](https://agentics.org/leadership/)
## I build AI systems that can prove what happened. **On a mission to make open source reliable enough to trust. One repository at a time.** I am **Rudy Mizrahi Celekli**, also known professionally as **Rudy Celekli**. I research and build long-horizon agent systems, evaluation environments, and evidence-bound execution, with a focus on evaluator robustness, deterministic replay, and causal fault isolation. The work has two connected fronts: building AI systems whose behavior can be inspected, and strengthening the open-source foundations those systems rely on. Open source is shared infrastructure. A silent data error, a misleading evaluation, or an agent that fails without a useful trace can become someone else's production problem. I work on those failure points: reproduce the problem, fix the cause, add a regression test, and get the change accepted upstream. Reliability and correctness are foundations of trust and safety. An accepted fix improves a shared dependency. A regression test helps maintainers keep that failure from returning. My goal is fewer inherited failures and software people can depend on. Research, owned products, upstream contributions, and measured results remain explicitly separate. ## Operating principles ```text Direct goals, constraints, acceptance criteria, escalation Orchestrate models, agents, tools, memory, and bounded loops Verify receipts, replay, tests, independent challenge Improve measured failure becomes a better next run ``` - **Can we trust the record?** Proof-bound execution evidence. - **Can we trust the score?** Adversarial evaluator stress testing. - **Can we reproduce the result?** Deterministic replay and committed artifacts. - **Can an agent remember?** Regression memory before another change reaches history. The standard is not that an AI system sounds convincing. ## I build AI systems that can prove what happened. **On a mission to make open source reliable enough to trust. One repository at a time.** I am **Rudy Mizrahi Celekli**, also known professionally as **Rudy Celekli**. I research and build long-horizon agent systems, evaluation environments, and evidence-bound execution, with a focus on evaluator robustness, deterministic replay, and causal fault isolation. The work has two connected fronts: building AI systems whose behavior can be inspected, and strengthening the open-source foundations those systems rely on. Open source is shared infrastructure. A silent data error, a misleading evaluation, or an agent that fails without a useful trace can become someone else's production problem. I work on those failure points: reproduce the problem, fix the cause, add a regression test, and get the change accepted upstream. Reliability and correctness are foundations of trust and safety. An accepted fix improves a shared dependency. A regression test helps maintainers keep that failure from returning. My goal is fewer inherited failures and software people can depend on. Research, owned products, upstream contributions, and measured results remain explicitly separate.
